questionEn: Which Arabic term in Surah Aal-Imran (3:96) refers to Makkah as the site of the first House of worship established for humanity?
optionsEn: Bakkah
Yathrib
Al-Juhfah
Al-Abwa
explanationEn: Surah Aal-Imran (3:96) states that the first House appointed for mankind was the one at Bakkah, an ancient name for Makkah associated with crowding or humbling the arrogant.

questionEn: What heavenly structure sits directly above the Kaaba in the seventh heaven, where seventy thousand angels enter daily never to return?
optionsEn: Sidrat al-Muntaha
Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur
Al-Kawthar
Al-A'raf
explanationEn: During Al-Isra wal-Mi'raj, the Prophet ﷺ was shown Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur in the seventh heaven, aligned above the earthly Kaaba, visited daily by seventy thousand angels.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Book of Beginning of Creation)

questionEn: Toward which directions do the four corners (Arkan) of the Holy Kaaba approximately point?
optionsEn: Directly toward Madinah and Jerusalem only
Northeast, Northwest, Southeast, and Southwest
East, North, West, and South
Randomly aligned with Mount Safa
explanationEn: The four corners of the Kaaba are roughly oriented toward the four cardinal directions: Al-Hajar al-Aswad (East), Al-Rukn al-Iraqi (North), Al-Rukn al-Shami (West), and Al-Rukn al-Yamani (South).

questionEn: Which corner of the Kaaba is called Al-Rukn al-Shami?
optionsEn: The corner adjacent to Maqam Ibrahim
The corner directly beneath the Kaaba door
The southern corner touched during Tawaf
The western corner adjacent to the western side of Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Al-Rukn al-Shami is the western corner of the Kaaba overlooking the western end of Hijr Ismail, named because it faces toward Al-Sham (the Levant).

questionEn: Why are the Iraqi and Shami corners NOT touched (istilam) by pilgrims during Tawaf, unlike the Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani?
optionsEn: Because they do not rest on the original foundations of Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
Because they are too high to reach
Because they face away from the Safa hill
Because they were added during the Ottoman era
explanationEn: When Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba, they shortened its northern side, leaving Hijr Ismail outside; thus only the Black Stone corner and Rukn al-Yamani rest on Ibrahim's original foundations.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari & Sahih Muslim (Book of Hajj)

questionEn: Who famously declared while kissing the Black Stone, 'I know you are only a stone that can neither harm nor benefit; had I not seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kiss you, I would not kiss you'?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)
Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
Uthman ibn Affan (RA)
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA)
explanationEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) spoke these words publicly to clarify Tawhid—that honoring the Black Stone is pure obedience to the Sunnah, not worship of a stone.

questionEn: How many distinct visible fragments of the original Black Stone are currently embedded inside the silver frame on the eastern corner?
optionsEn: 3 fragments
24 fragments
8 small fragments
1 single intact boulder
explanationEn: Due to historical fires and the 4th-century AH Qarmatian attack, eight small fragments of varying sizes remain visible, set in dark mastic within the silver bezel.

questionEn: At approximately what height above the Mataf ground is Al-Hajar al-Aswad set into the Kaaba's eastern corner?
optionsEn: 0.3 meters
5.5 meters
3.0 meters
1.1 to 1.5 meters
explanationEn: The Black Stone is positioned roughly 1.1 to 1.5 meters above the Mataf floor so that an average adult can conveniently reach or kiss it when uncrowded.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah action for a pilgrim passing Al-Hajar al-Aswad during Tawaf when crowds prevent kissing or touching it directly?
optionsEn: Point toward it with the right hand and say 'Allahu Akbar'
Throw a pebble toward the stone
Stop Tawaf until the crowd clears
Bow down toward the ground
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ gestured toward the Black Stone with his staff or hand from a distance and said 'Allahu Akbar' when unable to kiss it directly without harming others.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say the Black Stone will testify to on the Day of Resurrection?
optionsEn: Only the names of Makkah's governors
It will be given eyes and a tongue to testify in truth for everyone who touched or kissed it sincerely
It will measure the wealth of pilgrims
It will remain silent until the end of reckoning
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah will raise the Black Stone on the Day of Judgment with two eyes to see and a tongue to speak, testifying truthfully for those who touched it in faith.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic supplication is Sunnah to recite specifically between Rukn al-Yamani and Al-Hajar al-Aswad during every circuit of Tawaf?
optionsEn: Rabbana la tuzigh qulubana ba'da idh hadaytana
Rabbi ishrah li sadri wa yassir li amri
Rabbana atina fi'd-dunya hasanatan wa fi'l-akhirati hasanatan wa qina adhaban-nar
HasbunAllahu wa ni'mal-wakil
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn al-Sa'ib (RA) reported hearing the Prophet ﷺ recite 'Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire' between these two corners.

questionEn: Which part of the Kaaba wall is known as Al-Multazam?
optionsEn: The corner between Rukn al-Shami and Rukn al-Iraqi
The wall inside Hijr Ismail facing Syria
The roof edge beneath the golden spout
The space between Al-Hajar al-Aswad and the Door of the Kaaba
explanationEn: Al-Multazam is the approximately two-meter section of the Kaaba wall between the Black Stone and the Kaaba's door, where companions like Ibn Abbas (RA) pressed their chests and palms to make dua.

questionEn: What is the area on the rear (southwestern) wall of the Kaaba opposite the front door—where Ibn al-Zubayr's sealed rear door once stood—traditionally called?
optionsEn: Al-Mustajar
Al-Mas'a
Al-Miqat
Al-Safah
explanationEn: Al-Mustajar refers to the section on the back wall of the Kaaba opposite the front door, where the sealed rear door of Ibn al-Zubayr once opened.

questionEn: Approximately how high above the ground is the threshold of the Door of the Kaaba (Bab al-Ka'bah) today?
optionsEn: Flush with the floor
About 2.25 meters above the Mataf
About 6 meters above the Mataf
10 meters above the Mataf
explanationEn: Quraysh intentionally raised the Kaaba door roughly two meters above ground level to control who entered; today a portable wheeled staircase is brought up when the door is opened.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari (Book of Hajj) & Haram Architecture

questionEn: Who ordered the crafting of the current solid-gold-plated Door of the Kaaba installed in 1399 AH (1979 CE)?
optionsEn: Sultan Murad IV
Caliph al-Mahdi
King Khalid ibn Abdulaziz
Salahuddin al-Ayyubi
explanationEn: King Khalid ibn Abdulaziz commissioned the present double-leaf Kaaba door crafted by master goldsmith Ahmad ibn Ibrahim Badr using roughly 280 kg of pure gold over teakwood.
reference: History of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What is the sloped marble border around the bottom of three walls of the Kaaba—including the recessed threshold beneath the door—called?
optionsEn: Al-Mizab
Al-Atabah
Al-Hatim
Al-Shadhirwan
explanationEn: The sloped marble plinth along the base of the Kaaba (including beneath the door, where it forms a recessed step) is Al-Shadhirwan, marking the thicker lower foundation.

questionEn: When Aishah (RA) longed to enter inside the Kaaba to pray, what did the Prophet ﷺ instruct her to do?
optionsEn: Pray inside Al-Hijr (Hijr Ismail), as it is part of the House
Climb onto the roof
Wait until the next Ramadan
Pray behind Mount Safa
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ took Aishah (RA) by the hand into Al-Hijr and said, 'Pray here if you wish to enter the House, for it is indeed a piece of the House.'

questionEn: Why is the curved wall of Hijr Ismail also called 'Al-Hatim'?
optionsEn: Because it was built by Prophet Hud (AS)
Because it denotes the portion 'broken off' or excluded from the main cube by Quraysh
Because it was made from red granite
Because only scholars could approach it
explanationEn: Linguistically, Al-Hatim derives from 'hatama' (to break or cut off), referring to the broken-off remnant of the original Kaaba wall left unroofed.

questionEn: Is it permissible for a Muslim to perform supererogatory (nafl) prayer inside Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: No, prayer is forbidden there
Only during Maghrib
Yes, praying nafl inside Hijr Ismail carries the virtue of praying inside the Kaaba
Only on Mondays and Thursdays
explanationEn: Praying voluntary prayers inside Hijr Ismail is virtuous because part of it is the Kaaba; scholars advise keeping prayers brief so others may also enter safely.

questionEn: What is the primary architectural function of Al-Shadhirwan around the Kaaba's lower perimeter?
optionsEn: To seat guards around the walls
To mark the start of Sa'i
To channel Zamzam water outside
To protect the lower foundation walls from rainwater erosion and anchor the Kiswah rings
explanationEn: Al-Shadhirwan is the slanted marble buttress built at the base of the Kaaba (excluding the Hijr Ismail side) to protect its lower masonry from rainwater and anchor the Kiswah rings.

questionEn: Why do scholars advise pilgrims NOT to walk or climb onto Al-Shadhirwan during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Because it rests on the Kaaba's own foundation, so stepping onto it means failing to go completely around the House
Because it is solid gold
Because it faces away from Makkah
Because only Imams may step on it
explanationEn: Scholars note that Al-Shadhirwan is part of the thickness of Ibrahim's original Kaaba base; walking upon it during Tawaf compromises that portion of the circuit.

questionEn: What is the name of the enclosed interior staircase inside the Kaaba that leads up to its roof?
optionsEn: Bab al-Fath
Bab al-Tawbah
Bab al-Safar
Bab al-Umrah
explanationEn: Inside the Kaaba on the right corner stands Bab al-Tawbah (Door of Repentance), a small gilded wooden door enclosing the staircase leading to the roof.

questionEn: According to Ibn Umar (RA), what did Bilal (RA) report that the Prophet ﷺ did after entering the Kaaba on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: He remained seated without praying
He prayed facing the Black Stone from outside only
He prayed two rak'ahs between the front two pillars facing the opposite wall
He stayed inside for three days
explanationEn: Bilal (RA) informed Ibn Umar (RA) that the Prophet ﷺ entered with Usamah ibn Zayd and Uthman ibn Talhah, closed the door, and prayed two rak'ahs between the forward pillars facing the rear wall.

questionEn: What is the actual physical artifact preserved inside the glass-and-brass shrine known as Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: A staff of Prophet Musa (AS)
A silver vessel from Zamzam
The first handwritten Mushaf
The stone upon which Prophet Ibrahim (AS) stood while building the upper walls of the Kaaba
explanationEn: Maqam Ibrahim contains the miraculous stone that preserved the impressions of Prophet Ibrahim's (AS) footprints as he raised the Kaaba walls.

questionEn: Which Surah and verse explicitly command believers to take Maqam Ibrahim as a place of prayer?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125
Surah Al-Fatihah 1:5
Surah Al-Kahf 18:10
Surah Al-Mulk 67:1
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:125) commands: 'And take, [O believers], from the standing place of Ibrahim a place of prayer (musalla).'

questionEn: Who moved Maqam Ibrahim slightly further back from the wall of the Kaaba to its present distance so it would not obstruct crowds performing Tawaf?
optionsEn: Abdul-Muttalib
Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA)
Harun al-Rashid
Sultan Suleiman
explanationEn: When floods displaced the stone and crowds grew dense around the Kaaba wall, Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) positioned Maqam Ibrahim further back along the same alignment to ease Tawaf.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ recite in the two Sunnah rak'ahs prayed behind Maqam Ibrahim after Tawaf?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Falaq in both rak'ahs
Surah Yasin and Surah Al-Waqiah
Surah Al-Kafirun in the first rak'ah and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the second
Surah Al-Fil and Surah Quraysh
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) reported in his detailed account of the Prophet's ﷺ Hajj that he recited Qul ya ayyuhal-kafirun and Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad in those two rak'ahs.

questionEn: Roughly how far from the eastern wall of the Kaaba does Maqam Ibrahim stand?
optionsEn: 1 meter
100 meters
50 meters
About 10 to 11 meters
explanationEn: Maqam Ibrahim is situated roughly 10 to 11 meters east of the Kaaba's door wall inside the Mataf courtyard.

questionEn: What is the approximate height of the Kaaba building from the Mataf floor to its roof parapet?
optionsEn: 13 to 14 meters
5 meters
30 meters
45 meters
explanationEn: The Kaaba stands approximately 13.1 to 14 meters tall, constructed of bluish-gray Makkan granite.

questionEn: What kind of stone forms the structural masonry walls of the Holy Kaaba beneath the Kiswah?
optionsEn: White Carrara marble
Dark bluish-gray Makkan granite from nearby hills
Baked mud brick
Imported sandstone from Jerusalem
explanationEn: The Kaaba is built from dense, locally quarried gray-blue Makkan granite bonded with traditional mortar, later stabilized during modern restorations.

questionEn: Which wall of the Kaaba is the shortest horizontally, due to Quraysh's exclusion of Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: The northeastern Door wall
The southeastern wall (~12.8m)
The northwestern wall overlooking Hijr Ismail (~10.1m)
All four walls are identical to the millimeter
explanationEn: The northwestern face overlooking Hijr Ismail is roughly 10.1 meters wide, whereas the southeastern wall opposite it extends roughly 12.8 meters.

questionEn: What does the word 'Ka'bah' signify in classical Arabic?
optionsEn: A deep valley
A desert spring
A black curtain
A high, square-built structure or prominent elevated edifice
explanationEn: Classical lexicographers explain that Al-Ka'bah refers to an elevated, square-walled building rising prominently above its surroundings.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:97), Allah refers to the Kaaba as 'Al-Bayt al-Haram'—what role does He say He gave it for mankind?
optionsEn: A means of standing/support and stability (qiyaman) for the people
A commercial hub only
A seasonal market for poetry
A fortress for kings
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:97) states: 'Allah has made the Kaaba, the Sacred House, a standing support (qiyaman) for the people,' preserving their spiritual and worldly order.

questionEn: What is the outer black silk covering of the Holy Kaaba called?
optionsEn: Al-Sidanah
Al-Kiswah
Al-Rifadah
Al-Mihrab
explanationEn: Al-Kiswah literally means 'the garment' or 'covering' and refers to the sacred black silk drapery adorned with gold-embroidered Qur'anic verses that clothes the Kaaba.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What is the richly embroidered curtain that hangs specifically over the Door of the Kaaba called?
optionsEn: Al-Qiblah
Al-Hatim
Al-Burqu' (or Al-Sitara)
Al-Maqam
explanationEn: The ornate curtain covering Bab al-Ka'bah is called Al-Sitara or Al-Burqu', featuring intricate gold and silver embroidery of Surah Al-Fatihah, Ayat al-Kursi, and verses on Hajj.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What woven phrases subtly repeat across the black silk jacquard background of the Kiswah?
optionsEn: Names of Makkah's tribes
Poetry of pre-Islamic Makkah
Dates of past caliphs
Tasbih and Tahlil phrases such as 'Ya Hayyu Ya Qayyum', 'Ya Rahman Ya Rahim', and 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi'
explanationEn: The black silk fabric of the Kiswah is jacquard-woven with subtle monochrome patterns spelling invocations like 'La ilaha illAllah Muhammadun Rasulullah', 'SubhanAllahi wa bihamdihi', and 'Ya Hannan Ya Mannan'.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Which pre-Islamic ruler of Yemen is widely recorded in early Islamic history as the first person to drape the Kaaba in a full cloth Kiswah?
optionsEn: Tubba' As'ad Abu Karib of Himyar
Abraha al-Ashram
Khusraw Parviz
Negus of Abyssinia
explanationEn: Historical reports (including Ibn Hisham and al-Azraqi) state that Tubba' As'ad of Himyar honored the Kaaba and first dressed it completely in Yemeni striped cloth (Wasail).

questionEn: Before the modern 1st of Muharram schedule, on which day of Hajj was the Kiswah traditionally replaced for decades?
optionsEn: 8th of Dhul-Hijjah (Yawm al-Tarwiyah)
9th of Dhul-Hijjah (Day of Arafah), while pilgrims were at Arafat
12th of Dhul-Hijjah
1st of Shawwal
explanationEn: Changing the Kiswah on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah took advantage of the Mataf being relatively clear while pilgrims stood in worship at Mount Arafat.

questionEn: Why is the lower ~3 meters of the black Kiswah raised and wrapped in white cotton cloth during the Hajj season?
optionsEn: To signify the end of Ramadan
To paint the granite stones underneath
To protect the silk fabric from tearing or tugging by dense Hajj crowds—popularly called 'Ihram of the Kaaba'
To allow sunlight inside the Kaaba
explanationEn: Each year in mid-Dhul-Qi'dah, attendants raise the lower hem of the Kiswah roughly three meters and wrap the base in white cloth to prevent damage during peak Tawaf crowds.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: For centuries prior to 1927, which city famously produced and dispatched the ceremonial Kiswah with the Mahmal caravan to Makkah?
optionsEn: Cordoba
Delhi
Samarkand
Cairo (Dar al-Kiswah)
explanationEn: From the Mamluk era through much of the Ottoman and early 20th-century periods, Cairo's Dar al-Kiswah crafted the Kiswah annually and sent it via the Egyptian Hajj caravan.

questionEn: Approximately how much pure natural silk is used to weave a single Kiswah for the Holy Kaaba?
optionsEn: 670 to 850 kilograms
50 kilograms
5,000 kilograms
10 kilograms
explanationEn: Hundreds of kilograms of pure raw silk dyed deep black—along with over 120 kg of gold-plated silver wire—are used for each annual Kiswah.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Which prominent Makkan family holds the hereditary honor of Sidanah—keeping the key and opening the Door of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Banu Makhzum
Banu Shaybah
Banu Adi
Banu Sahm
explanationEn: On the Day of Conquest, the Prophet ﷺ handed the key back to Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) of Banu Shaybah, saying: 'Take it, O Banu Talhah, eternally until the Day of Resurrection; none shall take it from you except an oppressor.'

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ returned the Kaaba's key to Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) rather than giving it to his uncle Al-Abbas?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:1
Surah Al-Asr 103:1
Surah An-Nisa 4:58 ('Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due')
Surah Al-Kafirun 109:6
explanationEn: When Al-Abbas (RA) asked to combine Sidanah with Siqayah, Surah An-Nisa (4:58) was revealed, prompting the Prophet ﷺ to restore the trust to Uthman ibn Talhah (RA).

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:125), what covenant did Allah take from Ibrahim (AS) and Ismail (AS) regarding the Sacred House?
optionsEn: To build towers of silver around it
To restrict entry to Quraysh alone
To close it during winter months
To purify His House for those who perform Tawaf, those who stay in devotion (I'tikaf), and those who bow and prostrate
explanationEn: Allah commanded Ibrahim and Ismail (AS): 'Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who are staying [there] for worship and those who bow and prostrate [in prayer].'

questionEn: Why did Quraysh hesitate at first when tearing down the old walls of the Kaaba during their pre-Islamic reconstruction?
optionsEn: They feared divine wrath for dismantling the Sacred House
They lacked ropes and hammers
It was snowing in Makkah
They wanted Roman engineers to arrive first
explanationEn: Quraysh remembered Allah's destruction of Abraha's army and feared punishment until Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah struck the first corner while praying, 'O Allah, we intend only good,' and nothing harmed him.

questionEn: Who led the comprehensive reconstruction of the Kaaba in 65 AH, restoring it onto the full foundations of Ibrahim (AS) including Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan
Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA)
Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz
Al-Mansur
explanationEn: After the Kaaba suffered damage during the Umayyad siege of Makkah in 64 AH, Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA)—relying on his aunt Aishah's (RA) hadith—rebuilt the Kaaba enclosing Hijr Ismail with two ground-level doors.

questionEn: Why did Caliph Harun al-Rashid refrain from rebuilding the Kaaba again after Imam Malik ibn Anas advised against it?
optionsEn: Lack of imperial funds
Because the Black Stone was missing
So the Sacred House would not become a plaything for successive rulers to demolish and rebuild
Because Hijr Ismail had collapsed
explanationEn: Imam Malik wisely cautioned Harun al-Rashid: 'I implore you, O Commander of the Faithful, do not make the House of Allah a toy for kings, lest every ruler tear it down and rebuild it to his liking.'

questionEn: Which Ottoman Sultan ordered the complete rebuilding of the Kaaba's damaged walls in 1040 AH (1630 CE) after a catastrophic flash flood collapsed its eastern and northern sides?
optionsEn: Sultan Mehmed II
Sultan Bayezid I
Sultan Abdulhamid II
Sultan Murad IV
explanationEn: When heavy rains flooded Makkah in 1039–1040 AH and collapsed two walls of the Kaaba, Sultan Murad IV commissioned master engineers from Egypt and Makkah to rebuild it—the masonry still standing today.

questionEn: Which timber salvaged from a wrecked Byzantine merchant ship at Shu'aybah port was used by Quraysh to roof the Kaaba around 605 CE?
optionsEn: Cedar/teak planks along with the skills of a Coptic carpenter named Baqum
Bamboo from India
Olive wood from Taif
Date palm trunks from Madinah
explanationEn: Allah provided timber from a Byzantine vessel wrecked near Shu'aybah (Makkah's old port) and a carpenter named Baqum, enabling Quraysh to roof the Kaaba for the first time.

questionEn: What was the height and condition of the Kaaba before Quraysh rebuilt and roofed it in 605 CE?
optionsEn: It was twice its current height
It stood only about nine cubits tall without a roof, leaving treasures stored inside exposed to theft and rain
It had a golden dome
It was submerged beneath Zamzam
explanationEn: Before Quraysh rebuilt it, the Kaaba was roughly nine cubits tall without a roof, making it vulnerable to flash floods and theft of votive offerings kept in an interior pit.

questionEn: What does the phrase 'Al-Haram' mean in reference to Makkah's sacred sanctuary?
optionsEn: A desert oasis
A marketplace open only on Fridays
An inviolable sanctuary where certain worldly acts (like hunting and cutting native trees) are forbidden out of reverence for Allah
A royal palace
explanationEn: Al-Haram derives from 'hurmah' (inviolability/sanctity), denoting a divinely consecrated territory with strict laws protecting life, vegetation, and peace.

questionEn: When Ibrahim (AS) prayed for provision in Makkah (2:126), he initially asked for 'those among them who believe in Allah and the Last Day'—how did Allah respond?
optionsEn: Provision would be given only to prophets
Fruits would grow only inside the Kaaba
Only water would be provided
Allah grants worldly provision even to those who disbelieve for a brief enjoyment, then drives them to punishment if ungrateful
explanationEn: Allah answered in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:126) that in this world He grants sustenance both to believers and disbelievers alike as a trial, while eternal reward belongs to the faithful.

questionEn: What metallic material forms the gilded calligraphic borders and lettering of the Kiswah belt?
optionsEn: Pure silver threads plated with 24-karat gold
Painted plastic thread
Polished aluminum
Copper wire
explanationEn: Artisans at the Kiswah factory pad the calligraphy in cotton cord and couch over it with pure silver wires and gold-plated silver threads for durability and brilliance.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What material lines the underside of the silk Kiswah to protect it from rubbing directly against the rough granite walls of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Lead sheeting
Sturdy white cotton lining
Raw sheep wool
Cork boards
explanationEn: A heavy white cotton backing is stitched behind the black silk panels to shield the delicate silk from friction against the stone masonry and absorb moisture.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: During early Islamic history before black silk became standard under the Abbasids, which cloth styles were commonly used to drape the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Blue and orange wool
Bright purple silk
Red/white striped Yemeni cloth (Wasail/Qabati) and white Egyptian linen
Yellow felt only
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ draped the Kaaba in striped Yemeni cloth, Umar and Uthman (RA) used fine white Egyptian Qabati linen, and the Abbasids later popularized the iconic black Kiswah.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ command when he saw pagan paintings inside the Kaaba on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: To cover them with silk
To leave them as museum relics
To move them to Safa
To wash and erase all of them completely before he stepped inside to pray
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ refused to enter the Kaaba until Umar (RA) and others brought water and wiped away every picture inside it.

questionEn: What is the juristic distinction regarding praying an obligatory (fard) prayer versus voluntary (nafl) prayer inside the Kaaba or Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: Many scholars advise against fard prayer inside because a worshiper cannot face the Kaaba externally, whereas nafl prayer inside is universally valid and Sunnah
Obligatory prayer inside is required for every pilgrim
No prayer of any kind is valid inside
Only Maghrib is valid inside
explanationEn: Hanbali and other jurists distinguish between obligatory prayer (requiring facing the structure from outside) and voluntary prayer, which the Prophet ﷺ himself offered inside.

questionEn: How is the exact starting and ending alignment of Al-Hajar al-Aswad marked for pilgrims across the crowded Mataf today?
optionsEn: A red bridge over Mina
A green LED light panel on the mosque wall opposite the Black Stone corner (replacing an earlier floor stripe)
A white gate at Safa
A blue line at Muzdalifah
explanationEn: Historically a dark marble line ran from the Black Stone corner across the Mataf floor; to prevent halting in the middle of moving lanes, a bright green light on the opposite wall now marks the line.

questionEn: In which direction do pilgrims move when performing Tawaf around the Holy Kaaba?
optionsEn: Clockwise, keeping the Kaaba on their right
Alternating clockwise and counter-clockwise each lap
Counter-clockwise, keeping the Kaaba on their left
Backwards while facing the door
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ practice, every Tawaf begins aligned with Al-Hajar al-Aswad and proceeds counter-clockwise so the Kaaba remains on the pilgrim's left.

questionEn: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ helped carry stones alongside him when Quraysh rebuilt the Kaaba before prophethood?
optionsEn: Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Salman al-Farsi (RA)
Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA)
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) narrated that when the Kaaba was rebuilt, the Prophet ﷺ and his uncle Al-Abbas (RA) carried stones together; when the Prophet's izar loosened, he fainted out of innate modesty until clothed properly.

questionEn: How did the number of interior wooden pillars in Quraysh's pre-Islamic Kaaba compare to Ibn al-Zubayr's later design?
optionsEn: Quraysh placed 6 pillars in two rows of 3; Ibn al-Zubayr placed 3 pillars in a single row
Quraysh had 12 pillars; Ibn al-Zubayr had 1
Neither had any pillars
Both had 10 marble pillars
explanationEn: Quraysh originally erected six wooden columns in two rows to support their roof, whereas Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) streamlined the interior to three stout pillars in a central line.

questionEn: What happened to the Black Stone in 317 AH (930 CE) during the Qarmatian attack on Makkah?
optionsEn: It was buried beneath Mount Safa
Abu Tahir al-Qarmati pried it out and carried it to Al-Ahsa (Eastern Arabia), keeping it for about 22 years
It fell into the Red Sea
It was taken to Constantinople
explanationEn: In one of the darkest tragedies in Makkan history, the Qarmatians raided Makkah during Hajj in 317 AH and removed the Black Stone until it was returned in 339 AH.

questionEn: When the Qarmatians finally returned the Black Stone to Makkah in 339 AH, how did scholars confirm its authenticity?
optionsEn: By a golden seal stamped on its back
By weighing it on a camel scale
By testing its distinct physical properties and matching witnesses who knew its exact fractured shape and earlier silver fittings
By a letter from Cairo
explanationEn: Historical accounts record that witnesses examined the returned stone—matching its fractured edges to the corner masonry and testing its distinctive properties—confirming it was indeed Al-Hajar al-Aswad.

questionEn: Where on the Kaaba wall is the silver frame of Al-Hajar al-Aswad mounted?
optionsEn: Inside the interior ceiling
Along the top of Hijr Ismail
Above the door lintel
Recessed directly into a stone niche at the exterior eastern corner of the Kaaba
explanationEn: The Black Stone is embedded in a recessed niche inside the exterior eastern corner masonry at arm's reach for Tawaf pilgrims.

questionEn: Why does the Black Stone NOT appear as a massive solid corner boulder today?
optionsEn: It was shattered over centuries by fires and attacks, leaving eight visible pieces embedded in dark resin within the oval silver frame
It was carved down by the Abbasids
Half of it was moved to Madinah
It shrinks each century
explanationEn: The oval silver housing holds a dark ambergris-and-musk cement containing the remaining small dark fragments of the original heavenly stone.

questionEn: Which materials construct the protective enclosure around Maqam Ibrahim today?
optionsEn: Carved oak wood
Tempered crystal glass framed in gold-plated brass and copper
Plain iron bars
Black granite
explanationEn: In the 1960s and 1990s, the bulky stone pavilion over Maqam Ibrahim was replaced with a compact crystal-and-gilded-brass enclosure so more pilgrims could see the footprints and circulate smoothly.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the light of the Black Stone and Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: They glow blue during eclipses
They were formed from sunlight
They are two rubies from Paradise whose radiance Allah dimmed, or else they would illuminate everything between East and West
They came from Mount Sinai
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: 'The Corner (Black Stone) and the Maqam are two jewels from the jewels of Paradise; had Allah not extinguished their light, they would have illuminated all between East and West.'

questionEn: Why is it forbidden in Islam to build a replica of the Kaaba elsewhere for Tawaf or worship?
optionsEn: Because stone is scarce outside Makkah
Because replicas face north
Because only Cairo may weave Kiswahs
Because Allah appointed one single Sacred House on earth as the focal point of Tawaf and the Qiblah of all Muslims
explanationEn: Tawaf is an act of worship restricted exclusively by revelation to the Baitullah (House of Allah) in Makkah; circumambulating any other building as worship is strictly prohibited.

questionEn: Which wall of the Kaaba faces roughly toward Maqam Ibrahim and the direction of Mount Safa?
optionsEn: The northeastern wall (containing the Kaaba Door)
The northwestern wall (Hijr Ismail side)
The southwestern wall
The southern wall only
explanationEn: The northeastern facade contains the Kaaba's door and faces Maqam Ibrahim and the eastern arc of the Mataf.

questionEn: In what order are the four corners of the Kaaba passed during a single counter-clockwise Tawaf circuit?
optionsEn: Black Stone -> Rukn al-Yamani -> Rukn al-Shami -> Rukn al-Iraqi
Black Stone -> Rukn al-Iraqi -> Rukn al-Shami -> Rukn al-Yamani -> back to Black Stone
Rukn al-Iraqi -> Black Stone -> Rukn al-Yamani -> Rukn al-Shami
Rukn al-Shami -> Black Stone -> Rukn al-Iraqi -> Rukn al-Yamani
explanationEn: Starting at the Black Stone (East) and walking counter-clockwise, you pass Rukn al-Iraqi (North), round Hijr Ismail to Rukn al-Shami (West), reach Rukn al-Yamani (South), and return to the Black Stone.

questionEn: Which early Umayyad Caliph sent large quantities of gold to adorn the Kaaba's door, Mizab, and interior pillars?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)
Salman al-Farsi (RA)
Caliph Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
explanationEn: Historians like al-Azraqi note that Umayyad Caliph Al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik sent large quantities of gold to plate the Mizab, door, and interior pillars of the Kaaba.

questionEn: What do scholars clarify about standing beneath Mizab al-Rahmah inside Hijr Ismail when rain falls in Makkah?
optionsEn: Rain cools the Mataf only
The spout points toward Yemen
Rain never falls in Makkah
Rain itself is a blessed time for dua, and Hijr Ismail is part of the Kaaba, though no authentic hadith requires crowding beneath the spout itself
explanationEn: Rain itself is a blessed time when dua is answered, and Hijr Ismail is part of the Kaaba; scholars clarify there is no authentic specific hadith obligating crowding under the Mizab.

questionEn: Why do scholars discourage rubbing the Kiswah, Maqam Ibrahim enclosure, or northern Kaaba walls for blessing?
optionsEn: Because physical touching (istilam) is an act of worship strictly limited to the Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani as taught by the Prophet ﷺ
Because the fabric is delicate
Because the Kiswah is replaced daily
Because only guards may touch stone
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) corrected Mu'awiyah (RA) when the latter touched all four corners, reminding him that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ touched only the two Yemeni corners (Black Stone and Rukn al-Yamani).

questionEn: Which two corners of the Kaaba are collectively called 'Al-Ruknan al-Yamaniyyan' (the two Yemeni corners) in classical Hadith texts?
optionsEn: Rukn al-Iraqi and Rukn al-Shami
Al-Hajar al-Aswad and Rukn al-Yamani
Bab al-Safa and Bab al-Umrah
Maqam Ibrahim and Al-Hatim
explanationEn: Because both the eastern corner (Black Stone) and southern corner (Rukn al-Yamani) face roughly toward the southern/Yemeni quarter relative to Syria, early texts call both 'Al-Ruknayn al-Yamaniyyayn'.

questionEn: Why must pilgrims currently in the state of Ihram take care before touching the Black Stone, Rukn al-Yamani, or Kiswah?
optionsEn: They are wet with rainwater
They are hot to the touch
Attendants frequently apply musk, oud, and ambergris perfume to them, and wearing perfume is prohibited while in Ihram
They are closed on Mondays
explanationEn: Because the Black Stone, Rukn al-Yamani, and Kiswah are frequently perfumed with musk and oud, a pilgrim in Ihram must take care not to transfer wet perfume onto their hands or garments.

questionEn: What sits inlaid on the marble floor inside the Kaaba marking where the Prophet ﷺ prayed on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: A golden throne
A wooden pulpit
A sunken fountain
A distinct inlaid marble slab (Rukhamah) positioned between the pillars facing the rear wall
explanationEn: A differently patterned marble tile on the Kaaba floor marks the traditional spot where the Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer between the two forward columns.

questionEn: What do the marble plaques mounted along the upper interior walls of the Kaaba commemorate?
optionsEn: Dates and rulers who carried out historical restorations of the Kaaba (such as Ibn al-Zubayr, Murad IV, and modern custodians)
Names of Makkah merchants
Poetry from Ukaz market
Tax ledgers
explanationEn: Inscribed marble plaques mounted inside the upper interior walls record dates and rulers who restored the Kaaba, including Sultan Murad IV and modern custodians.

questionEn: Why is the Kiswah assembled from 47 vertical strips of black silk organized into five main sections?
optionsEn: To represent the 47 tribes of Makkah
To fit the four walls separately plus the door curtain (Sitara), making hoisting and installation around the 14-meter walls manageable
Because looms can only weave 10 cm
To allow pilgrims to take strips home during Tawaf
explanationEn: The Kiswah comprises four giant wall curtains (one per side) plus the door Sitara, assembled from 47 woven silk breadths joined carefully in place around the Kaaba.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: How is the bottom edge of the Kiswah secured firmly against Makkan desert winds?
optionsEn: With iron chains
With plastic clips
With heavy braided ropes laced through bottom eyelets to brass rings set into Al-Shadhirwan
With velvet ribbons
explanationEn: Strong cotton ropes run through eyelets along the bottom of the Kiswah and anchor tightly to brass rings fixed into the Shadhirwan base so desert winds cannot billow it.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What happens when strong wind occasionally lifts the Kiswah slightly to reveal the stone wall underneath?
optionsEn: It is considered a bad omen
The Haram must close
Tawaf must pause
It simply reveals the underlying Makkan granite masonry, reminding believers that sanctity belongs to the House itself rather than its silk drape
explanationEn: In earlier times, winds lifting the Kiswah was seen simply as a natural occurrence showing the bare stones of Baitullah; today strong tension ropes secure it against gusts.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic Surah emphasizes that the Kaaba was built as a house of guidance ('hudan lil-alamin') and contains 'clear signs, among them Maqam Ibrahim'?
optionsEn: Surah Aal-Imran 3:96-97
Surah Yusuf 12:1
Surah Maryam 19:1
Surah Al-Qasas 28:1
explanationEn: Surah Aal-Imran (3:96-97) reads: 'Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Bakkah—blessed and a guidance for the worlds. In it are clear signs, the standing place of Ibrahim...'

questionEn: What is the third 'clear sign' mentioned in Surah Aal-Imran (3:97) right after mentioning Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: Whoever enters it is rich
Whoever enters it shall be safe (wa man dakhalahu kana aminan)
Whoever touches it becomes immortal
Whoever builds beside it rules Makkah
explanationEn: Surah Aal-Imran (3:97) declares 'wa man dakhalahu kana aminan'—whoever enters the Sanctuary is granted security under Allah's sacred law.

questionEn: What did Angel Jibril (AS) teach Prophet Ibrahim (AS) after showing him the site of the Kaaba, according to classical Tafsir narrations?
optionsEn: How to trade in Damascus
How to mine silver
The rites of Hajj (manasik), fulfilling Ibrahim's prayer 'And show us our rites' (2:128)
How to build ships
explanationEn: Classical Tafsir reports that Jibril (AS) guided Ibrahim (AS) through the rites of pilgrimage, fulfilling his prayer in 2:128: 'And show us our rites (wa arina manasikana).'

questionEn: What was the famous prayer Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) made for their descendants while raising the Kaaba walls in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:129)?
optionsEn: To send them kings of gold
To end all travel to Makkah
To move the Kaaba to Jerusalem
To raise among them a Messenger from themselves who would recite Allah's verses, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them
explanationEn: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ famously said: 'I am the answer to the supplication of my father Ibrahim,' referring directly to Surah Al-Baqarah 2:129.

questionEn: Which exterior wall of the Kaaba runs cleanly without doors, Hijr Ismail, or spouts, stretching from Rukn al-Yamani to Rukn al-Shami?
optionsEn: The southwestern face (the back wall)
The northeastern face
The northwestern face
The eastern corner
explanationEn: The southwestern wall stretches smoothly from Rukn al-Shami to Rukn al-Yamani, historically containing the sealed rear door site known as Al-Mustajar.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ specifically warn Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) about regarding kissing the Black Stone in crowds?
optionsEn: To push everyone aside forcefully
'O Umar, you are a strong man; do not crowd around the Stone lest you harm the weak'
Never to approach the eastern corner
To kiss it only after Arafat
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ specifically instructed Umar (RA) not to harm weaker pilgrims at the Black Stone, teaching strength must always be paired with gentleness in the Haram.

questionEn: Besides his freedman Usamah ibn Zayd (RA), which two companions entered inside the Kaaba with the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: Abu Sufyan and Khalid
Salman and Abu Dharr
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) and Uthman ibn Talhah (RA)
Talhah and Zubayr
explanationEn: Uthman ibn Talhah (custodian of the key), Usamah ibn Zayd, and Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) entered inside with the Prophet ﷺ, while others waited outside.

questionEn: What does 'Istilam' mean in the terminology of Tawaf around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Climbing the roof of Al-Haram
Shaving one's head at Marwah
Drinking Zamzam after sunset
Touching, kissing, or gesturing toward Al-Hajar al-Aswad (and touching Rukn al-Yamani)
explanationEn: Istilam comes from 'salam' or touching with the palm; in Tawaf it refers to greeting/touching the Black Stone (or gesturing to it) and touching Rukn al-Yamani.

questionEn: How does a pilgrim determine when they have completed a full Tawaf of seven circuits?
optionsEn: They begin aligned with Al-Hajar al-Aswad and pass Al-Hajar al-Aswad seven full times (finishing the 7th circuit back at the Black Stone line)
They start at Bab al-Salam and stop at Safa
They count five circuits on the upper floor
They walk around Maqam Ibrahim seven times
explanationEn: Each circuit begins and ends at the line of the Black Stone; completing seven full circles brings the pilgrim back past the Black Stone line at the end of the seventh lap.

questionEn: If the Iqamah for an obligatory congregational prayer is called while a pilgrim is in the middle of Tawaf, what must they do?
optionsEn: Continue walking during the prayer
Pause Tawaf at their current spot, pray the obligatory prayer in congregation, and afterward resume Tawaf from where they stopped
Leave the mosque immediately
Restart all seven circuits from scratch
explanationEn: Obligatory congregational prayer takes precedence; pilgrims stop at their position, join the prayer facing the Kaaba, and then resume from that exact point to finish their circuit.

questionEn: Which Prophet is uniquely commanded in Surah Al-Hajj (22:27) to proclaim the call of Hajj to all humanity across time?
optionsEn: Prophet Musa (AS)
Prophet Isa (AS)
Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
Prophet Yusuf (AS)
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:27), Allah commanded Ibrahim (AS): 'And proclaim to the people the Hajj; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel from every distant pass.'

questionEn: What does 'Al-Rukn' by itself usually refer to in early Hadith texts about Makkah?
optionsEn: Mount Safa
Bab al-Fath
The roof of Zamzam
Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Corner of the Black Stone)
explanationEn: In classical Hadith narrations, 'Al-Rukn' (the Corner) without further qualification typically denotes the corner of the Black Stone, whereas 'Al-Rukn al-Yamani' specifies the southern corner.

questionEn: Why is the Black Stone positioned at the eastern corner rather than in the middle of a wall?
optionsEn: To mark a clear starting and ending landmark visible from two sides as pilgrims turn into each circuit
Because stones could not fit in the middle
Because it was dropped by wind
To hide it behind Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: Placing Al-Hajar al-Aswad right at the eastern angle ensures every pilgrim turning that corner sees a distinct focal marker for beginning and ending each Tawaf lap.

questionEn: What is the purpose of the two open gaps between the Kaaba's northwestern corners and the curved Hijr Ismail wall?
optionsEn: Solid bronze walls
Open passageways allowing worshipers to step inside Hijr Ismail to pray
Water canals leading to Jeddah
Lockers for shoes
explanationEn: Two open passageways roughly 2.2 meters wide exist between the Kaaba corners and the curved Hatim wall, allowing pilgrims to enter and exit Al-Hijr.

questionEn: Which early builders are recorded in Makkan chronicles like al-Azraqi as having rebuilt or tended the Kaaba prior to Qusayy ibn Kilab?
optionsEn: Prophet Zakariyya (AS) and Yahya (AS)
Prophet Yunus (AS) and Prophet Yusuf (AS)
Ibrahim & Ismail (AS), followed by Amaliqah and Jurhum
Prophet Lut (AS) and Shu'ayb (AS)
explanationEn: Al-Azraqi and classical historians trace the Kaaba's ancient custodianship through Ibrahim & Ismail (AS), followed by the tribes of Amaliqah and Jurhum before Qusayy and Quraysh.

questionEn: Which ancestor of the Prophet ﷺ united Quraysh in Makkah, rebuilt the Kaaba with palm beams, and organized Makkah's civic sanctuary offices?
optionsEn: Amr ibn al-As
Abu Lahab
Al-Walid ibn Yazid
Qusayy ibn Kilab
explanationEn: After claiming custody of Makkah, Qusayy ibn Kilab rebuilt the Kaaba and organized Makkan civic offices around the sanctuary.

questionEn: What nickname did Quraysh give Muhammad ﷺ before prophethood that led them to accept his arbitration over the Black Stone immediately?
optionsEn: Al-Amin (The Trustworthy)
Al-Fatih
Al-Ghazi
Al-Hakim
explanationEn: When the elders agreed to let the next man entering Bab Bani Shaybah judge the dispute, they rejoiced seeing Muhammad ﷺ, exclaiming: 'This is Al-Amin! We are pleased with him!'

questionEn: Who was the oldest elder of Quraysh who proposed letting the first person to enter the sanctuary gate arbitrate the Black Stone dispute?
optionsEn: Abu Jahl
Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi
Utbah ibn Rabi'ah
Al-Nadr ibn al-Harith
explanationEn: After four or five nights of tense standoff nearly erupting into bloodshed, the elder Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah proposed accepting the verdict of the first person entering the gate.

questionEn: How did Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) reassure terrified Makkans when demolishing the fire-damaged Kaaba walls in 65 AH?
optionsEn: He waited for permission from Yemen
He waited for winter rain
He climbed up himself and removed stones for three days until people saw no harm befell him and joined in
He brought 10,000 camels
explanationEn: When people fled to Mina fearing divine wrath as demolition began, Ibn al-Zubayr stood atop the Kaaba removing stones himself until everyone saw his sincere intention and returned to help.

questionEn: What did Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) uncover when he excavated along the northern Hijr Ismail side?
optionsEn: A Roman road
A bronze statue
A sunken palace
The original foundation stones laid by Prophet Ibrahim (AS), resembling interlocked camel necks
explanationEn: Ibn al-Zubayr summoned fifty Makkan notables to witness the ancient interlocking green-tinted foundation boulders of Ibrahim (AS) buried beneath Hijr Ismail.

questionEn: Which compass direction does the Kaaba's main facade (with the Door) face roughly?
optionsEn: Northeast
Due West
Due South
Northwest
explanationEn: The Door of the Kaaba sits on the northeastern wall, facing roughly toward Maqam Ibrahim and the eastern arc of Al-Mataf.

questionEn: Why does the Kaaba carry a black silk Kiswah in contrast to pilgrims' white Ihram garments?
optionsEn: Solely for camera visibility
Adopted by the Abbasids and enduring ever since, black silk provides solemn majesty and striking visual contrast in Makkah's sunlit valley
Because black dye only grows in Makkah
Because white silk is forbidden on buildings
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ permitted different clean cloths for the Kiswah; the black silk with gold calligraphy became the enduring Islamic tradition since the Abbasid era, evoking solemn majesty.

questionEn: What is the approximate height (width) of the golden Hizam belt around the Kiswah?
optionsEn: 10 cm
4 meters
95 centimeters (nearly 1 meter)
8 meters
explanationEn: The Hizam measures roughly 95 cm tall and runs 47 meters in total length around all four walls, making its golden calligraphy clearly legible across the Mataf.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Which Arabic calligraphic script style is used for the monumental Qur'anic verses on the Kiswah's golden belt?
optionsEn: Diwani
Kufic geometric only
Ruq'ah shorthand
Classic Thuluth script
explanationEn: Master calligraphers execute the Kiswah's verses—drawn from Surahs Al-Baqarah, Aal-Imran, Al-Hajj, and Al-Fath—in monumental Thuluth script.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What damaged the Kiswah and Kaaba walls during the 64 AH siege of Makkah against Ibn al-Zubayr (RA)?
optionsEn: Wind carried sparks from a brazier/catapult fire, igniting the dry silk Kiswah and weakening the stone and roof timbers
The Kiswah extinguished the fire automatically
A snowstorm collapsed the roof
Sea waves reached Makkah
explanationEn: Sparks blown by strong wind ignited the dry silk Kiswah and timber ceiling during the 64 AH siege, prompting Ibn al-Zubayr's (RA) subsequent full reconstruction.

questionEn: When performing Istilam at the Black Stone, what short phrase did the Prophet ﷺ pronounce?
optionsEn: SubhanAllah wal-hamdu lillah
Allahu Akbar (or Bismillahi Allahu Akbar)
Astaghfirullah al-Azim
La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) reported that the Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf on his camel, pointing to the Black Stone with a curved staff and saying 'Allahu Akbar' (and Ibn Umar added 'Bismillahi Allahu Akbar').

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ perform Tawaf during the Farewell Pilgrimage so that large crowds could see him clearly?
optionsEn: He asked someone else to walk for him
He skipped Tawaf altogether
He rode his camel, pointing to the Black Stone with his curved staff (mihjan)
He performed Tawaf from Mount Safa
explanationEn: To let the large crowds see him clearly and learn the rites, the Prophet ﷺ performed Tawaf riding his camel, demonstrating the permissibility of mounts or wheelchairs when needed.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim perform a standalone Tawaf by proxy on behalf of a healthy living person who is absent from Makkah?
optionsEn: Only Imams may make dua during Tawaf
Yes, seven laps per family member automatically
It is forbidden to make dua for others during Tawaf
Standalone proxy Tawaf for a healthy living person is not valid; instead one makes abundant dua for loved ones during one's own Tawaf
explanationEn: While one may perform a full Umrah or Hajj on behalf of a deceased or permanently incapacitated person, standalone proxy Tawaf for a healthy absent person is not established; make sincere dua for them instead.

questionEn: Why do scholars advise against shouting 'Bismillahi Allahu Akbar' in loud group choruses during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Saying Takbir individually and calmly preserves serenity, humility, and concentration for other worshipers
Because Arabic is forbidden in the Mataf
Because only the Muezzin may speak
Because it must be whispered only at night
explanationEn: Saying 'Allahu Akbar' softly or at normal personal volume preserves humility and avoids disturbing fellow worshipers engaged in prayer and supplication.

questionEn: Approximately how long is one close ground-level lap directly around the Kaaba compared to upper-floor circuits?
optionsEn: Exactly 5 kilometers close to the wall
Roughly 50–70 meters close to the Kaaba, expanding to hundreds of meters in the outer Mataf and upper floors
Only 10 meters
Exactly 1 mile inside
explanationEn: Walking close to the Kaaba covers around 50–70 meters per lap (under 500 meters total), whereas upper-tier Tawaf paths cover several kilometers over 7 laps.

questionEn: What sits directly beneath the Kaaba's door threshold on the Shadhirwan stone?
optionsEn: A silver bridge
A well of oil
A recessed dark marble step traditionally called Al-Ma'jan (or threshold step)
Nothing—the door reaches the floor
explanationEn: A recessed notch in the Shadhirwan right under the Door of the Kaaba marks an ancient praying/stepping spot; today pilgrims pass smoothly without climbing onto it.

questionEn: How are the two golden leaves of Bab al-Ka'bah fastened from the outside?
optionsEn: They are welded shut permanently
With wooden pegs
With a fingerprint scanner
With a heavy traditional padlock whose key is safeguarded by the senior custodian of Banu Shaybah
explanationEn: The Door of the Kaaba is secured with a traditional heavy lock housed in a protective sleeve; the key rests in a green embroidered pouch held by the Shaybah custodian.

questionEn: What is the roof of the Holy Kaaba surfaced with today?
optionsEn: White marble tiles and waterproofing around a small roof-access hatch
Thatched palm leaves
Black velvet
Solar panels
explanationEn: Modern restorations paved the flat Kaaba roof in white marble sloping gently toward Mizab al-Rahmah to ensure rapid rainwater drainage.

questionEn: Which two prophets are linked directly with Maqam Ibrahim as they collaborated to build the House?
optionsEn: Musa and Harun (AS)
Ibrahim and Ismail (AS)
Dawud and Sulayman (AS)
Yaqub and Yusuf (AS)
explanationEn: As Ibrahim (AS) raised the courses of stone handed to him by Ismail (AS), Maqam Ibrahim served as his standing stone.

questionEn: Why did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) stand upon the stone of Maqam Ibrahim while raising the Kaaba walls?
optionsEn: To avoid touching sand
Because the ground was flooded
So he could reach the upper courses of stone comfortably while Ismail handed stones up to him
To address Quraysh
explanationEn: Standing upon the stone enabled Ibrahim (AS) to lift the masonry higher while Ismail (AS) passed each stone up to him as they both recited 'Rabbana taqabbal minna'.

questionEn: How frequently did the Prophet ﷺ acknowledge Al-Hajar al-Aswad during his Farewell Tawaf?
optionsEn: He walked past without acknowledging it
He covered it with his cloak
He touched it only on circuit 7
He touched or gestured to it at the start and end of every circuit
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) and Ibn Umar (RA) recorded that the Prophet ﷺ acknowledged (kissed, touched, or gestured to) the Black Stone at the start of Tawaf and at the completion of each of the seven laps.

questionEn: Does a pilgrim need to be in a state of ritual purity (Wudu) for Tawaf according to the majority of Islamic jurists?
optionsEn: Yes, the majority (Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali) hold Wudu is a condition of Tawaf based on the hadith comparing Tawaf to prayer
No, Wudu is irrelevant
Only for the 7th circuit
Only for men
explanationEn: Because Tawaf resembles prayer in sanctity and takes place inside Al-Masjid al-Haram, maintaining Wudu (while avoiding idle chatter) is emphasized by the majority of scholars.

questionEn: What makes Tawaf different from Salah according to the famous narration from Ibn Abbas (RA)?
optionsEn: Facing the Kaaba directly with the chest is required in Tawaf
Allah permitted speaking good words during Tawaf, whereas speech invalidates Salah
Tawaf requires no intention
Tawaf has only 3 circuits
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Tawaf around the House is similar to prayer, except that you speak during it; so whoever speaks during it, let him speak nothing but good.'

questionEn: What is 'Raml' in Tawaf around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Sprinkling sand on the head
Running all seven circuits
Walking briskly with short, firm steps (for men only) during the first three circuits of an arrival or Umrah Tawaf
Sitting after each circuit
explanationEn: Raml is a Sunnah specifically for men in the first three laps of Tawaf al-Qudum or Umrah Tawaf (not women, and not in the last four laps or voluntary Tawafs).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ allow the companions to walk at a normal pace between Rukn al-Yamani and the Black Stone during Umrah al-Qada'?
optionsEn: Because that side was flooded
Because it was raining
Because the Black Stone was missing
Because Quraysh onlookers on the northern hills could not see them behind that southern face—allowing them to rest briefly
explanationEn: Out of compassion, the Prophet ﷺ let them catch their breath between Rukn al-Yamani and the Black Stone out of Quraysh's line of sight, though in later Hajj he performed Raml fully around all four sides.

questionEn: What is 'Idtiba' during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Passing the upper Ihram cloth (rida) under the right armpit and throwing it over the left shoulder, leaving the right shoulder bare
Covering the head completely
Wearing green sandals
Folding the arms on the chest
explanationEn: Idtiba' is a Sunnah for men during the Umrah/Qudum Tawaf only; once Tawaf concludes, both shoulders must be covered before praying the two rak'ahs.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding performing Raml when the Mataf is extremely packed and brisk walking would cause collisions?
optionsEn: Push people aside anyway
Walk calmly at the crowd's pace, as Raml is a Sunnah that is waived when it causes harm or isn't feasible
Leave the Mataf and do Raml in the street
Repeat Tawaf at dawn
explanationEn: Jurists unanimously emphasize that Raml is Sunnah only when space permits safely; preserving safety and avoiding jostling overrides brisk striding.

questionEn: Which face of the Kaaba sits closest to Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: The northwestern face (Hijr Ismail)
The southwestern rear wall
The northeastern face (the Door wall near Al-Hajar al-Aswad)
The roof edge only
explanationEn: Maqam Ibrahim stands straight out from the northeastern wall (the Door wall), slightly closer toward the Black Stone corner than the Iraqi corner.

questionEn: Where does the Imam of Al-Masjid al-Haram stand when leading the daily prayers?
optionsEn: Facing away from the Kaaba
On Mount Safa
Inside Hijr Ismail facing Syria
Facing the Kaaba (traditionally near Maqam Ibrahim), with the congregation forming complete circles around the Kaaba
explanationEn: The Imam faces the Kaaba directly, and worshipers form concentric circles all around the Sacred House.

questionEn: What is the unique geometry of prayer rows inside Al-Masjid al-Haram compared to every other mosque on earth?
optionsEn: Rows form unbroken concentric circles encircling the Kaaba from all four sides
Rows are diagonal
Only one straight row exists
People pray facing west only
explanationEn: Al-Masjid al-Haram is the only mosque where believers pray in full circles around the Qiblah, visibly embodying the unity of the Muslim Ummah centered on Allah's House.

questionEn: How did Qusayy ibn Kilab's descendant Hashim earn his famous name (literally 'Crusher of Bread') in Makkah?
optionsEn: He broke stones for the Kaaba
During a severe famine, he brought bread from Syria and crumbled it into meat broth (Tharid) to feed Makkah's people and pilgrims
He shattered idols
He milled wheat inside Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Born Amr ibn Abd Manaf, he earned the honored title 'Hashim' for crumbling bread into broth to sustain hungry Makkans and visiting pilgrims under the Rifadah office.

questionEn: What did the office of 'Al-Hijabah' (Al-Sidanah) entail in pre-Islamic and Islamic Makkah?
optionsEn: Guiding caravans to Iraq
Selling camels at Mina
Holding the key to the Kaaba, opening/closing its door, and maintaining its Kiswah and interior
Collecting rain at Arafat
explanationEn: Hijabah (or Sidanah) meant exclusive stewardship of the Kaaba's key and interior, entrusted permanently by the Prophet ﷺ to Uthman ibn Talhah and Banu Shaybah.

questionEn: Where did Qusayy ibn Kilab build 'Dar al-Nadwah', the assembly house of Quraysh elders, relative to the Kaaba?
optionsEn: On top of Jabal al-Noor
Inside Mina valley
At the summit of Arafat
Directly facing the Kaaba on its northwestern side, with a door opening straight onto the sanctuary courtyard
explanationEn: Dar al-Nadwah stood immediately northwest of the Kaaba; Quraysh met there for major civic councils, and centuries later its site was absorbed into Al-Haram's courtyard.

questionEn: What truth did the Prophet ﷺ explain to Aishah (RA) beginning 'Were it not that your people are close to the time of ignorance...'?
optionsEn: Why he did not demolish the Kaaba to restore Ibrahim's full foundations and add two ground-level doors
Why Muslims should not visit Safa
Why the Kaaba should move to Madinah
Why the black Kiswah was chosen
explanationEn: This narration teaches profound Prophetic wisdom: avoiding unnecessary social upheaval over structural changes when the core worship of the Kaaba was already intact.

questionEn: How did the height of the Kaaba change between Quraysh's 605 CE rebuild and Ibn al-Zubayr's 65 AH rebuild?
optionsEn: Quraysh lowered it to 2 meters
Quraysh raised it from ~9 to 18 cubits, and Ibn al-Zubayr raised it to 27 cubits (~13–14 meters)
Both kept it at 9 cubits
Both built it 100 cubits tall
explanationEn: Quraysh doubled the Kaaba's height from 9 to 18 cubits and roofed it; Ibn al-Zubayr (RA) later raised it to 27 cubits (~13–14 meters), which remains its majestic height today.

questionEn: What did Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan exclaim years later upon learning that Aishah (RA) truly narrated the Prophet's ﷺ wish for Ibn al-Zubayr's Kaaba layout?
optionsEn: 'Move Maqam Ibrahim inside'
'Tear it down again immediately'
'I wish I had left Abu Khubayb (Ibn al-Zubayr) with what he had built!'
'Close the sanctuary'
explanationEn: Realizing Ibn al-Zubayr had faithfully acted on an authentic hadith from Aishah (RA), Caliph Abd al-Malik deeply regretted reversing the Hijr Ismail restoration.

questionEn: Which natural hazard repeatedly damaged the lower walls of the Kaaba across pre-modern centuries until diversion tunnels were built?
optionsEn: Volcanic lava
Ocean tides
Glaciers
Flash floods (Suyul) pouring down Makkah's steep rocky valleys directly into the low-lying Kaaba basin
explanationEn: Because the Kaaba sits at the lowest basin (Batn Makkah) surrounded by bare granite hills, heavy seasonal rainstorms historically flooded the Mataf up to the Black Stone level or higher.

questionEn: What engineering infrastructure solved the centuries-old problem of flash floods inundating Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Modern subterranean flood-diversion tunnels, valley culverts, and Mataf drainage channels
Building a wall 50 meters high around Makkah
Moving the Kaaba higher up a hill
Removing Mount Safa
explanationEn: Massive underground stormwater diversion tunnels carved beneath Makkah's surrounding valleys now channel heavy seasonal rains safely away from the Haram courtyard.

questionEn: What is the special thermal property of the white Thassos marble paving the Mataf courtyard today?
optionsEn: It glows red at night
It reflects sunlight and absorbs nocturnal moisture through tiny pores, keeping the floor cool for barefoot worshipers even in midday summer heat
It is heated electrically
It is coated in wax
explanationEn: Imported Greek Thassos marble slabs reflect solar radiation and retain coolness underfoot, allowing millions of pilgrims to walk barefoot comfortably in Makkah's intense sun.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: Toward which geographic region does 'Al-Rukn al-Yamani' point?
optionsEn: Toward Iraq
Toward Damascus
Toward Yemen (South/Southwest)
Toward Jeddah
explanationEn: Rukn al-Yamani sits at the southern corner of the Kaaba, pointing generally southward toward the Arabian Peninsula's Yemeni quarter.

questionEn: According to scholars following Ibn Umar (RA), what should a pilgrim do if crowds prevent reaching Rukn al-Yamani?
optionsEn: Point to it and say Allahu Akbar, just like the Black Stone
Stop and touch the floor
Go back and try again
Simply pass by without pointing to it or saying Takbir specifically for it, as gesturing from afar is established only for the Black Stone
explanationEn: Scholars clarify that pointing from afar with Takbir is specific to Al-Hajar al-Aswad; for Rukn al-Yamani, one touches it directly if accessible, and simply passes if crowded.

questionEn: What is the Sunnah upon seeing the Holy Kaaba for the very first time?
optionsEn: Raise one's hands in sincere supplication (dua) and praise Allah—without any single rigid mandatory formula
Take a photo immediately before praying
Run directly into Hijr Ismail
Throw coins toward Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: While no specific wording is obligatory from the Prophet ﷺ, scholars recommend raising hands and making heartfelt dua upon first sighting the Kaaba, remembering Umar's (RA) dua 'Allahumma Antas-Salam wa minkas-salam'.

questionEn: How many idols had Quraysh and Arab tribes placed around the Kaaba before the Prophet ﷺ purified it on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: 12 idols
360 idols
700 idols
3 idols
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) reported that on the Day of Conquest, 360 idols stood around the Kaaba; the Prophet ﷺ struck them with a staff reciting 17:81 until every one toppled.

questionEn: What Qur'anic verse did the Prophet ﷺ recite as he pointed his staff at the 360 idols around the Kaaba on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Falaq 113:1
Surah Al-Fil 105:1
Surah Al-Isra 17:81 ('Truth has come, and falsehood has vanished. Indeed is falsehood ever bound to vanish.')
Surah Al-Kafirun 109:1
explanationEn: Reciting Surah Al-Isra 17:81 and Surah Saba 34:49, the Prophet ﷺ toppled the idols without touching them, restoring the Kaaba permanently to pure Tawhid.

questionEn: Who climbed onto the roof of the Kaaba on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah to call the first Islamic Adhan over the sanctuary?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)
Abu Sufyan (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
explanationEn: Commanded by the Prophet ﷺ, the once-enslaved Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) stood atop the Kaaba and proclaimed the Adhan of Tawhid across Makkah.

questionEn: What corrupt pre-Islamic practice did some Arab tribes perform during Tawaf that Islam abolished in Surah Al-A'raf (7:31) and in 9 AH?
optionsEn: Performing Tawaf completely naked, claiming they would not worship in clothes in which they had sinned
Walking backward
Carrying umbrellas
Tawaf at dawn
explanationEn: The Hums (Quraysh) forced outside pilgrims to buy Makkan garments or perform Tawaf naked; Islam banned naked Tawaf entirely and commanded 'Take your adornment at every mosque' (7:31).

questionEn: What did the Qur'an describe as the sum total of pagan worship around the Kaaba in Surah Al-Anfal (8:35)?
optionsEn: Quiet meditation
Nothing but whistling and clapping of hands (muka'an wa tasdiyah)
Chanting Arabic grammar
Giving charity to orphans
explanationEn: Surah Al-Anfal (8:35) rebukes Quraysh: 'And their prayer at the House was not except whistling and handclapping,' contrasting pagan noise with sincere Islamic Salah and Dhikr.

questionEn: Which companion led the 9 AH Hajj delegation to Makkah and had Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) proclaim that no polytheist could enter Al-Masjid al-Haram after that year?
optionsEn: Uthman ibn Affan (RA)
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
explanationEn: In 9 AH, the Prophet ﷺ appointed Abu Bakr (RA) as Amir al-Hajj and sent Ali (RA) to announce the opening verses of Surah At-Tawbah, permanently ending pagan rites at the Kaaba.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim on a wheelchair or mobility scooter perform Tawaf on the designated upper Mataf levels?
optionsEn: Only on the ground floor beside the Black Stone
No, wheelchairs are barred from Al-Haram
Only if pushed backwards
Yes, designated wheelchair and electric cart lanes on the upper floors allow smooth, valid Tawaf
explanationEn: Al-Masjid al-Haram provides dedicated ramps, elevators, free manual wheelchairs, and electric scooter lanes on upper tiers so elderly or disabled pilgrims complete Tawaf and Sa'i comfortably.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: Which category of pilgrim is explicitly excused by the Prophet ﷺ from performing Tawaf al-Wada' before departing Makkah?
optionsEn: Menstruating women (and women in post-natal bleeding)
Young men under 20
Merchants from Yemen
Anyone traveling by camel
explanationEn: When Safiyyah (RA) menstruated after Tawaf al-Ifadah, the Prophet ﷺ exempted her from Tawaf al-Wada' so her caravan would not be delayed.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim who has completed Tawaf al-Wada' exit Al-Masjid al-Haram according to the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Walking backward all the way out of the mosque
Walking out normally with humility and prayer, without the unauthentic practice of walking backward
Running out through Bab al-Fath
Sitting outside for 24 hours
explanationEn: Scholars point out that walking backward out of the mosque has no basis in the Sunnah and poses a tripping hazard; one simply departs normally facing forward with dua.

questionEn: Which two prophets are paired in Sahih Muslim (1360) for supplicating respectively for Makkah and for Madinah?
optionsEn: Prophet Dawud (AS) and Prophet Sulayman (AS)
Prophet Musa (AS) and Prophet Isa (AS)
Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
Prophet Nuh (AS) and Prophet Hud (AS)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ famously supplicated: 'O Allah, Ibrahim was Your slave, Your friend, and Your prophet, and I am Your slave and prophet; he prayed to You for Makkah, and I pray to You for Madinah the like of what Ibrahim prayed for Makkah.'

questionEn: What heartfelt words did the Prophet ﷺ speak looking back at Makkah as he departed during the Hijrah?
optionsEn: 'I will never care for this valley'
'I prefer Damascus'
'Only Jeddah is blessed'
'By Allah, you are the best of Allah's land and the most beloved of Allah's land to Allah; had I not been driven out of you, I would never have left you'
explanationEn: These tender words of the Prophet ﷺ express his deep love for Makkah and confirm its unmatched spiritual rank as the most beloved place on earth to Allah.

questionEn: Why is the stone of Maqam Ibrahim kept enclosed inside tempered crystal glass rather than left open for touching?
optionsEn: To protect the ancient stone's fragile surface from erosion while letting pilgrims see it clearly and circulate safely
To keep it invisible
Because it is radioactive
Because it floats
explanationEn: Centuries of hands rubbing the stone wore away finer details of the footprints; encasing it in transparent crystal preserves the blessed relic for future generations.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What is the rule regarding praying two Sunnah rak'ahs after a voluntary (nafl) Tawaf?
optionsEn: Only obligatory Tawafs have two rak'ahs
Two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim (or anywhere in the mosque) follow EVERY completed 7-circuit Tawaf, whether obligatory or voluntary
One must pray seven rak'ahs
One prays only at night
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ general practice, every complete Tawaf of seven laps concludes with two rak'ahs of Sunnah prayer.

questionEn: Why is it forbidden in Islam to perform Tawaf directly around Maqam Ibrahim instead of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Because Maqam Ibrahim belongs to Madinah
Because Maqam Ibrahim is too small
Because Tawaf is an act of worship exclusively around the Holy Kaaba itself
Because it blocks Bab al-Safa
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Hajj (22:29), Allah specifies 'wal-yattawwafu bil-Baytil-Atiq'—circumambulation belongs solely to the Ancient House, never around shrines or Maqams on their own.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when handing the Kaaba key back to Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: That Banu Shaybah would keep the key for only ten years
That only kings could hold it
That the key should be melted down
That none would try to seize the Kaaba's key from Banu Talhah/Banu Shaybah except an oppressor
explanationEn: Saying 'Khudhuha ya Bani Talhah khalidatan talidah,' the Prophet ﷺ confirmed permanent stewardship of the Kaaba key for Uthman ibn Talhah's lineage until the Day of Resurrection.

questionEn: Which two prominent Quraysh commanders rode from Makkah to Madinah together with Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) in 8 AH to accept Islam?
optionsEn: Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA) and Amr ibn al-As (RA)
Abu Lahab and Abu Jahl
Utbah and Shaybah
Safwan and Ikrimah
explanationEn: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah in early 8 AH, Khalid ibn al-Walid, Amr ibn al-As, and Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) rode together to Madinah and embraced Islam.

questionEn: According to Bilal's (RA) description to Ibn Umar (RA), roughly how far from the rear interior wall of the Kaaba did the Prophet ﷺ stand when praying inside?
optionsEn: Right inside the doorway threshold
About three cubits from the opposite wall ahead of him, between the two forward pillars
Behind the third pillar facing the door
Inside the stairwell
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) asked Bilal (RA) precisely how far from the opposite wall the Prophet ﷺ prayed; Bilal replied 'about three cubits from the wall ahead of him.'

questionEn: What is the ornate chest/table kept inside the Kaaba primarily used for?
optionsEn: Holding Zamzam cups
Holding pilgrims' passports
Storing pure oud, rosewater, incense, and perfumes used during the Kaaba washing ceremony
Serving as a podium
explanationEn: A small decorative chest inside the Kaaba stores pure fragrances, rosewater flasks, and cleaning implements used by the custodians.

questionEn: Which famous Qur'anic passages are embroidered onto the Sitara (door curtain) of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: No Qur'an appears on the Sitara
Only Surah Al-Masad
Only Surah Al-Kawthar
Surah Al-Fatihah, Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), Surah Al-Ikhlas, and Surah Quraysh among others
explanationEn: The Sitara is famously embroidered with Surah Al-Fatihah, Ayat al-Kursi, the opening of Surah Al-Fath, Surah Quraysh, and invocations of Allah's mercy.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: How does the stone of Maqam Ibrahim visually contrast with the dark bluish-gray granite of the Kaaba walls?
optionsEn: It is a softer yellowish-white/brownish pitted stone preserved as a distinct historic relic
It is painted bright green
It is made of solid gold
It is dried clay
explanationEn: Descriptions note Maqam Ibrahim is roughly 50 cm tall and yellowish-white in hue, differing visibly from the dark granite of the Kaaba walls.

questionEn: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ see leaning against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur in the seventh heaven directly above the Kaaba during Al-Mi'raj?
optionsEn: Prophet Sulayman (AS)
Prophet Ibrahim (AS)
Prophet Yunus (AS)
Prophet Lut (AS)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ ascended to the seventh heaven during Mi'raj, Prophet Ibrahim (AS) was leaning against Al-Bayt al-Ma'mur, illustrating the cosmic harmony between earthly Tawaf and heavenly worship.

questionEn: What title does the Qur'an give Makkah in Surahs Al-An'am (6:92) and Ash-Shura (42:7) highlighting its central status among all towns on earth?
optionsEn: Dar al-Hijrah
Madinat al-Noor
Umm al-Qura (Mother of Cities)
Ard al-Sham
explanationEn: Allah revealed the Qur'an to warn 'Umm al-Qura' (Makkah) and all those around it—signifying Makkah as the ancestral and spiritual metropolis of humanity.

questionEn: What is the rule regarding hunting or killing a wild pigeon inside Al-Masjid al-Haram or anywhere inside Makkah's Haram boundaries?
optionsEn: Permissible for food
Permissible outside the mosque walls
Permissible only on Eid
Strictly forbidden—even frightening wild birds or game inside the Haram is prohibited
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared on the Day of Conquest: 'Its game shall not be chased (or frightened), its thorns shall not be cut...' protecting all wild creatures within the Haram.

questionEn: If someone deliberately or accidentally kills a wild pigeon inside the Haram boundaries, what do Islamic jurists require?
optionsEn: A compensatory expiation (fidyah/jaza') equivalent to the value of the animal (such as a sheep for a pigeon according to the Sahabah's precedent)
Nothing at all
Leaving Makkah forever
Fasting 60 days automatically
explanationEn: Based on Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:95) and verdicts of Umar and Uthman (RA), harming Haram game carries an equivalent compensation (jaza') fed to the poor of the Haram.

questionEn: Which harmful creatures are explicitly exempted from the Haram hunting ban—meaning they may be killed even inside the Haram if they pose danger?
optionsEn: Pigeons and gazelles
The five harmful creatures (al-fawasiq): rabid dog, scorpion, kite/crow, mouse/rat, and venomous snake
Camels and goats
Sparrows and hawks only
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ permitted killing five harmful pests—scorpion, crow/kite, rat, biting dog, and snake—even in Ihram or inside the Haram to protect human life.

questionEn: What spiritual purpose do the subtle Tasbih phrases woven black-on-black into the Kiswah silk serve?
optionsEn: To trace trade routes to Yemen
To record the genealogy of Quraysh
To remind pilgrims of continuous Dhikr and pure monotheism while circling the Kaaba
To teach rules of grammar
explanationEn: Every aspect of the Kiswah—both its subtle woven black-on-black Tasbih and its golden Qur'anic verses—elevates the worshiper's heart in remembrance of Allah.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Which Surah begins with Allah swearing by 'this secure city (wa hadhal-baladil-amin)'—referring directly to Makkah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Asr (103:1)
Surah Al-Falaq (113:1)
Surah Al-Kawthar (108:1)
Surah Al-Tin (95:3)
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Tin (95:1-3), Allah swears by the fig, the olive, Mount Sinai, and 'this secure city'—Makkah al-Mukarramah.

questionEn: For how long was fighting made lawful inside Makkah for the Prophet ﷺ on the Day of Conquest, before its permanent sanctity resumed?
optionsEn: Only for a brief hour of a single daytime, after which the Prophet ﷺ declared it sacred until the Day of Resurrection
For one hundred years
For three months
For seven years
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ declared: 'It was never made lawful for anyone before me, nor will it be lawful for anyone after me; it was only made lawful for me for an hour of a day, and now it has returned to its sacredness.'

questionEn: How many circuits did the Prophet ﷺ perform in every single Tawaf—whether arrival, Ifadah, Wada', or Umrah?
optionsEn: Three
Seven
Five
Twelve
explanationEn: Every valid Tawaf around the Kaaba consists of exactly seven continuous anti-clockwise circuits starting and ending at the Black Stone line.

questionEn: Is kissing one's own hand after gesturing toward the Black Stone from afar established in the Sunnah?
optionsEn: Yes, every scholar mandates kissing one's hand
Yes, three times per lap
No—scholars clarify there is no authentic evidence for kissing one's own hand after gesturing from afar; kissing applies only when one actually touches or kisses the Stone itself
Only if wearing gloves
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ kissed his staff only because the staff itself touched the Black Stone; when simply pointing from a distance, one says 'Allahu Akbar' without kissing one's palm.

questionEn: How can a believer honor a deceased Muslim relative through pilgrimage to the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Only children under five can do it
Pilgrimage can never benefit the deceased
Only by doing Tawaf al-Wada' for them
By performing a complete Umrah or Hajj on their behalf (provided one has already completed one's own)
explanationEn: Performing a full Umrah or Hajj for a deceased parent or relative (after completing one's own) is clearly established in authentic hadith.
