questionEn: What does the Prophet ﷺ equate a completed seven-circuit Tawaf followed by two rak'ahs of prayer to in reward in Sunan Ibn Majah?
optionsEn: Freeing a slave
Building a palace
Fasting one day
Visiting Taif
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that completing seven circuits and praying two rak'ahs equals the reward of freeing a slave.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ tell Aishah (RA) that Tawaf, Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, and stoning the Jamarat were instituted?
optionsEn: For athletic exercise
Solely to establish the remembrance of Allah (iqamati dhikriLlah)
To compete in speed
To memorize poetry
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Tawaf around the House, between Safa and Marwah, and stoning the Jamarat were legislated only to establish the remembrance of Allah.'

questionEn: What happens if someone walks around the Kaaba solely as a shortcut to reach an exit gate without intending Tawaf?
optionsEn: It automatically counts as Tawaf
It counts as half a Tawaf
It does not count as worship (Tawaf), because acts of worship require niyyah (intention)
It invalidates their prayer
explanationEn: Based on 'Actions are judged by intentions' (Bukhari 1), walking around the Mataf without intending Tawaf does not constitute a valid circuit.

questionEn: Why did Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) add a second ground-level door on the western wall of the Kaaba when he rebuilt it?
optionsEn: To hide from guards
To store chariots inside
To face Mount Safa from both sides
So pilgrims could enter through the eastern door and exit smoothly through the western door, fulfilling the Prophet's ﷺ wish to Aishah (RA)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ had told Aishah (RA) he wished the Kaaba had two ground-level doors—one for entry and one for exit—so Ibn al-Zubayr built both in 65 AH.

questionEn: How is the curved semi-circular wall of Hijr Ismail finished visually today?
optionsEn: Clad in polished white/beige marble topped with stone coping and decorative lanterns
Covered in black velvet
Built of raw timber
Painted bright blue
explanationEn: The Hatim wall is clad in polished marble capped with stone coping and illuminated pedestals so pilgrims can clearly distinguish its boundary day and night.

questionEn: What did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) build above Makkah to protect the Kaaba from seasonal mountain torrents?
optionsEn: A wooden bridge over Safa
Sadd Umar (a stone embankment dam) in the upper valley to divert floodwaters away from the sanctuary
A wall around Jeddah
A moat around Mount Hira
explanationEn: After the devastating 'Umm Nahshal' flood carried Maqam Ibrahim downstream, Umar (RA) ordered an embankment (Radm/Sadd Umar) constructed up-valley to shield Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Which famous historic flood during Umar ibn al-Khattab's (RA) caliphate swept Maqam Ibrahim down the valley, prompting Umar to hurry from Madinah to restore it?
optionsEn: Sayl al-Arim
The Flood of 1941
Sayl Umm Nahshal
The Flood of Tabuk
explanationEn: Known as Sayl Umm Nahshal, this torrent swept Maqam Ibrahim down toward lower Makkah; Umar (RA) hurried from Madinah, consulted witnesses who knew its spot, and fixed it back securely.

questionEn: Which Surah states that Allah made the Kaaba, the Sacred Month, the sacrificial animals, and the garlands as means of stability for people?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Inshiqaq 84:1
Surah Al-Mulk 67:5
Surah Al-Qalam 68:1
Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:97
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:97) explicitly unites the sanctity of the Kaaba, the Sacred Months, and the sacrificial offerings (hady) as pillars of peace and spiritual stability.

questionEn: Why does the Qur'an mention 'the garlands' (al-qala'id) alongside the Kaaba in Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:2 and 5:97)?
optionsEn: Pilgrims marked sacrificial animals (hady) bound for the Haram with distinctive neck garlands so bandits would recognize their sanctity and leave them unharmed
They were flower necklaces for kings
They were gold coins hung on Maqam Ibrahim
They were bracelets worn in Ihram
explanationEn: Placing a garland or mark around sacrificial animals bound for Makkah signaled they belonged to Allah's sanctuary, ensuring safe passage even among hostile tribes.

questionEn: What does 'their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House' in Surah Al-Hajj (22:33) mean in Islamic jurisprudence?
optionsEn: Sacrificing animals right inside Hijr Ismail
Sacrificing within the sacred Haram boundaries surrounding the Kaaba (such as Mina and Makkah), not outside the Haram
Sacrificing inside the Kaaba chamber
Sacrificing in Jeddah port
explanationEn: Jurists explain 'Al-Bayt al-Atiq' here encompasses the entire Haram sanctuary of Makkah (including Mina), where sacrificial animals for Hajj and fidyah must be slaughtered and distributed to the poor.

questionEn: What moved the companions deeply when the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah for Umrah al-Qada' in 7 AH with Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) leading his camel?
optionsEn: They fought Quraysh at Safa
They entered silently at midnight
Abdullah ibn Rawahah recited verses declaring 'There is no deity except Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise and aided His servant'
They brought 10,000 horses
explanationEn: Walking ahead of the Prophet's ﷺ she-camel, Abdullah ibn Rawahah (RA) chanted verses celebrating Islam's triumph until the Prophet ﷺ gently told him to say 'La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu...'.

questionEn: How does a Muslim fulfill the command in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:144) 'Turn your face toward Al-Masjid al-Haram' when praying thousands of miles away from Makkah?
optionsEn: By facing Madinah
Only prayers inside Makkah are valid
By facing east regardless of country
By facing the general direction (jihah) of the Kaaba in Makkah
explanationEn: Scholars distinguish between those inside Al-Masjid al-Haram who see the Kaaba (facing its exact structure, 'ayn al-Ka'bah) and distant Muslims worldwide (facing its direction, jihah).

questionEn: Who was the famous Makkah-born jurist and Tabi'i scholar, a student of Ibn Abbas (RA), who taught circles inside Al-Masjid al-Haram for decades and was relied upon by Caliphs for Hajj rulings?
optionsEn: Ata ibn Abi Rabah
Abu Yusuf
Al-Bukhari
Ibn Taymiyyah
explanationEn: Imam Ata ibn Abi Rabah (d. 114 AH), a former slave who became the undisputed Mufti of Makkah, held his famed teaching circle inside Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Which great Sunni Imam grew up in Makkah after moving there as a child from Gaza and studied inside Al-Masjid al-Haram under Muslim ibn Khalid al-Zanji?
optionsEn: Imam Abu Hanifah
Imam Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i
Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal
Imam Al-Awza'i
explanationEn: Imam al-Shafi'i (d. 204 AH) memorized the Qur'an by age seven in Makkah, studied with the Mufti of Makkah inside Al-Haram, and earned permission to issue fatwas at a young age.

questionEn: Which young governor of Makkah appointed by the Prophet ﷺ at roughly age 20 governed the sacred city after the Conquest?
optionsEn: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib
Usamah ibn Zayd (RA)
Attab ibn Asid (RA)
Ibn Umar (RA)
explanationEn: Attab ibn Asid (RA) of Banu Umayyah accepted Islam at the Conquest and proved so upright that the Prophet ﷺ entrusted Makkah's administration to him.

questionEn: Whom did the Prophet ﷺ name as the first person to introduce idol worship to Makkah and alter the pure religion of Ibrahim (AS)?
optionsEn: Abraha al-Ashram
Qusayy ibn Kilab
Jurhum ibn Qahtan
Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i
explanationEn: In an authentic narration, the Prophet ﷺ stated he saw Amr ibn Luhayy in the Fire because he first brought idols like Hubal to Makkah and instituted pagan superstitions.

questionEn: How is the flat roof of the Kaaba accessed from inside the Sacred House?
optionsEn: Through the enclosed interior stairwell Bab al-Tawbah leading up to a small roof hatch
Through four glass skylights
Through vents under Maqam Ibrahim
Through ladders outside the Black Stone
explanationEn: With no windows in its granite walls, the Kaaba interior is accessed via Bab al-Ka'bah and connected to the roof solely through the small roof hatch atop the Bab al-Tawbah stairs.

questionEn: What marks the spot inside the Kaaba floor where the Prophet ﷺ placed his forehead in sujud on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: A silver carpet
A distinct inlaid marble panel between the two forward teak pillars
A wooden platform
A bronze fountain
explanationEn: Inside the Kaaba floor, a distinctive inlaid marble slab marks the spot between the two forward teak pillars where Bilal (RA) saw the Prophet ﷺ pray.

questionEn: Why should pilgrims performing Tawaf avoid holding onto the Kiswah or climbing onto Al-Shadhirwan?
optionsEn: The marble breaks immediately
Cameras are banned everywhere in Saudi Arabia
It damages the silk embroidery, obstructs moving lanes, and stepping onto Al-Shadhirwan compromises that section of the Tawaf circuit
It blocks Safa
explanationEn: Respecting the sanctity of Baitullah means preserving its Kiswah, keeping Mataf lanes flowing safely, and keeping both feet outside Al-Shadhirwan during Tawaf.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What is 'Tawaf al-Qudum' around the Holy Kaaba?
optionsEn: Tawaf performed only in Safar
The final Tawaf before leaving Makkah
Tawaf performed during an eclipse
The Sunnah arrival Tawaf performed by non-resident pilgrims entering Makkah for Hajj Ifrad or Qiran
explanationEn: Pilgrims arriving from afar for Hajj Ifrad or Qiran perform Tawaf al-Qudum as a greeting to the House of Allah (whereas Tamattu' pilgrims perform their Umrah Tawaf upon arrival).

questionEn: Can a Muslim who enters Al-Masjid al-Haram solely to pray Salah (not intending Tawaf) pray two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid instead of doing Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes; while Tawaf serves as the greeting for one intending Tawaf, praying two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid is valid for residents or visitors entering simply for Salah
No, praying Salah without Tawaf is invalid
They must sit immediately without praying
They must pray outside the gate
explanationEn: Jurists clarify that Tawaf is the premier greeting of Al-Masjid al-Haram for newcomers and those intending Tawaf, while locals or travelers entering just for prayer may pray two rak'ahs of Tahiyyat al-Masjid.

questionEn: What spiritual warning did Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) derive from Surah Al-Hajj (22:25) for residents and visitors in Makkah?
optionsEn: Residents are exempt from prayer
Good deeds are multiplied in Makkah, and evil deeds are also grave in weight there due to the sanctity of the place
Only strangers face accountability
Speech is forbidden in Makkah
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Abbas and Ibn Mas'ud (RA) warned pilgrims to guard their tongues, temper, and dealings in Makkah because sinning inside the Haram violates Allah's Sacred Territory.

questionEn: If a pilgrim touches only the silver bezel framing Al-Hajar al-Aswad instead of the recessed black fragments inside, did they touch the Black Stone?
optionsEn: Yes, the entire Kiswah is the Black Stone
Yes, the silver frame is the Black Stone
No—the silver frame protects the fragments; to touch the Black Stone itself, one must touch the dark stone fragments inside the frame
The stone is invisible
explanationEn: Many visitors mistakenly kiss the metal silver rim thinking it is the Black Stone; the stone fragments sit recessed in the dark center of the silver bezel.

questionEn: Which side of the Kaaba sits closest to the Safa and Marwah corridor (Al-Mas'a)?
optionsEn: The western side
The roof
The northern side
The eastern/southeastern side (past Maqam Ibrahim toward Bab al-Safa)
explanationEn: Exiting the Mataf on the eastern side near Al-Hajar al-Aswad and Maqam Ibrahim leads directly through the Safa colonnade onto Mount Safa to begin Sa'i.

questionEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:196), what does Allah command regarding Hajj and Umrah once a believer enters Ihram for them?
optionsEn: 'And complete the Hajj and Umrah for Allah'
'Leave whenever tired'
'Perform only Tawaf and omit Sa'i'
'Perform them only in winter'
explanationEn: Once a Muslim enters Ihram for Hajj or Umrah, Allah commands completing all its rites sincerely for Him, unlike voluntary prayers which may be exited.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ promise regarding a person who performs Hajj without obscenity or transgression?
optionsEn: Only their financial debts are canceled
They return as pure from sin as the day their mother bore them
They forget their native language
They receive a title in Makkah
explanationEn: This famous hadith underscores the transformative spiritual rebirth granted to a pilgrim who guards manners and sincerity at the House of Allah.

questionEn: What is the approximate vertical length of each Kiswah wall panel?
optionsEn: 50 meters tall
Only 2 meters tall
Roughly 14 meters high, matching the full height of the Kaaba walls from parapet to Shadhirwan
50 cm tall
explanationEn: Each vertical breadth of black silk measures around 14 meters in height so the Kaaba is draped seamlessly from top parapet down to the Shadhirwan rings.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: How do specialists hoist and install the new 14-meter-tall Kiswah curtains onto the Kaaba without leaving the House bare?
optionsEn: Using bamboo ladders
By helicopters
By climbing on each other's shoulders
Using hydraulic lifts/cranes alongside roof attendants who lower each old curtain simultaneously as the new side is raised
explanationEn: Trained specialists use modern hydraulic cranes and roof pulleys to lift each heavy embroidered curtain smoothly while the old side is lowered simultaneously, so the Kaaba is never left bare.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What sits wrapped around the lower base of the Maqam Ibrahim stone inside its crystal enclosure?
optionsEn: A historical protective silver-and-gold collar fitted around the stone's lower portion to reinforce it
A modern speaker
A Zamzam tap
A candle holder
explanationEn: Visible inside the glass enclosure, a fitted metal collar cradles the lower stone of Maqam Ibrahim—a preservation method dating back centuries.

questionEn: Where must a pilgrim stand relative to Maqam Ibrahim and the Kaaba when praying the two post-Tawaf rak'ahs behind the Maqam?
optionsEn: Stand with your back to the Kaaba facing Maqam Ibrahim
Stand so that Maqam Ibrahim is between you and the Kaaba (facing the Kaaba with the Maqam ahead of you)
Stand on top of the Maqam base
Face away toward Jeddah
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ example, pilgrims position Maqam Ibrahim directly between themselves and the Kaaba—facing the Kaaba, never facing away from it.

questionEn: Which two corners of the Kaaba sit at the eastern and western ends of Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: Al-Hajar al-Aswad and Rukn al-Yamani
Only Bab al-Ka'bah
Al-Rukn al-Iraqi (east end of Hijr) and Al-Rukn al-Shami (west end of Hijr)
Maqam Ibrahim and Safa
explanationEn: Looking at the northwestern face of the Kaaba, Hijr Ismail curves between the northern corner (Rukn al-Iraqi) and the western corner (Rukn al-Shami).

questionEn: Why is 'Al-Rukn al-Iraqi' named after Iraq?
optionsEn: It uses stone imported from Baghdad
It faces the Euphrates dam
It was built by an Iraqi architect in 1950
It points geographically northeast toward the land of Iraq
explanationEn: Just as Rukn al-Shami faces Sham (Syria/Levant) and Rukn al-Yamani faces Yemen, Rukn al-Iraqi was named by Arab geographers and Makkans because it points northeast toward Iraq.

questionEn: Why did every major Quraysh clan accept the Prophet's ﷺ cloak solution when replacing the Black Stone in 605 CE?
optionsEn: Because each clan's representative held an edge of the cloak and shared equally in lifting the sacred stone to the wall
Because he paid them in gold
Because he let them build four doors
Because he excluded Banu Hashim
explanationEn: By turning rivalry into shared honor—and personally setting the stone into the wall—the 35-year-old Muhammad ﷺ averted a devastating clan war in Makkah.

questionEn: Which steadfast companion was counseled by his mother Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) near the Kaaba during Al-Hajjaj's siege in 73 AH?
optionsEn: Imam Malik
Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA)
Abu Hurayrah (RA)
Bilal (RA)
explanationEn: In 73 AH, aged and blind Asma bint Abi Bakr (RA) famously counseled her son Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) near the Kaaba: 'A slaughtered sheep feels no pain when skinned,' inspiring his steadfastness.

questionEn: What did the Prophet's ﷺ prophecy say will happen to the Kaaba near the very end of time after believers have passed away?
optionsEn: It will sink into Zamzam
It will fly to Madinah
An Abyssinian man with thin shanks (Dhul-Suwayqatayn) will dismantle the Kaaba stone by stone
It will turn into crystal
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ foretold that at the very end of time—after the believers have passed away—Dhul-Suwayqatayn from Abyssinia will tear down the Kaaba stone by stone.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim regard rainwater falling off Mizab al-Rahmah into Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: Avoid touching rainwater completely
Believe it cures blindness automatically by hadith
Consider it Zamzam water
Welcome rain as a general blessing ('ma'an mubarakan' in Qur'an 50:9) and a blessed time for dua, without attributing unverified charms to the spout
explanationEn: Rain is described in the Qur'an as blessed water, and making dua while rain falls in Al-Haram is cherished, while avoiding unverified exaggerations.

questionEn: Which exterior elements of the Kaaba remain uncovered by the black silk Kiswah?
optionsEn: Al-Hajar al-Aswad, the exposed corner of Rukn al-Yamani, the golden Door, the Shadhirwan plinth, and Mizab al-Rahmah
Only the Black Stone
The entire northern wall
All four corners equally
explanationEn: While the stone masonry of all four walls is draped in silk, the Black Stone, Rukn al-Yamani corner stone, the gilded door, the marble Shadhirwan base, and the Mizab spout remain visible.

questionEn: How did Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) compare the sanctity of the Kaaba to that of a believing human being?
optionsEn: The Kaaba is far greater than all believers combined
Looking at the Kaaba, he exclaimed: 'How great you are and how great is your sanctity! Yet the believer is more sacred to Allah than you!'
The Kaaba has no sanctity compared to trees
Only gold gives the Kaaba sanctity
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) gazed at the Kaaba and reminded the Ummah that even higher than the sacredness of Allah's House is the inviolability of a believer's blood, honor, and property.

questionEn: Which landmark does the elevated golden Door of the Kaaba face directly across the eastern Mataf?
optionsEn: Mount Thawr
Rukn al-Shami
Maqam Ibrahim
Jannat al-Mu'alla
explanationEn: The Kaaba's entrance faces northeast into the eastern Mataf directly toward Maqam Ibrahim.

questionEn: Which two corners are meant by Ibn Umar's (RA) statement 'I never saw the Prophet ﷺ touch anything of the House except the two Yemeni corners'?
optionsEn: Al-Rukn al-Iraqi and Al-Rukn al-Shami
Hijr Ismail and Maqam Ibrahim
Bab al-Safa and Bab al-Fath
Al-Hajar al-Aswad and Al-Rukn al-Yamani
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) referred to the eastern corner (Black Stone) and the southern corner (Rukn al-Yamani), the two corners resting on Ibrahim's (AS) original foundations.

questionEn: How do pilgrims performing Tawaf on the upper floors or roof accurately track the Black Stone starting line?
optionsEn: By aligning with the green marker light on the mosque wall facing the Black Stone corner
By guessing after 10 minutes
By counting pillars randomly
By asking a shopkeeper
explanationEn: Bright green indicator lights are aligned on the upper levels too, allowing wheelchair users and walkers on every tier to track the exact start and completion of each circuit.

questionEn: Why does Haram security temporarily regulate or cordon off entry into Hijr Ismail during peak Hajj days?
optionsEn: Because it is closed permanently in Islam
To protect crowd safety and prevent bottlenecks inside the narrow semi-circular space during peak Mataf density
Because it is flooded year-round
Because only custodians enter
explanationEn: During intense crowd peaks, Haram security temporarily regulates entry into Hijr Ismail to prevent dangerous trampling while keeping the outer Mataf flowing smoothly.

questionEn: According to Sahih Muslim (166), which valley did the Prophet ﷺ pass through while mentioning that seventy prophets passed that way performing Hajj to the Ancient House?
optionsEn: The Nile Delta
Wadi Rum
Wadi al-Azraq (near Usfan on the Madinah-Makkah road)
The Jordan Valley
explanationEn: Authentic narrations in Sahih Muslim and Musnad Ahmad describe seventy prophets passing through Wadi al-Azraq / Usfan en route to perform Hajj at Al-Bayt al-Atiq.

questionEn: Which mountain pass between Makkah and Madinah did the Prophet ﷺ point out as the path where Prophet Yunus ibn Matta (AS) recited the Talbiyah?
optionsEn: Wadi Fatimah
Mount Sinai
Jabal Uhud
Thaniyyat Harsha / Wadi al-Azraq
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ pointed out Thaniyyat Harsha / Wadi al-Azraq between Makkah and Madinah where earlier prophets passed praising Allah on pilgrimage to the Sacred House.

questionEn: Why does Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:2) pair 'Al-Bayt al-Haram' with 'the Sacred Months'?
optionsEn: To teach pilgrims not to violate Allah's symbols (Sha'a'ir), nor attack pilgrims seeking Allah's bounty and pleasure at the Sacred House
To limit Makkah visits to only one week
To ban trade in Makkah
To forbid riding camels
explanationEn: Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:2) calls believers to revere Allah's sacred symbols—protecting peaceful pilgrims traveling to Al-Bayt al-Haram from hostility or aggression.

questionEn: What does 'Sha'a'irillah' (Symbols/Rites of Allah) signify when applied to Makkah landmarks like the Kaaba, Safa, and Marwah?
optionsEn: Tribal flags
Sacred signs and rituals appointed by Allah whose outward reverence reflects inner Taqwa (piety of the heart)
Decorative arches
Pre-Islamic poems
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj (22:32) states: 'Whoever honors the symbols of Allah (sha'a'irAllah)—indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.'

questionEn: How many heavy brass rings embedded into Al-Shadhirwan anchor the tension cords of the Kiswah?
optionsEn: Four rings, one per corner
None—it hangs loose
Over 50 heavy brass anchor rings spaced around the marble Shadhirwan
Two iron stakes
explanationEn: Embedded neatly into the sloped Shadhirwan plinth around the walls are dozens of brass/copper rings through which the Kiswah tension cords are laced tight.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What is the Arabic term for the metal anchor rings in Al-Shadhirwan that hold the Kiswah taut?
optionsEn: Mizab
Qanadil
Mihrab
Halaqat al-Shadhirwan
explanationEn: These sturdy metal rings embedded in Al-Shadhirwan keep the lower border of the Kiswah firmly anchored against wind and pilgrim brushing.

questionEn: How long does it typically take weavers, embroiderers, and calligraphers at the Makkah complex to craft ONE complete Kiswah?
optionsEn: Approximately 8 to 10 months of meticulous hand and loom craftsmanship
About two weeks
Ten years
Three days
explanationEn: From silk dyeing and jacquard weaving to hand-stitching 120 kg of gold and silver thread onto the Hizam, Sitara, and Samadiyyah panels, each Kiswah takes most of an entire Islamic year to complete.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What are the five main vertical components assembled on the Kaaba during the annual Kiswah change?
optionsEn: Ten roof domes
Four wall curtains (one for each face of the Kaaba) plus the Door Curtain (Al-Sitara)
Seven prayer mats
Three pillars
explanationEn: Each of the Kaaba's four faces receives a tailored silk curtain joined securely at the corners, topped off by suspending Al-Sitara over the elevated golden door.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Why does the Sitara curtain over Bab al-Ka'bah measure over six meters tall?
optionsEn: To hide Maqam Ibrahim
To touch the Mataf marble
Because the door stands 2.25 meters above the floor, so the Sitara drapes from the upper lintel down across the full double doors
To cover Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Measuring over 6 meters tall, the Sitara frames the entire elevated doorway from its upper lintel down to the threshold step.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What was the 'Mahmal' that historically accompanied the Kiswah caravan from Cairo or Damascus to Makkah?
optionsEn: A stone bridge
A warship in Jeddah
A silver lock
An empty, richly decorated ceremonial camel litter symbolizing state patronage of the Hajj caravan
explanationEn: The Mahmal was an ornate ceremonial palanquin riding ahead of the Egyptian or Syrian Hajj caravan carrying the Kiswah—later discontinued in the 1920s.

questionEn: Why did King Abdulaziz establish the first Makkah Kiswah workshop in Ajyad in 1346 AH (1927 CE)?
optionsEn: To ensure the Kiswah was crafted honorably right inside Makkah after interruptions in external shipments from Egypt
To export silk to Rome
To stop weaving black cloth
To replace marble with silk
explanationEn: Following diplomatic disruptions in the 1920s, King Abdulaziz established the Makkah Kiswah factory in 1927 so Makkah itself would weave the House's garment uninterruptedly.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: At roughly what angle does the marble plinth of Al-Shadhirwan slope outward from the lower Kaaba walls?
optionsEn: Completely vertical 90 degrees
At roughly 45 degrees slope around the three exterior base walls
Inverted inward
Curved into a dome
explanationEn: Sloping outward roughly 40–45 cm from the vertical wall face, Al-Shadhirwan protects the lower foundation masonry from water pooling.

questionEn: How do pilgrims enter and exit Hijr Ismail without climbing over its 1.3-meter marble wall?
optionsEn: Through an underground tunnel
By using wooden ladders
Through two open ~2.2-meter entryways left between the curved wall ends and the northern Kaaba corners
Via bridges from Safa
explanationEn: The two 2.2-meter openings at the Iraqi and Shami ends welcome worshipers to enter Hijr Ismail calmly for nafl Salah and dua.

questionEn: What must a pilgrim do if they realize mid-Tawaf that they accidentally walked through the inside of Hijr Ismail on one lap?
optionsEn: Abandon Umrah altogether
Count it as double
Sacrifice a camel
Go back outside Hijr Ismail and repeat that incomplete circuit properly
explanationEn: Because Hijr Ismail is part of the House, cutting through it fails to circumambulate the entire Kaaba; simply walking back around the outside corrects the incomplete lap.

questionEn: Which direction should a worshiper face when offering voluntary prayer inside Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: Face the main Kaaba stone wall inside the Hijr, offer brief nafl rak'ahs without blocking entrances, and exit gently
Pray facing outward toward Safa
Lie down to sleep for hours
Face the curved Hatim wall instead of the Kaaba
explanationEn: Inside Hijr Ismail, facing the main Kaaba wall ensures you face the structure directly while offering brief voluntary prayer in consideration of others waiting.

questionEn: Standing in front of Maqam Ibrahim facing the Door of the Kaaba, which corner stands at your RIGHT?
optionsEn: Al-Hajar al-Aswad
Al-Rukn al-Iraqi (northern corner)
Rukn al-Yamani
Bab al-Safa
explanationEn: Facing the northeastern Door wall, Al-Rukn al-Iraqi lies on the right side leading into Hijr Ismail, while Al-Hajar al-Aswad lies on the left.

questionEn: What is the approximate distance between Al-Hajar al-Aswad and the Door of the Kaaba (the span of Al-Multazam)?
optionsEn: About 50 centimeters
About 20 meters
About 2 meters
About 12 meters
explanationEn: Bab al-Ka'bah sits closer to the Black Stone corner than to the Iraqi corner, leaving a span of roughly two meters known as Al-Multazam.

questionEn: What Sunnah practice did Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As (RA) demonstrate at Al-Multazam when uncrowded?
optionsEn: He stood silent facing Safa
He climbed onto the roof
He leaned against Maqam Ibrahim instead
He placed his chest, face, forearms, and outstretched palms against the wall between the Stone and the Door while making dua
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Amr (RA) demonstrated this authentic Sunnah posture at Al-Multazam when uncrowded, clinging humbly to Allah's House in earnest supplication.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1899 & Sunan Ibn Majah 2962

questionEn: Which Qur'anic Surah mentions both 'this House' (the Kaaba) and the winter and summer trade caravans of Quraysh?
optionsEn: Surah Quraysh (106)
Surah Al-Qadr (97)
Surah Al-Zalzalah (99)
Surah Al-Humazah (104)
explanationEn: Surah Quraysh (106:1-4) reminds Quraysh that their safe winter caravans to Yemen and summer caravans to Syria were a blessing from 'the Lord of this House', who fed them against hunger and secured them from fear.

questionEn: What made Quraysh's merchant caravans uniquely safe from desert highwaymen across Arabia before Islam?
optionsEn: They hired Roman legions
Their status as guardians of Allah's Sacred House (the Kaaba) in Makkah earned them universal respect among Arab tribes
They traveled only underground
They carried no goods
explanationEn: Especially after Allah destroyed Abraha's army in the Year of the Elephant, Arab tribes revered Quraysh as custodians of the Sacred House, granting them safe passage—'Ilaf'.

questionEn: Where did Abraha's elephant 'Mahmud' kneel down and refuse to advance toward the Kaaba?
optionsEn: At Jeddah beach
Inside Hijr Ismail
At Al-Mughammas / Wadi Muhassar near the boundary entering Makkah's Haram
At Mount Uhud
explanationEn: Whenever directed toward Yemen, Syria, or East, Mahmud rose and ran; whenever turned toward Makkah's Sacred House, the elephant knelt down at Wadi Muhassar / Al-Mughammas until Allah sent the Ababil birds.

questionEn: What famous sentence did Abdul-Muttalib speak to Abraha when demanding back his 200 plundered camels?
optionsEn: 'Pay me in Yemeni silk'
'Take the Kaaba and keep the camels'
'Let us fight inside the Mataf'
'I am the lord (owner) of the camels, and the House has a Lord Who will protect it!'
explanationEn: Abdul-Muttalib's resolute faith—holding onto the Kaaba's door-ring in dua and trusting Allah to defend His own Sanctuary—remains an immortal episode in Makkan history.

questionEn: Who among the Prophet's ﷺ ancestors first held all six civic offices of Makkah around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Qusayy ibn Kilab
Abu Talib
Hamzah (RA)
Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
explanationEn: Qusayy ibn Kilab gathered scattered Quraysh clans into central Makkah around the Kaaba, earning the title Al-Mujammi' (the Uniter) and organizing Hijabah, Siqayah, Rifadah, Nadwah, Liwa, and Qiyadah.

questionEn: Which Quraysh clan retained the office of Al-Siqayah (providing water/Zamzam to pilgrims) into the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime and after the Conquest?
optionsEn: Banu Makhzum
Banu Hashim (specifically Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib RA)
Banu Taym
Banu Jumah
explanationEn: Al-Abbas (RA), the Prophet's ﷺ uncle, administered Siqayah; during the Farewell Hajj, the Prophet ﷺ drank from his cup, praised his family's service, and urged them to continue.

questionEn: What filled the historic stone and leather troughs (hiyad) near Zamzam before modern marble water dispensers?
optionsEn: Rose petals
Olive oil
Freshly drawn Zamzam water for pilgrims and animals around the sanctuary
Molten silver
explanationEn: Early chronicles describe leather cisterns (hiyad) filled manually by buckets from Zamzam for pilgrims and camels around the sanctuary.

questionEn: What does the Arabic word 'Hijr' in 'Hijr Ismail' literally signify?
optionsEn: A golden gate
A desert mountain
A river bend
A walled-off enclosure or sanctuary space (distinct from 'Hajar', which means stone)
explanationEn: In Arabic, Hijr (حِجْر) denotes a protected enclosure or boundary (like the crescent space adjoining the Kaaba), distinct from Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Black Stone).

questionEn: Which face of the Kaaba does a worshiper stand facing when making dua at Al-Multazam?
optionsEn: Directly facing the northeastern wall between the Black Stone and the Door
Facing away toward Safa
Facing toward Hijr Ismail
Facing north toward Madinah
explanationEn: At Al-Multazam, one stands directly facing the Kaaba wall—specifically the two-meter segment between Al-Hajar al-Aswad and Bab al-Ka'bah.

questionEn: Why did all four Umrahs of the Prophet ﷺ take place in the sacred month of Dhul-Qi'dah?
optionsEn: Because Makkah was closed in Ramadan
To demonstrate that Umrah is valid in the sacred months of Hajj—refuting pre-Islamic superstitions that forbade Umrah during Hajj months
Because camels rested in winter
Because Safa was flooded in Rajab
explanationEn: Pre-Islamic Arabs considered performing Umrah during the Hajj months one of the worst sins; by doing his Umrahs in Dhul-Qi'dah, the Prophet ﷺ decisively dismantled that superstition.

questionEn: During which Umrah was the Prophet ﷺ blocked by Quraysh at Al-Hudaybiyyah before reaching the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Umrah from Al-Ji'ranah in 8 AH
Umrah al-Qada' in 7 AH
His first intended Umrah in 6 AH
His Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH
explanationEn: In Dhul-Qi'dah 6 AH, Quraysh barred the Prophet ﷺ and 1,400 companions at Al-Hudaybiyyah; Allah still counted it among his Umrahs and sent down Surah Al-Fath calling the treaty a 'clear victory'.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say about the spiritual reward of performing Umrah specifically in the month of Ramadan?
optionsEn: 'Umrah in Ramadan equals fasting one day'
'Umrah in Ramadan is discouraged'
'Umrah in Ramadan requires no Tawaf'
'An Umrah in Ramadan equals Hajj (or Hajj with me) in reward'
explanationEn: In a famous hadith, the Prophet ﷺ comforted a woman who missed Hajj by saying: 'Perform Umrah in Ramadan, for it is equivalent to Hajj (or performing Hajj with me).'

questionEn: Does performing Umrah in Ramadan fulfill the once-in-a-lifetime Fard obligation of Hajj?
optionsEn: No—the hadith equates its spiritual reward, not its legal obligation; a capable Muslim still owes the Fard Hajj
Yes, it replaces Hajj completely
Only for people over 60
Only if repeated three times
explanationEn: Scholars unanimously agree that 'equals Hajj' refers to immense spiritual reward, just as Surah Al-Ikhlas equals one-third of the Qur'an in reward without replacing the rest of the Qur'an.

questionEn: Which verses from Surah Al-Baqarah describing Ibrahim's (AS) prayer for the House appear prominently on the Kiswah's golden Hizam belt?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:282 (the debt verse)
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125-128
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:60
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:222
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125–128—chronicling Maqam Ibrahim, purifying the House, and Ibrahim and Ismail raising its foundations—feature prominently in gold embroidery on the Kiswah belt.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) ask Allah in Surah Ibrahim (14:35) regarding Makkah and his descendants?
optionsEn: 'Let Quraysh rule Rome'
'Make this valley full of silver rivers'
'My Lord, make this city [Makkah] secure and keep me and my sons away from worshiping idols'
'Build a fortress of iron'
explanationEn: Surah Ibrahim (14:35) reveals that Ibrahim's supreme concern for Makkah was twofold: outward peace/security and inward protection from shirk (idolatry).

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Hajj (22:28) connect pilgrims' journeys to the Kaaba with worldly and spiritual benefits?
optionsEn: 'That they may build palaces'
'That they may avoid all trade'
'That they may stay in silence'
'That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days'
explanationEn: Surah Al-Hajj (22:28) encompasses both eternal spiritual rewards (forgiveness, closeness to Allah) and lawful worldly benefits (brotherhood, knowledge exchange, lawful trade).

questionEn: What is the Qur'anic ruling in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:198) on lawful trade or buying necessities during pilgrimage in Makkah?
optionsEn: Permissible ('There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord')
Strictly forbidden in the Qur'an
Permissible only after returning home
Permissible only on Wednesdays
explanationEn: When early Muslims felt hesitant about trading at Makkah's markets during Hajj, Allah revealed 2:198 permitting honest livelihood while prioritizing worship.

questionEn: Which direction must a pilgrim face inside Al-Masjid al-Haram when performing the two post-Tawaf rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim?
optionsEn: Facing Mount Safa
Directly toward the Kaaba (with Maqam Ibrahim between them and the Kaaba)
Facing King Fahd Gate
Facing any random direction
explanationEn: Standing behind Maqam Ibrahim means Maqam Ibrahim lies directly between the worshiper and the Kaaba—always facing toward the Sacred House.

questionEn: Where does Prophetic guidance advise praying the two post-Tawaf rak'ahs when the space immediately behind Maqam Ibrahim is densely crowded?
optionsEn: In the middle of the green light path
Right inside the tightest circle touching the Kiswah
Further back behind Maqam Ibrahim out of the circling crowd, or anywhere inside Al-Masjid al-Haram facing the Kaaba
Outside Makkah altogether
explanationEn: Stepping well clear of the active Mataf flow—either further back in line with Maqam Ibrahim or in the covered prayer halls—protects your concentration and everyone else's safety.

questionEn: What was the historic freestanding stone arch 'Bab Bani Shaybah' that stood inside the Mataf courtyard until the 1960s?
optionsEn: A tower over Zamzam
A bridge to Mina
A wall around Safa
An ornate ceremonial arch marking the ancient sanctuary entrance path near Maqam Ibrahim, later removed to widen the Mataf
explanationEn: Visible in classic early-20th-century photographs of Makkah, the ornate Bab Bani Shaybah arch stood near Maqam Ibrahim and the Zamzam pavilion until the First Saudi Expansion cleared the Mataf floor.

questionEn: Around which decade did King Abdulaziz unify congregational prayers in Al-Masjid al-Haram behind a single Imam?
optionsEn: In the mid-1920s (around 1343–1345 AH), ending separate madhhab congregations
In 700 CE
explanationEn: Shortly after entering Makkah in 1343 AH (1924/1925 CE), King Abdulaziz restored a single unified congregational Salah led by one Imam for all Muslims.

questionEn: What structure stood inside the Mataf courtyard directly over the Zamzam well until the 1960s (1383 AH)?
optionsEn: A palm grove
A two-story stone pavilion ('Qubbat Zamzam' / Zamzam building) housing the wellhead, later moved underground to dramatically expand the Mataf
A golden minaret
A royal library
explanationEn: Relocating Zamzam access underground into a basement drinking hall (and later pumping it to chilled dispensers) removed the bulky pavilion, allowing tens of thousands more pilgrims to perform Tawaf safely.

questionEn: Which corner of the Kaaba sits farthest from Mount Safa?
optionsEn: Al-Hajar al-Aswad
Al-Rukn al-Iraqi
Al-Rukn al-Shami (on the opposite western side)
Bab al-Ka'bah
explanationEn: Mount Safa lies to the southeast/east of the Kaaba, placing the western corner (Rukn al-Shami) opposite it.

questionEn: How do the dyed silk and gold-plated silver embroidery of the Kiswah withstand a full year of Makkan heat and rain?
optionsEn: They are covered in plastic
They are repainted weekly
They turn bright blue in summer
High-purity gold-plated silver wire and rigorously UV-tested dyed silk resist tarnishing and fading until replaced annually
explanationEn: Tested rigorously at the Kiswah factory for tensile strength, UV resistance, and weather durability, the dyed silk and gold-plated silver embroidery endure Makkah's harsh desert sun gracefully.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: What spiritual lesson did classical scholars draw from Ibrahim and Ismail (AS) begging 'Rabbana taqabbal minna' while building the Kaaba?
optionsEn: True righteousness combines noble effort with deep humility and hope for Allah's acceptance
Building with stone is disliked
Only builders pray
Words matter without action
explanationEn: Wuhayb ibn al-Ward wept when reading 2:127, marveling that the Friend of Allah building Allah's own House still anxiously prayed for acceptance.

questionEn: What does 'Tawaf' literally mean in Arabic?
optionsEn: Standing still in a corner
Circling or going around something repeatedly
Climbing a mountain
Reading aloud
explanationEn: From 'tafa/yatufu' (to circle around), Tawaf signifies orbiting the House of Allah in harmony with cosmic and angelic worship.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if their Wudu breaks in the middle of a 7-circuit Tawaf?
optionsEn: Wait until next year
Continue Tawaf without Wudu
Exit calmly, renew Wudu, and return to complete Tawaf (resuming from the interrupted circuit if brief, or restarting if prolonged)
Pay a fine immediately
explanationEn: If Wudu breaks mid-Tawaf, exit carefully, perform Wudu, and return; Hanbali and many contemporary scholars allow resuming from where one stopped (or starting that lap/Tawaf fresh if a long break occurred).

questionEn: Why is the Black Stone positioned at waist-to-chest height rather than flush with the ground?
optionsEn: To hide it behind Maqam Ibrahim
Because it floated upward
Because Quraysh put it on the roof first
So pilgrims can reach, touch, or kiss it comfortably without lying flat on the Mataf floor
explanationEn: Placed around 1.1–1.5 meters above the Mataf pavement, Al-Hajar al-Aswad rests at an ergonomic height for passing pilgrims.

questionEn: What holds the sacred key to Bab al-Ka'bah when carried by the senior custodian of Banu Shaybah?
optionsEn: A specially embroidered green and gold silk pouch crafted alongside the Kiswah
A plain wooden box
A leather saddlebag
A brass cylinder
explanationEn: Each year, the Kiswah factory also crafts an ornate embroidered green silk pouch bearing Qur'anic verses (including 4:58) to house the sacred key of the Kaaba.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Which two walls of the Kaaba meet at Al-Hajar al-Aswad?
optionsEn: The northwestern wall and southwestern wall
The northeastern wall (Door wall) and the southeastern wall
Only the Hijr Ismail walls
The roof and the floor
explanationEn: Al-Hajar al-Aswad sits at the eastern corner where the Door facade (northeast) meets the southeastern wall running toward Rukn al-Yamani.

questionEn: Which two walls of the Kaaba meet at Al-Rukn al-Yamani?
optionsEn: Hijr Ismail and Maqam Ibrahim
The northeastern wall and northwestern wall
The southeastern wall and the southwestern (rear) wall
Only the Door wall
explanationEn: Rukn al-Yamani forms the southern angle where the southeastern face meets the bare southwestern rear wall.

questionEn: How did Mizab al-Rahmah evolve from Quraysh's 605 CE rebuild to later Islamic eras?
optionsEn: It was built by Julius Caesar
It was carved out of ice
It was added only in 2010
Quraysh installed a wooden rain spout, and later Umayyad, Abbasid, and Ottoman rulers renewed and plated it in gold
explanationEn: Quraysh invented the roof spout when roofing the Kaaba in 605 CE; later Umayyad, Abbasid, and Ottoman rulers plated and renewed Mizab al-Rahmah in gold.

questionEn: What Islamic invocation is inscribed along the sides of the gilded Mizab al-Rahmah?
optionsEn: 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' along with historical dedication inscriptions
Only numbers
Names of Makkah gates
It is completely blank
explanationEn: The gilded Mizab carries 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim' and 'Ya Allah', preserving centuries of craftsmanship including Ottoman and modern restorations.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ explain the Day of Judgment testimony of the Black Stone?
optionsEn: It speaks Arabic every Friday today
Allah will grant it two eyes and a tongue on Judgment Day to bear truthful witness for everyone who touched it sincerely
It glows red at noon
It was carved by Suleiman (AS)
explanationEn: Tirmidhi (961) preserves the Prophetic promise that the Black Stone will be raised with sight and speech solely as a witness of truthful faith for sincere worshipers.

questionEn: What kind of base supports the crystal enclosure of Maqam Ibrahim on the Mataf floor today?
optionsEn: A wooden raft
A 10-meter pyramid
A compact octagonal stepped marble base raised slightly above the Mataf floor
A sunken pit
explanationEn: Maqam Ibrahim rests on a sleek octagonal marble plinth elevated slightly so pilgrims can spot the landmark easily from across the Mataf.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: Why do scholars advise pilgrims against tying threads, leaving notes, or wiping handkerchiefs on the Maqam Ibrahim enclosure?
optionsEn: Because only green ink is allowed
Because paper blocks the wind
Because cloth stains the brass
Because seeking blessing through superstitious innovations has no basis in the Sunnah; true blessing comes from Tawhid, Salah, Tawaf, and sincere dua to Allah
explanationEn: Islamic scholars teach pilgrims to follow pure prophetic worship—Salah, Tawaf, Dhikr, and dua—and avoid ungrounded superstitions like tying cloth scraps or rubbing barriers.

questionEn: How frequently is the interior of the Holy Kaaba ceremonially washed under current practice?
optionsEn: Once annually in Muharram (historically twice a year in Sha'ban and Muharram/Dhul-Hijjah)
Every single morning
Once every fifty years
Never since 1950
explanationEn: Historically washed twice yearly (in Muharram and Sha'ban), the ceremonial washing in recent years is held once annually in Muharram to keep interruptions to the crowded Mataf minimal.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: What does the small embroidered dedication panel (Ahda') on the Kiswah record?
optionsEn: A street address
That the Kiswah was crafted in Makkah al-Mukarramah under the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques
An emergency exit sign
A calendar of eclipses
explanationEn: Beneath the Sitara or on the dedication band, an embroidered panel records where and when the Kiswah was woven in Makkah al-Mukarramah.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: From which ancient Quraysh clan did the hereditary custodians Banu Shaybah descend?
optionsEn: Banu Ghifar
Banu Thaqif
Banu Abd al-Dar
Banu Sulaym
explanationEn: Qusayy gave the key (Hijabah) to his eldest son Abd al-Dar, whose branch Banu Shaybah (Uthman ibn Talhah and Shaybah ibn Uthman) faithfully preserved it into Islam.

questionEn: How did Shaybah ibn Uthman become united with his cousin Uthman ibn Talhah (RA) in faithful custodianship of the Kaaba?
optionsEn: He sold the key
He fled to Abyssinia
He stayed in Taif
He embraced Islam sincerely at the Battle of Hunayn when the Prophet ﷺ touched his chest, dispelling his grief and uniting Banu Shaybah in Islam
explanationEn: Shaybah ibn Uthman's sincere conversion at Hunayn united his branch permanently with Uthman ibn Talhah (RA), giving the custodian family its enduring name 'Banu Shaybah'.

questionEn: How long did Muslims in Madinah pray toward Bayt al-Maqdis before Allah revealed Surah Al-Baqarah (2:144) restoring the Qiblah to the Kaaba?
optionsEn: About 16 to 17 months after the Hijrah
Ten years
Three days
Forty years
explanationEn: After arriving in Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ prayed toward Jerusalem for 16–17 months while yearning toward Ibrahim's Kaaba, until Allah revealed 2:144 turning believers back toward Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ orient himself while praying in Makkah BEFORE the Hijrah so as to face both the Kaaba and Jerusalem?
optionsEn: He faced west only
He stood south of the Kaaba near Rukn al-Yamani facing north, placing the Kaaba directly between himself and Bayt al-Maqdis
He prayed inside Cave Thawr
He prayed facing Yemen
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ positioned himself facing Rukn al-Yamani and the southern wall so both the Kaaba and Jerusalem lay straight ahead.

questionEn: How did Allah reassure the companions in 2:143 regarding Muslims who died before the Qiblah changed back to Makkah?
optionsEn: They had to be prayed over again
Their prayers were lost
'And never would Allah have caused you to lose your faith [meaning your earlier prayers toward Jerusalem]'
Only fasting counted
explanationEn: In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:143), Allah lovingly comforted the community that 'iman' (referring to their earlier Salah toward Bayt al-Maqdis) was completely accepted and rewarded.

questionEn: Why are non-Muslims prohibited from entering the Haram boundary of Makkah under Islamic law (Surah At-Tawbah 9:28)?
optionsEn: Only during Ramadan
Because hotels lack space
Because of ancient visa fees
Because Makkah's Sacred Sanctuary is reserved exclusively for worshipers of the One True God (Tawhid) following Allah's Qur'anic decree in 9 AH
explanationEn: Revealed in 9 AH, Surah At-Tawbah (9:28) commanded that polytheists no longer approach Al-Masjid al-Haram after that year, preserving Makkah as a pure sanctuary of monotheistic worship.

questionEn: How did Allah answer Makkans who feared economic loss when polytheists were barred from entering the Haram in 9:28?
optionsEn: 'And if you fear poverty, Allah will enrich you out of His bounty if He wills'
'Stop all markets permanently'
'Move Makkah to Yemen'
'Ask Rome for loans'
explanationEn: Allah promised to compensate Makkah with far greater lawful prosperity through Muslim pilgrims from all corners of the globe—a promise visibly fulfilled ever since.

questionEn: Why does Al-Masjid al-Haram remain open 24 hours a day, 365 days a year?
optionsEn: Because doors have no locks
Because Tawaf and Salah around the Kaaba never cease day or night, fulfilling Ibrahim's prayer for continuous devotion at Allah's House
Because lights cannot be turned off
Only during summer
explanationEn: By day and night without interruption—save brief congregational prayer pauses—believers continuously circle the Kaaba in living testimony to Surah 2:125.

questionEn: What classical saying attributed to Ibn Abbas (RA) illustrates the hierarchy of worship around the Kaaba?
optionsEn: That sleeping in the Mataf is best
That gazing outweighs Tawaf
That Allah sends 120 mercies daily upon the House: sixty for those doing Tawaf, forty for those praying, and twenty for those gazing upon it
That worship applies only on Fridays
explanationEn: While scholars note the specific numbering is an athar rather than a strong marfu' hadith, it vividly reflects why Tawaf ranks highest around the Kaaba, followed by Salah and loving contemplation.

questionEn: Which times of day generally offer calmer crowd flow and milder temperatures in the open Mataf outside peak Hajj/Ramadan rushes?
optionsEn: Only right after Friday Jumu'ah
Right at sunset rush
During Iqamah
Late night / pre-dawn hours before Fajr or mid-morning after Duha
explanationEn: While valid any hour, late night and mid-morning hours typically offer gentler temperatures and calmer space around Maqam Ibrahim and the Black Stone.

questionEn: What does the Talbiyah phrase 'Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik' chanted on the way to the Kaaba mean?
optionsEn: 'Here I am at Your service, O Allah, here I am! Here I am, You have no partner, here I am!'
'O Allah, guide me to Jeddah'
'Peace upon Mount Safa'
'Bless my caravan'
explanationEn: The Talbiyah is the pilgrim's ecstatic response to Ibrahim's ancient proclamation, declaring pure monotheism and readiness to obey Allah alone.

questionEn: What did the eyewitnesses summoned by Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr (RA) observe when digging down beneath Hijr Ismail?
optionsEn: Pink coral bricks
Huge greenish-gray foundation boulders interlocked tightly together like camel necks, laid by Ibrahim (AS)
White chalk
Painted terracotta
explanationEn: Eyewitnesses summoned by Ibn al-Zubayr (RA) marveled at ancient green-hued boulders locked solidly together, confirming Ibrahim's original foundation line.

questionEn: Which corners of the Kaaba receive NO specific istilam (touching or gesturing) during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Rukn al-Yamani
Al-Hajar al-Aswad
Al-Rukn al-Iraqi and Al-Rukn al-Shami
None—all four are kissed
explanationEn: Only Al-Hajar al-Aswad (kiss/touch/gesture + Takbir) and Rukn al-Yamani (touch if easy, without kissing) receive specific istilam; past the Iraqi and Shami corners one continues general Dhikr and dua.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim accidentally begins walking Tawaf from Maqam Ibrahim instead of aligning with Al-Hajar al-Aswad?
optionsEn: It invalidates their Ihram
It counts as two circuits
They cannot pray behind Maqam Ibrahim
The portion walked before reaching the Black Stone line does not count as the first circuit; counting begins properly from Al-Hajar al-Aswad
explanationEn: Because Al-Hajar al-Aswad is the mandatory starting and ending line of every circuit, starting past it means that initial partial walk isn't counted until passing the Black Stone line.

questionEn: How does a blind or visually impaired pilgrim perform Istilam during Tawaf?
optionsEn: Guided by a companion, they simply turn briefly toward the Black Stone direction, raise their right hand, and say 'Allahu Akbar'
They cannot perform Tawaf
They must touch all four walls
They must wait until midnight alone
explanationEn: Islam makes worship deeply accessible: accompanied visually impaired pilgrims follow the exact same Sunnah of gesturing and saying Takbir when aligned with the Black Stone line.

questionEn: Where are antique historic keys and locks of the Kaaba from Mamluk and Ottoman eras preserved today?
optionsEn: Buried under Mount Safa
In museums such as the Two Holy Mosques Exhibition in Makkah, Riyadh, and Topkapi Palace
Thrown into the Red Sea
Lost completely
explanationEn: Dozens of antique engraved keys gifted by Abbasid, Mamluk, and Ottoman rulers survive in collections, while the current key stays with Banu Shaybah.

questionEn: Which face and corner of the Kaaba catch Makkah's early morning sunrise first?
optionsEn: The southwestern rear wall
The western Shami corner
The eastern corner (Al-Hajar al-Aswad) and the northeastern Door facade
Inside Hijr Ismail only
explanationEn: Because Al-Hajar al-Aswad points East and Bab al-Ka'bah faces Northeast, the golden Door and Black Stone corner catch Makkah's early morning sunlight first.

questionEn: Which verse in Surah Al-Fath (48:24) is the only verse in the Qur'an spelling the city's name with an 'M' ('Makkah')?
optionsEn: Surah Quraysh 106:1
Surah Aal-Imran 3:96
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:125
'And it is He who withheld their hands from you and your hands from them within the valley of Makkah (bi-batni Makkah)'
explanationEn: While 3:96 uses 'Bakkah', Surah Al-Fath (48:24) is the unique Qur'anic verse spelling 'Makkah' explicitly, referring to the valley of Makkah / Hudaybiyyah peace.

questionEn: What does the phrase 'Batn Makkah' in Surah Al-Fath (48:24) describe geographically?
optionsEn: The low hollow valley basin of Makkah containing Al-Masjid al-Haram
The Red Sea coast
The peak of Taif
A cave in Madinah
explanationEn: Makkah sits in a low rocky basin ('batn'—hollow/valley floor) cradled by granite hills, with the Kaaba resting at its natural lowest focal point.

questionEn: Why did Allah withhold armed combat inside Makkah in Surah Al-Fath (48:25) during the Hudaybiyyah expedition?
optionsEn: Because Muslims had no horses
Out of mercy to hidden believing men and women inside Makkah whom Muslims did not recognize, lest they be harmed unknowingly
Because it was winter
Because Quraysh surrendered immediately
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fath (48:25) reveals Allah's tender mercy: hidden faithful Makkans lived silently in the city, so Allah withheld combat to protect their lives and lead to peaceful conquest two years later.

questionEn: What do the two terms 'Al-Mataf' and 'Al-Mas'a' refer to inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Al-Hijr and Al-Haram
Al-Miqat and Al-Mina
Al-Mataf is the circumambulation courtyard around the Kaaba, and Al-Mas'a is the corridor linking Safa and Marwah
Al-Sidanah and Al-Rifadah
explanationEn: Al-Mataf is the circumambulation courtyard surrounding the Kaaba, while Al-Mas'a is the corridor linking Mount Safa and Mount Marwah.

questionEn: How do the two green light markers inside Al-Masjid al-Haram differ in purpose?
optionsEn: Green lights mark Zamzam taps
They mark the exact same place
Green lights mark hotel exits
The single green light on the Mataf wall marks the Black Stone Tawaf line, while the twin green pillar zones in Al-Mas'a mark where men jog briskly between Safa and Marwah
explanationEn: Pilgrims should note two distinct green light markers: one single green light panel aligned with the Black Stone in the Mataf, and two green pillar zones marking Batn al-Wadi inside Al-Mas'a.

questionEn: Which face of the Kiswah does the heavy white cotton lining touch?
optionsEn: It faces inward directly against the granite walls of the Kaaba to buffer the heavy black silk exterior from abrasion
It faces outward toward pilgrims
It covers only the roof
It hangs inside Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Backing the heavy silk panels with breathable white cotton guards the fine silk fibers against rough stone masonry throughout the year.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Who assisted Prophet Ibrahim (AS) directly in raising the foundations and stone walls of the Kaaba according to Surah Al-Baqarah (2:127)?
optionsEn: His son Prophet Ishaq (AS)
His son Prophet Ismail (AS)
Prophet Musa (AS)
Prophet Dawud (AS)
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:127) honors both father and son: 'And [mention] when Ibrahim was raising the foundations of the House and [with him] Ismail.'

questionEn: What did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) leave behind on the stone of Maqam Ibrahim as an enduring physical sign?
optionsEn: His carved signature
A bronze statue
The clear impressions of both his feet—explicitly called 'clear signs' (ayat bayyinat) in Surah Aal-Imran 3:97
A water spring inside the stone
explanationEn: Surah Aal-Imran (3:97) cites Maqam Ibrahim as a visible sign of the prophetic heritage connecting Islam directly to Ibrahim (AS).

questionEn: Is reciting Surah Al-Kafirun and Surah Al-Ikhlas in the two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim obligatory or Sunnah?
optionsEn: No Qur'an is recited in those two rak'ahs
Strictly obligatory—any mistake voids Tawaf
Only Surah Al-Baqarah is valid
Recommended Sunnah—any other Qur'an surahs after Al-Fatihah also leave the prayer completely valid
explanationEn: While Surahs Al-Kafirun and Al-Ikhlas are the beautiful Sunnah affirming pure Tawhid, any Qur'anic passage after Al-Fatihah fulfills the two rak'ahs validly.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim genuinely forgets to pray the two Sunnah rak'ahs after Tawaf until reaching Mount Safa or later?
optionsEn: They may pray those two rak'ahs whenever they remember—even later or outside the Mataf—without repeating Tawaf
Their Tawaf is permanently invalid
They must repeat all seven circuits
They must sacrifice a camel
explanationEn: Even according to schools treating the two rak'ahs as wajib, praying them later upon remembering suffices without repeating Tawaf.

questionEn: Which two mosques are universally honored with the title 'Al-Haramayn al-Sharifayn' (The Two Noble Sanctuaries)?
optionsEn: Safa and Marwah
Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and Al-Masjid al-Nabawi in Madinah
Mount Hira and Mount Thawr
Arafat and Mina
explanationEn: Al-Haramayn al-Sharifayn refers universally to the Two Holy Mosques: Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah and Al-Masjid al-Nabawi in Madinah.

questionEn: How do classical scholars distinguish Al-Masjid al-Aqsa from Makkah and Madinah regarding the legal definition of a 'Haram'?
optionsEn: Only Jerusalem is a Haram
Jerusalem has the exact same Miqat boundaries
Only Makkah and Madinah are legal Harams with hunting/plant prohibitions, while Al-Masjid al-Aqsa is the Third Sacred Mosque ('Ula al-Qiblatayn')
Makkah is not a Haram
explanationEn: Al-Masjid al-Aqsa holds immense rank as one of the three mosques to which religious travel is legislated (Bukhari 1189), while Makkah and Madinah uniquely hold the strict legal Haram sanctuary rules.

questionEn: Why are harsh chemical detergents never used inside the Kaaba during the washing ceremony?
optionsEn: Because the floor is carpet
Because soap doesn't exist in Makkah
Because water evaporates instantly
Out of reverence for the House of Allah and to protect its historic marble and wood, using pure Zamzam water blended with natural rosewater and oud
explanationEn: Natural Zamzam water scented with Taif rosewater and oud leaves the marble radiant and fragrant while honoring prophetic modesty and stewardship.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: How does a pilgrim distinguish the Black Stone corner when performing Tawaf from a crowded upper-tier deck?
optionsEn: By spotting the green starting-line indicator light on the mosque wall, aligned directly with Al-Hajar al-Aswad
By looking for a red minaret
By counting 50 steps from Safa
There is no way to tell from upper floors
explanationEn: The green beacon on the outer wall aligns directly with the Black Stone corner, letting pilgrims on upper tiers and the roof accurately track every circuit.

questionEn: Which corner of the Kaaba sits immediately BEFORE Al-Hajar al-Aswad as you complete each counter-clockwise Tawaf lap?
optionsEn: Al-Rukn al-Iraqi
Al-Rukn al-Yamani (the southern corner)
Al-Rukn al-Shami
Maqam Ibrahim
explanationEn: Rounding Rukn al-Yamani puts you on the final straight stretch of each lap leading up to Al-Hajar al-Aswad—where the Prophet ﷺ recited 'Rabbana atina fi'd-dunya hasanah...'.

questionEn: How does Surah Al-Baqarah (2:200-201) contrast the misguided prayers of pre-Islamic pilgrims with true believers at the House of Allah?
optionsEn: One group prays silently
One group asks only for rain
Some ask only for worldly gains ('Our Lord, give us in this world'), whereas true believers ask for good in BOTH this world and the Hereafter and protection from the Fire
Both groups say identical words
explanationEn: Verses 2:200–201 rebuke purely materialistic pilgrimage prayers and elevate 'Rabbana atina fi'd-dunya hasanah...' as the balanced model for every believer.

questionEn: What protects the upper seams and corners of the heavy Kiswah curtains from tearing during hoisting and high winds?
optionsEn: Leather straps
Iron plates
Bamboo rods
Heavy reinforced seams and braided cotton edging secured around the upper parapet hooks
explanationEn: Reinforced hems along the top parapet anchor the heavy silk panels smoothly over the roof lip while braided corner seams handle wind tension.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: Why do Kiswah embroiderers alternate pure silver wire alongside gold-plated silver wire on the Sitara and Hizam?
optionsEn: To create rich visual contrast, floral depth, and border clarity
Because they run out of gold
To use aluminum scraps
To mark mistakes
explanationEn: Master embroiderers alternate pure bright silver thread with 24-karat gold-plated silver thread to create rich contrast across the Sitara and Hizam borders.
reference: King Abdulaziz Complex for the Kiswah

questionEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (1885), how did the Prophet ﷺ compare his prayer for Madinah's blessing to Ibrahim's (AS) earlier blessing for Makkah?
optionsEn: He asked Allah to remove blessings from Makkah
He asked Allah to place in Madinah TWICE the blessing (barakah) He had placed in Makkah
He compared Makkah to Egypt
He never prayed for either city
explanationEn: Honoring Ibrahim's (AS) earlier supplication for Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ prayed: 'O Allah, place in Madinah twice the blessing You placed in Makkah!'

questionEn: When Bilal (RA) recovered from fever shortly after the Hijrah, what features of Makkah did he long for in his famous poetry?
optionsEn: Poems about Yemen's castles
Poems about Damascus
Spending a night in Makkah's valley surrounded by fragrant Idhkhir and Jalil grasses and drinking the waters of Majannah
Songs about ships
explanationEn: Bilal's (RA) poignant verses yearning for Makkah's sweet Idhkhir grass and nearby springs moved the Prophet ﷺ to pray for Madinah's health and blessing.

questionEn: What spiritual responsibility does being 'neighbors of Allah's House' (residents of Makkah) carry according to classical scholars?
optionsEn: Permission to hunt inside the Haram
Exemption from Salah
Exemption from fasting
Heightened accountability to uphold righteousness, honesty, hospitality to Allah's guests, and reverence for the Haram
explanationEn: Scholars remind Makkah's residents and visitors alike that proximity to the House demands greater piety, honesty, and kindness to Allah's guests—not complacency.

questionEn: Why did early Muslims eagerly ask returning Hajj and Umrah pilgrims from Makkah to make dua for them?
optionsEn: Because Prophetic hadith teaches that Allah's pilgrim guests are answered in supplication and return purified when sincere
Because Makkans forbade dua inside the Haram
Because only travelers knew Arabic
Because it was required by law
explanationEn: Inspired by Prophetic narrations on the 'delegation of Allah', early Muslims eagerly asked returning Hajj and Umrah pilgrims to pray for them before they entered their homes.

questionEn: What architectural landmark stands directly in front of Bab al-Ka'bah roughly 10.5 meters away across the eastern Mataf?
optionsEn: Mount Marwah
Maqam Ibrahim
Bab al-Umrah
Jabal Thawr
explanationEn: Stepping out from Bab al-Ka'bah toward the eastern Mataf, Maqam Ibrahim stands directly ahead roughly 10.5 meters away.

questionEn: Roughly where beneath the Mataf floor is the historic Zamzam wellhead located relative to the Kaaba?
optionsEn: At the top of Jabal al-Noor
Inside Hijr Ismail
Roughly 20–21 meters east-southeast of the Black Stone corner, near Maqam Ibrahim
Outside King Fahd Gate
explanationEn: The covered subterranean wellhead of Zamzam lies beneath the marble floor roughly 20–21 meters east-southeast of the Black Stone corner, near Maqam Ibrahim.

questionEn: What principle did Shaybah ibn Uthman and Umar (RA) affirm regarding remaining gold or wealth stored inside the Kaaba's pit?
optionsEn: That it should be buried in Mina
That it should be melted into statues
That it should be thrown into the sea
That wealth donated to the House should benefit the needy in Allah's cause rather than sit hoarded idly
explanationEn: Narrations in Sunan Abi Dawud (2030) record Shaybah and Umar (RA) affirming that excess gold/silver in the Kaaba's interior pit should be distributed to the poor rather than hoarded.

questionEn: In which direction do the two tall golden leaves of Bab al-Ka'bah swing when unlocked by Banu Shaybah?
optionsEn: Inward into the Kaaba chamber, bridged to the Mataf floor by a wheeled staircase
Outward onto the Mataf
Sideways on sliding tracks
Upward toward the roof
explanationEn: Unlocked manually by the senior custodian of Banu Shaybah using the sacred key, the grand doors swing inward while a wheeled staircase bridges the 2.25m gap to the Mataf floor.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: How were pilgrims able to walk cleanly across the pre-modern pebble courtyard (Al-Hasba) of Al-Masjid al-Haram before full marble paving?
optionsEn: Wooden rafts floated on floodwater
Radial stone pathways led from the outer gates across the gravel toward Maqam Ibrahim and the Kaaba
Silk carpets covered the whole valley
Suspended bridges crossed overhead
explanationEn: Before the 20th-century Saudi expansions paved the entire courtyard in marble, radial stone pathways crossed the pebble-covered courtyard (Al-Hasba) so pilgrims wouldn't walk over hot gravel.

questionEn: What was the pebble-covered open courtyard of Al-Masjid al-Haram historically called before full marble paving?
optionsEn: Al-Hazwarah
Al-Mas'a
Al-Hasba (the pebble courtyard)
Al-Tan'eem
explanationEn: Covered in clean river pebbles brought from nearby valleys to prevent dust and mud, the open courtyard surrounding the stone walkways was long known as Al-Hasba.

questionEn: Which two prophets' names are permanently honored on 'Maqam Ibrahim' and 'Hijr Ismail' at the heart of Al-Mataf?
optionsEn: Nuh (AS) and Hud (AS)
Musa (AS) and Isa (AS)
Dawud (AS) and Sulayman (AS)
Father and son: Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and Prophet Ismail (AS)
explanationEn: Standing side by side at the heart of the Mataf, Maqam Ibrahim and Hijr Ismail preserve the living legacy of the two prophets who built the Sacred House together.

questionEn: What advantage do the second and third tiers of Al-Mataf offer elderly or heat-sensitive pilgrims during daytime Tawaf?
optionsEn: Covered shaded arcades, cooler air circulation, and dedicated wheelchair/cart lanes
Shorter distance than the ground floor
Direct access to touch the Black Stone
Only 3 circuits needed
explanationEn: Although upper-level Tawaf circuits are wider and take slightly longer per lap, shaded colonnades, fans, and uncrowded lanes make them ideal for elderly and heat-sensitive pilgrims.

questionEn: Why should a pilgrim performing Tawaf avoid halting abruptly in front of Al-Hajar al-Aswad for lengthy personal dua?
optionsEn: Because dua is invalid near the Black Stone
Because halting at the Black Stone bottlenecks thousands behind you; gesturing once in motion keeps everyone safe
Because you must sprint past it
Because it blocks Safa
explanationEn: Following the Prophet's ﷺ care for believers' safety, pilgrims keep the flow smooth at the eastern corner and save prolonged stationary dua for uncrowded areas.

questionEn: How thick are the granite masonry walls of the Holy Kaaba at their base?
optionsEn: About 10 centimeters
5 meters thick
Over 1 meter thick, tapering slightly upward
2 centimeters
explanationEn: Built of massive interlocking granite blocks and traditional lime-pozzolanic mortar, the Kaaba's thick load-bearing walls have withstood flash floods and centuries of desert climate.

questionEn: What rite does the Qur'anic phrase 'end their untidiness (tafasahum), fulfill their vows, and perform Tawaf around the Ancient House' (22:29) describe?
optionsEn: Fasting on Eid
Washing the Kiswah
Forbidding leaving Makkah
Exiting partial Ihram on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah (shaving/trimming, sacrificing) followed by Tawaf al-Ifadah at the Kaaba
explanationEn: Ending 'tafath' means trimming nails, shaving/cutting hair, and putting on clean clothes after stoning Jamrat al-Aqabah—culminating in Tawaf al-Ifadah around Al-Bayt al-Atiq.

questionEn: What miraculous memory did the Prophet ﷺ share in Sahih Muslim (2277) regarding a particular stone in Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Indeed I know a stone in Makkah that used to greet me with Salam before I was sent as a Prophet; I recognize it even now!'
That stones in Makkah floated in water
That Mount Arafat greeted him
That Safa turned to gold
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Samurah (RA) narrated in Sahih Muslim (2277) that the Prophet ﷺ fondly remembered a specific stone in a Makkan alley that greeted him with 'Al-Salamu alayka ya RasulAllah' before prophethood.

questionEn: Where did the stone that greeted the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah before revelation traditionally stand according to Makkan chroniclers?
optionsEn: Inside Hijr Ismail
Near the historic Zuqaq al-Hajar (Alley of the Stone) east of Al-Masjid al-Haram
On top of Mount Thawr
In Jeddah
explanationEn: Makkan chroniclers preserved the memory of Zuqaq al-Hajar (the Alley of the Stone) near the eastern side of the sanctuary as the neighborhood associated with that Prophetic miracle.

questionEn: Which two Makkah landmarks are paired in Jami at-Tirmidhi (878) as 'two rubies/jewels from the jewels of Paradise'?
optionsEn: Bab al-Safa and Bab al-Fath
Hijr Ismail and Mizab al-Rahmah
Al-Hajar al-Aswad (the Corner) and Maqam Ibrahim
Rukn al-Iraqi and Rukn al-Shami
explanationEn: Both the Black Stone and Maqam Ibrahim are heavenly-originated stones sent to earth during the building of Allah's House, honored in this Tirmidhi narration.

questionEn: After completing Tawaf al-Umrah and praying two rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, what did Jabir (RA) report the Prophet ﷺ did before heading to Mount Safa?
optionsEn: He left Al-Haram for Mina
He slept for three hours
He shaved his head immediately before Sa'i
He drank Zamzam water, returned briefly to touch the Black Stone, and walked out through Bab al-Safa for Sa'i
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) recorded that after praying the two rak'ahs at Maqam Ibrahim, the Prophet ﷺ drank Zamzam (and poured some over his head), briefly returned to touch the Black Stone, and walked out through Bab al-Safa for Sa'i.

questionEn: How does the Kaaba serve as a daily spiritual anchor even for Muslims who have not yet visited Makkah?
optionsEn: Every time a believer stands for the five daily prayers—or turns in dua or burial—their face and heart orient toward the Sacred House in Makkah
Only pilgrims face Makkah
It affects only Ramadan
It only applies on Fridays
explanationEn: From birth to burial, every Muslim worldwide faces the exact coordinates of the Holy Kaaba in Makkah at least five times a day, forging an unbreakable spiritual bond with Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: Who was the noble mother of Prophet Ismail (AS) whom Prophet Ibrahim (AS) settled with her infant son in the barren valley of Makkah by Allah's command?
optionsEn: Sarah (RA)
Hajar (RA)
Asiyah (RA)
Maryam (AS)
explanationEn: Following Allah's command, Prophet Ibrahim (AS) brought Hajar (RA) and their nursing infant Ismail (AS) to the uncultivated valley of Makkah beside the site of the Sacred House.

questionEn: What did Hajar (RA) ask Prophet Ibrahim (AS) three times as he turned to leave her and infant Ismail (AS) in Makkah's empty valley?
optionsEn: 'Where is the nearest market?'
'When will the next trade caravan arrive?'
'Has Allah commanded you to do this?'—and when he signaled yes, she replied, 'Then He will never abandon us!'
'Why did we not stay in Egypt?'
explanationEn: Hajar's (RA) unshakeable reliance upon Allah (Tawakkul)—'Idhan la yudayyi'una' (Then He will not neglect us)—became the spiritual foundation of the rites of Makkah.

questionEn: Where did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) pause and turn back toward the valley of the Kaaba—out of Hajar's sight—to raise his hands and recite the famous prayer of Surah Ibrahim (14:37)?
optionsEn: Inside Cave Thawr
On top of Mount Uhud
By the shore of the Red Sea
At the mountain pass of Al-Thaniyyah (Kada') overlooking Makkah
explanationEn: When Ibrahim (AS) reached the pass of Al-Thaniyyah where Hajar and Ismail could no longer see him, he faced the Sacred House and prayed 'Rabbana inni askantu min dhurriyyati...'.

questionEn: Under what kind of tree near the site of Zamzam did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) place Hajar (RA) and infant Ismail (AS) along with a leather bag of dates and a waterskin?
optionsEn: A large Dawhah (desert acacia/shrub tree) above the location of Zamzam
A tall cedar tree
An apple orchard
A bamboo grove
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that Ibrahim (AS) placed them beneath a large tree (dawhah) above the spot of Zamzam in the highest part of the mosque area when Makkah had neither inhabitants nor water.

questionEn: Why did Hajar (RA) climb Mount Safa first when her waterskin ran dry and infant Ismail (AS) began crying from thirst?
optionsEn: Because a bridge connected Safa to Syria
Because Mount Safa was the nearest hill to her, so she stood upon it hoping to spot any traveler or caravan in the valley
Because an idol stood there
Because she wanted to gather firewood
explanationEn: Finding Safa the closest hill to the tree, Hajar (RA) climbed it and scanned the horizon looking for any human presence before descending toward Marwah.

questionEn: Why did Hajar (RA) gather up her garment and run swiftly through the low valley floor (Batn al-Wadi) between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: Because it was raining heavily
Because wild lions chased her
Because descending into the dip hid infant Ismail (AS) from her view, so she hurried across until she could see him again from the rising slope
To race a passing caravan
explanationEn: In the low hollow of the valley bed, Hajar lost sight of her baby; out of maternal anxiety she ran briskly across that dip until ascending the opposite slope—instituting the Sunnah between the two green markers.

questionEn: How many times did Hajar (RA) go back and forth between Mount Safa and Mount Marwah searching for help?
optionsEn: Three times
Five times
Ten times
Seven times
explanationEn: Hajar (RA) traversed the distance between Safa and Marwah seven times; the Prophet ﷺ said: 'And that is why the people perform Sa'i between them.'

questionEn: On which hill was Hajar (RA) standing at the end of her seventh lap when she heard a voice and saw the angel at the site of Zamzam?
optionsEn: Mount Marwah
Mount Safa
Jabal al-Noor
Jabal Thawr
explanationEn: Starting Lap 1 at Safa and alternating seven times placed Hajar (RA) atop Mount Marwah at the finish of her seventh lap when she heard the angel near Ismail (AS).

questionEn: Who struck the earth beside infant Ismail (AS) with his heel or wing so that the water of Zamzam gushed forth?
optionsEn: A merchant from Yemen
Angel Jibril (AS)
King Tubba'
Qusayy ibn Kilab
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (3364), Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that Angel Jibril (AS) dug/struck the earth with his heel (or wing) until water burst forth at the spot of Zamzam.

questionEn: What did Hajar (RA) immediately do when she saw water bubbling out of the sand beside Ismail (AS), and what did the Prophet ﷺ say about her action?
optionsEn: She walked away to Syria
She covered it with stones so it stopped
She scooped sand around it like a basin saying 'Zumm! Zumm!'—and the Prophet ﷺ said: 'May Allah have mercy on the mother of Ismail! Had she left Zamzam alone, it would have been a flowing river!'
She built a wooden tower over it
explanationEn: Fearing the precious water would seep away into the desert sand, Hajar banked earth around it and scooped it into her waterskin; the Prophet ﷺ affectionately praised her while noting it would otherwise have flowed as a surface stream.

questionEn: What reassuring promise did Angel Jibril (AS) give Hajar (RA) beside the newly sprung well of Zamzam?
optionsEn: 'Wait for Roman soldiers'
'Leave Makkah before winter'
'Dig three more wells at Safa'
'Do not fear being neglected, for here is the House of Allah which this boy and his father will build, and Allah never abandons His people'
explanationEn: Jibril (AS) consoled Hajar (RA) with the glad tidings that infant Ismail and his father Ibrahim (AS) would raise the House of Allah right beside that blessed spring.

questionEn: How did the Arab tribe of Jurhum discover that water had miraculously appeared in the hitherto dry valley of Makkah?
optionsEn: They saw water-loving birds circling in the sky over the valley and realized birds only circle where water exists
They received a written letter
They heard thunder from Taif
They followed a river from the Red Sea
explanationEn: Camping at lower Makkah (Kada'), a clan of Jurhum noticed birds wheeling over the valley they knew to be bone-dry; their scout returned amazed to report the spring of Zamzam.

questionEn: What condition did Hajar (RA) stipulate when the tribe of Jurhum politely asked her permission to camp and settle around her at Zamzam?
