optionsEn: 'Pay a hundred gold coins monthly'
'Yes, you may settle here, but you shall have no ownership claim over the water itself'
'Leave after one week'
'Build a wall around Marwah'
explanationEn: Jurhum honorably sought Hajar's permission rather than seizing the well by force, and she welcomed their companionship while preserving the public/prophetic stewardship of Zamzam.

questionEn: What language did young Ismail (AS) learn from the tribe of Jurhum as he grew up around Zamzam in Makkah?
optionsEn: Greek
Aramaic
Pure Arabic
Coptic
explanationEn: Growing up among Jurhum in Makkah, Ismail (AS) mastered eloquent Arabic and married into their tribe when he came of age.

questionEn: In the famous account of Ibrahim's (AS) visits to Makkah to check on Ismail (AS), what figurative message did Ibrahim leave with Ismail's first wife vs his second wife?
optionsEn: He left them a bag of silver
He told both to move to Yemen
He asked them to dig another well
He told the ungrateful first wife 'Change the threshold of your door', and told the hospitable, grateful second wife 'Keep the threshold of your door firm'
explanationEn: The first wife complained about Makkah's hardship, while the second wife praised Allah and offered meat and Zamzam water, praying for their blessing—leading Ibrahim (AS) to bless Makkah with meat and water.

questionEn: What two staple provisions did Prophet Ibrahim (AS) specifically bless for Makkah when Ismail's second wife hospitably served them to him?
optionsEn: Meat and water
Wheat and barley
Apples and figs
Fish and rice
explanationEn: Because Makkah had no sown grain fields at that time, Ismail's wife served meat from Ismail's hunting and Zamzam water; Ibrahim (AS) prayed: 'O Allah, bless them in their meat and their water!'

questionEn: Why did the well of Zamzam disappear from sight for several centuries between the era of Jurhum and the time of Abdul-Muttalib?
optionsEn: An earthquake moved it to Taif
When Jurhum was expelled by Khuza'ah for violating Makkah's sanctity, their chief Mudad ibn Amr buried the treasures of the Kaaba inside Zamzam and leveled sand over it
The Romans sealed it with lead
It dried up for a thousand years
explanationEn: Before fleeing Makkah, Mudad ibn Amr of Jurhum buried the two golden gazelles and Qal'i swords in the Zamzam shaft and concealed its surface location so completely that generations forgot its exact spot.

questionEn: Who was guided by a series of four vivid dreams in Hijr Ismail to rediscover and re-excavate the long-lost well of Zamzam?
optionsEn: Waraqah ibn Nawfal
Abu Talib
Abdul-Muttalib ibn Hashim (grandfather of the Prophet ﷺ)
Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt
explanationEn: Sleeping in Hijr Ismail, Abdul-Muttalib was commanded in successive dreams to dig 'Taybah', 'Barrah', 'Al-Madnunah', and finally 'Zamzam'.

questionEn: What four names were spoken to Abdul-Muttalib in his four consecutive nights of dreams before he dug up Zamzam?
optionsEn: Bakkah, Umm al-Qura, Balad, and Haram
Safa, Marwah, Mina, and Arafat
Salsabil, Kawthar, Tasnim, and Furat
Taybah (the Pure), Barrah (the Pious/Beneficent), Al-Madnunah (the Precious/Treasured), and Zamzam
explanationEn: Each night's dream highlighted a noble attribute of the well—purity, goodness, preciousness—culminating on the fourth night with 'Dig Zamzam! It never runs dry nor is it ever disparaged; it waters the grand pilgrim congregation!'

questionEn: What descriptive signs were given to Abdul-Muttalib in his dream to pinpoint the exact buried spot of Zamzam inside the Mataf?
optionsEn: Between the dung and blood of sacrifices, at the pecking spot of the white-winged crow, by the ant-hill
On top of Mount Safa
Inside Dar al-Nadwah
At the gate of Jeddah
explanationEn: Going the next morning with his pickaxe, Abdul-Muttalib found the exact signs—an ant-hill and a white-marked crow pecking between the sacrificial spots near the idols Isaf and Na'ilah—and began digging.

questionEn: Which lone son of Abdul-Muttalib stood by his father to dig out Zamzam when Abdul-Muttalib did not yet have ten sons?
optionsEn: Abu Lahab
Al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib (his eldest son)
Hamzah (RA)
Al-Abbas (RA)
explanationEn: At the time of digging Zamzam, Abdul-Muttalib had only one son, Al-Harith, who stood beside him defending his father's work while Quraysh challenged him.

questionEn: What solemn vow did Abdul-Muttalib make when Quraysh elders challenged him while he had only his one son Al-Harith to back him at Zamzam?
optionsEn: He vowed to seal the well again
He vowed to leave Makkah
He vowed that if Allah granted him ten sons who grew up to protect him, he would sacrifice one of them at the Kaaba—a vow later ransomed with 100 camels for Abdullah
He vowed to build ten towers
explanationEn: Feeling vulnerable with only one son, Abdul-Muttalib vowed to sacrifice one son if blessed with ten; years later the lot fell on his beloved youngest son Abdullah (father of the Prophet ﷺ), who was ransomed with 100 camels.

questionEn: What ancient buried artifacts from the Jurhum era did Abdul-Muttalib uncover when his pickaxe struck the stone casing of Zamzam?
optionsEn: Scrolls of papyrus
Roman coins and glass
A silver boat
Two golden gazelles, Qal'i swords, and suits of armor
explanationEn: Upon uncovering the ancient stone rim of Ismail's well, Abdul-Muttalib shouted 'Allahu Akbar!' and found the two golden gazelles and swords buried centuries earlier by Jurhum.

questionEn: What did Abdul-Muttalib do with the Qal'i swords and the two golden gazelles he recovered from the Zamzam well?
optionsEn: He forged the iron swords into a door for the Kaaba and plated the door with the two golden gazelles
He sold them in Syria
He threw them back into the well
He gave them to Abraha
explanationEn: Rather than keeping the treasure for himself, Abdul-Muttalib honored the House of Allah by fashioning the swords into a Kaaba door adorned with the golden gazelles.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ famously declare about the spiritual and physical efficacy of Zamzam water?
optionsEn: 'Zamzam may only be drunk in winter'
'The water of Zamzam is for whatever purpose it is drunk for' (Ma'u Zamzama lima shuriba lah)
'Zamzam is only for washing hands'
'Zamzam loses its blessing after noon'
explanationEn: Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) in Sunan Ibn Majah and Musnad Ahmad, the Prophet ﷺ taught that drinking Zamzam with sincere intention and dua—for healing, knowledge, faith, or relief—is answered by Allah.

questionEn: In Sahih Muslim (2473), how did the Prophet ﷺ describe Zamzam water to Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA) when learning Abu Dharr had survived in Al-Masjid al-Haram for 30 days drinking nothing else?
optionsEn: 'Water cannot sustain a person'
'You should have eaten dates from Taif'
'Indeed, it is blessed (mubarakah); it is a nourishing food (ta'amu tu'm) [and a cure for illness]'
'Drink it only once a week'
explanationEn: When Abu Dharr (RA) hid near the Kaaba for thirty days and nights with no food except Zamzam water until his stomach folds grew plump without hunger, the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'It is blessed, and it is a food that nourishes!'

questionEn: Which great companion hid behind the curtains of the Kaaba for a month upon first arriving in Makkah to seek the Prophet ﷺ, sustaining himself solely on Zamzam water?
optionsEn: Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
Salman al-Farsi (RA)
Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
explanationEn: Traveling from the Ghifar tribe to investigate the Prophet's ﷺ message in Makkah, Abu Dharr (RA) stayed inside Al-Masjid al-Haram drinking only Zamzam until Ali (RA) hosted him and led him to the Prophet ﷺ.

questionEn: With what water did Angel Jibril (AS) wash the noble heart of the Prophet ﷺ in a golden basin before filling it with wisdom and faith prior to Al-Mi'raj?
optionsEn: Zamzam water
Rainwater from Jerusalem
Water from the Nile
Dew from Mount Sinai
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Anas ibn Malik (RA) narrated from Abu Dharr (RA) that the Prophet's ﷺ chest was opened in Makkah, his heart washed with Zamzam water in a golden vessel, and filled with hikmah and iman.

questionEn: According to Ibn Abbas (RA), in what posture did the Prophet ﷺ drink Zamzam water when Ibn Abbas served him at the well?
optionsEn: Lying down
Standing, facing the Kaaba
While running between Safa and Marwah
Only while seated on Mount Safa
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (1637): 'I gave the Prophet ﷺ Zamzam water to drink, and he drank it while standing.' Scholars note both standing and sitting are permissible.

questionEn: What supplication did Abdullah ibn Abbas (RA) famously recite whenever he drank Zamzam water?
optionsEn: 'Allahumma ajirni min an-nar'
'Rabbana hab lana min azwajina'
'Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'an, wa rizqan wasi'an, wa shifa'an min kulli da'' (O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, abundant provision, and healing from every illness)
'Bismillahi tawakaltu ala Allah'
explanationEn: Recorded by al-Daraqutni and al-Hakim from Ibn Abbas (RA), this comprehensive three-part dua for beneficial knowledge, ample sustenance, and cure from all ailments is beloved by scholars and pilgrims.

questionEn: What are the recommended Sunnah etiquettes documented by scholars like Ibn Majah and Ibn al-Qayyim when drinking Zamzam water?
optionsEn: Drink only three drops
Drink in one single gulp facing north
Never say Bismillah
Face the Qiblah, say Bismillah, drink in three breaths, drink one's fill (tawallu'), praise Allah (Alhamdulillah), and make sincere dua
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) advised drinking Zamzam in three breaths facing the Qiblah, drinking until one's ribs feel full (tawallu'), praising Allah, and asking Allah for one's heartfelt needs.

questionEn: Why did Ibn Abbas (RA) mention 'al-tawallu'' (drinking until one's ribs/stomach are completely full) as a special practice with Zamzam water?
optionsEn: Because hypocrites could not drink their fill of Zamzam, whereas believers drink it abundantly with love and faith
Because water was taxed by weight
To avoid carrying water skins
Only for athletes
explanationEn: In Sunan Ibn Majah (3061), Ibn Abbas (RA) reported the saying: 'The sign distinguishing us from the hypocrites is that they do not drink their fill (la yatadalla'una) of Zamzam.'

questionEn: Is it permissible in Islam to carry Zamzam water out of Makkah to one's home country for family and the sick?
optionsEn: No, Zamzam may never leave the Haram boundary
Yes, Aishah (RA) used to carry Zamzam water back in bottles and report that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ carried it
Only residents of Jeddah may take it
Only during Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: Jami at-Tirmidhi (963) records that Aishah (RA) carried Zamzam water in glass/clay flasks and stated that the Prophet ﷺ carried it in waterskins and flasks, pouring it over the sick and giving them to drink.

questionEn: Which great Hadith scholar drank Zamzam water in Makkah with the specific intention of memorizing Hadith and attaining mastery in knowledge?
optionsEn: Abu Jahl
Imru' al-Qays
Imam al-Shafi'i, Imam Ibn Khuzaymah, Imam al-Hakim, and Imam Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani (among many classical scholars)
Al-Mutanabbi
explanationEn: Imam Ibn Khuzaymah was asked where he acquired his vast knowledge and replied: 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said Zamzam is for whatever it is drunk for, and when I drank it, I asked Allah for beneficial knowledge!'

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say when he came to the Zamzam well during the Farewell Hajj and saw Banu Abd al-Muttalib drawing water for pilgrims?
optionsEn: 'Cover the well with timber'
'Stop drawing water at noon'
'Hand the well over to Khuza'ah'
'Draw water, O Banu Abd al-Muttalib! Were it not that the people would overwhelm you around your watering duty, I would draw along with you!'
explanationEn: Out of wisdom, the Prophet ﷺ refrained from pulling the rope himself only because if he did, pilgrims would consider pulling the rope themselves a mandatory rite and crowd out Banu Hashim's stewards.

questionEn: What is the approximate total depth of the Zamzam well shaft beneath the Mataf floor?
optionsEn: About 30 to 31 meters deep
5 meters deep
300 meters deep
1,000 meters deep
explanationEn: Hydrogeological surveys by the Saudi Geological Survey confirm the Zamzam well is approximately 30 to 31 meters deep, consisting of an upper stone-lined alluvial section and a lower bedrock section.

questionEn: Into what two geological sections is the 30-meter vertical shaft of the Zamzam well divided?
optionsEn: Two wooden barrels stacked together
An upper ~12.8-meter stone-lined section through wadi alluvium, and a lower ~17.2-meter section cut directly into solid diorite bedrock
Sand all the way down
Limestone caves and ocean coral
explanationEn: The upper 12.8 meters through valley sand are lined with dressed stone masonry, while the lower 17.2 meters are excavated through solid crystalline bedrock.

questionEn: From which three directions do the main underground bedrock fractures (fissures) feed water into the Zamzam well at around 13 meters depth?
optionsEn: From the Nile River
From the Red Sea in Jeddah
Mainly from the direction of the Kaaba/Black Stone (the largest source), alongside fissures toward Safa and Marwah
From artificial city water pipes
explanationEn: Hydrogeological inspections revealed that the primary rock fissure feeding Zamzam comes directly from the direction of the Holy Kaaba and Black Stone corner, supplemented by smaller openings toward Safa and Marwah.

questionEn: What is the name of the state-of-the-art facility in Makkah's Kudai district opened in 1431 AH (2010 CE) to filter, sterilize with UV light, and bottle Zamzam water?
optionsEn: Ain Zubaydah Reservoir
Jeddah Desalination Plant
Taif Rosewater Factory
King Abdullah ibn Abdulaziz Zamzam Water Project (KPZW)
explanationEn: Located in Kudai, the King Abdullah Zamzam Water Project uses automated micro-filtration and ultraviolet sterilization without altering Zamzam's natural mineral composition, supplying both Holy Mosques and 5-liter bottles.

questionEn: How does Zamzam water travel from the well beneath Al-Mataf to the Kudai treatment plant and to the drinking fountains across Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Through dedicated corrosion-resistant stainless steel underground pipelines
By camel caravans
In open concrete canals
By helicopters
explanationEn: Food-grade stainless steel underground pipes transport raw Zamzam to storage and UV treatment facilities and back to chilled marble fountains and insulated cylinders inside Al-Haram.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: How is Zamzam water also provided daily inside Al-Masjid al-Nabawi in Madinah—over 400 km north of Makkah?
optionsEn: Drawn from a second Zamzam well in Madinah
Transported daily from Makkah in dedicated sealed stainless-steel tanker trucks to Madinah's reservoirs
Made from local Madinah tap water
Zamzam is not served in Madinah
explanationEn: Every day, specialized sealed tanker trucks transport hundreds of tons of pure Zamzam water from Makkah to Al-Masjid al-Nabawi in Madinah so visitors there enjoy authentic Zamzam.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: Why does natural Zamzam water have a slightly distinct, refreshing mineral taste compared to ordinary distilled water?
optionsEn: Because rosewater is mixed into all dispensers
Because salt is added at the factory
Because it is naturally rich in beneficial dissolved minerals such as calcium, magnesium, sodium, and bicarbonates
Because it comes from the sea
explanationEn: Natural hydrogeological mineralization through Makkah's granite bedrock gives Zamzam higher levels of calcium, magnesium, and bicarbonates, contributing to its sustaining, alkaline character.

questionEn: Why do the insulated Zamzam water dispensers inside Al-Masjid al-Haram carry two different temperature labels ('Chilled' and 'Not Chilled / Normal')?
optionsEn: Because 'Not Chilled' is ordinary tap water
Because 'Not Chilled' is for washing floors
Because only children may drink chilled water
So pilgrims who are overheated, elderly, or have sore throats can choose mild room-temperature Zamzam while others enjoy cold water
explanationEn: Providing both chilled and mildly cool ('Ghayr Mubarrad') Zamzam protects pilgrims' throats and health while ensuring everyone drinks pure Zamzam comfortably.

questionEn: What is the Islamic ruling on using Zamzam water for Wudu vs Istinja (cleaning impurity in the restroom)?
optionsEn: Using Zamzam for drinking and Wudu is permissible, whereas scholars strongly dislike/forbid using blessed Zamzam water for Istinja (removing filth) out of respect
Zamzam cannot be used for Wudu
Zamzam is only for laundry
There is no difference at all
explanationEn: Because Zamzam is an honored, blessed food and drink ('ta'amu tu'm'), jurists permit Wudu with it if needed while discouraging its use for removing physical impurities (istinja).

questionEn: Which Surah and verse explicitly name Both 'Al-Safa' and 'Al-Marwah' as symbols of Allah ('Sha'a'irillah')?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Fatihah 1:7
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:158
Surah Al-Kahf 18:18
Surah Al-Ikhlas 112:2
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158) begins: 'Inna as-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah'—'Indeed, Al-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah.'

questionEn: Why did some Ansar and early Muslims hesitate to perform Sa'i between Safa and Marwah before Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158) was revealed?
optionsEn: Because there was no roof over Al-Mas'a
Because the hills were too steep to climb
Because in pre-Islamic times two idols (Isaf and Na'ilah) stood on Safa and Marwah, and in Jahiliyyah the Ansar had chanted Talbiyah for Manat, so they feared sinning by walking between them
Because they thought Sa'i was only for women
explanationEn: As Aishah (RA) explained to her nephew Urwah ibn al-Zubayr in Sahih al-Bukhari (1643), the verse 'there is no blame upon him to walk between them' removed the Companions' hesitation caused by pre-Islamic idols—while confirming Sa'i is an essential rite!

questionEn: How did Aishah (RA) correct her nephew Urwah ibn al-Zubayr when he thought the phrase 'there is no blame upon him' in 2:158 meant Sa'i between Safa and Marwah was merely optional?
optionsEn: She said Sa'i applies only in Ramadan
She agreed that Sa'i is optional
She said only three laps are needed
She explained the historical context of the verse and declared: 'Allah does not complete the Hajj or Umrah of anyone who does not perform Sa'i between Safa and Marwah!'
explanationEn: Aishah (RA) showed that had the verse meant Sa'i was optional, it would have said 'no blame if he does NOT walk between them'; rather, both the Prophet ﷺ and the Muslims performed Sa'i as a required rite.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ say upon ascending Mount Safa to begin Sa'i, directly quoting Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158)?
optionsEn: 'Inna as-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah—abda'u bima bada'Allahu bihi' ('I begin with that with which Allah began!')
'Subhana Rabbiyal-A'la'
'Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik'
'Rabbana taqabbal minna'
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated in Sahih Muslim (1218) that as the Prophet ﷺ approached Mount Safa, he recited 2:158 and said 'I begin with what Allah began with'—starting strictly at Safa.

questionEn: Is the phrase 'Inna as-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah; abda'u bima bada'Allahu bihi' recited on every lap of Sa'i, or ONLY once when approaching Safa at the very start of Lap 1?
optionsEn: At both Safa and Marwah on all seven laps
Only once when first approaching Mount Safa at the start of the first lap
Only at the end of the seventh lap at Marwah
While jogging between the green lights
explanationEn: Scholars note from Jabir's (RA) hadith that the Prophet ﷺ recited this opening verse only once upon first ascending Safa to begin Sa'i, not on subsequent returns.

questionEn: How are the seven laps (ashwat) of Sa'i between Safa and Marwah counted?
optionsEn: Starting at Marwah and ending at Safa
Going Safa -> Marwah -> Safa counts as 1 lap (requiring 14 one-way walks)
Walking from Safa to Marwah is Lap 1, and returning from Marwah to Safa is Lap 2—starting at Safa and finishing Lap 7 at Marwah
Walking around Safa in circles seven times
explanationEn: Each one-way traverse between the two hills is one complete lap (shawt): odd-numbered laps (1, 3, 5, 7) go from Safa to Marwah, and even-numbered laps (2, 4, 6) return from Marwah to Safa.

questionEn: On which hill does a pilgrim ALWAYS finish the seventh and final lap of Sa'i?
optionsEn: Mount Arafat
Mount Safa
Jabal Abi Qubays
Mount Marwah
explanationEn: Because Lap 1 starts at Safa and goes to Marwah, the seventh lap necessarily ends atop Mount Marwah—where men then shave or trim their hair to exit Umrah Ihram.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim mistakenly starts their Sa'i at Mount Marwah instead of Mount Safa?
optionsEn: The first walk from Marwah to Safa does not count; their 1st valid lap begins once they start from Safa toward Marwah, so they must add one final lap to finish at Marwah
It is completely valid as is
They must redo their Tawaf too
They must pay a camel penalty
explanationEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ commanded 'Begin with what Allah began with' (Safa), a walk starting from Marwah is disregarded, and counting starts from Safa.

questionEn: What is the approximate one-way distance between Mount Safa and Mount Marwah, and the total distance of all seven laps?
optionsEn: 50 meters one way (350 meters total)
Roughly 394 meters one way (about 2.76 kilometers total for 7 laps)
2 kilometers one way (14 kilometers total)
10 kilometers one way
explanationEn: The corridor of Al-Mas'a measures approximately 394 meters from the Safa rock to the Marwah rock, totaling roughly 2.75 to 2.8 kilometers across seven laps.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do each time he ascended Mount Safa and Mount Marwah during Sa'i?
optionsEn: He kissed the stones of Safa
He prayed two rak'ahs of Salah on top of the rocks

He climbed until he could see the Kaaba (facing the Qiblah), proclaimed Allahu Akbar three times, praised Allah, recited 'La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu la sharika lah... Anjaza wa'dahu...', and made lengthy personal dua three times
He clapped his hands twice
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) recorded that at both Safa and Marwah, the Prophet ﷺ faced the Qiblah, pronounced Takbir and Tahlil, recited the famous dhikr three times, and supplicated earnestly between them.

questionEn: Which powerful phrase of Tawhid and victory did the Prophet ﷺ include in his dhikr atop Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: 'Astaghfirullah al-Azim'
'Bismillahi majreha wa mursaha'
'Subhana man sakhkhara lana hadha'

'La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu, anjaza wa'dahu, wa nasara 'abdahu, wa hazamal-ahzaba wahdah' ('There is no god but Allah alone; He fulfilled His promise, aided His servant, and defeated the confederates alone')
explanationEn: Standing atop Safa where Quraysh had once mocked his earliest call, the Prophet ﷺ proclaimed that Allah alone had fulfilled His promise and granted victory to His servant.

questionEn: How should a pilgrim raise their hands when making dua atop Safa and Marwah facing the Kaaba?
optionsEn: Raise both palms upward in humble supplication (dua posture), NOT gesturing or waving as if doing Takbiratul-Ihram in Salah
Point with one finger only
Keep hands locked behind the back
Touch the floor with both palms
explanationEn: Many pilgrims mistakenly wave their hands at Safa as if greeting the hill; the Sunnah is to face the Kaaba and raise one's open palms in the normal posture of dua.

questionEn: At the completion of the 7th lap atop Mount Marwah, do pilgrims repeat the long standing dua, or has their Sa'i concluded upon reaching Marwah?
optionsEn: They must walk an 8th lap back to Safa
Sa'i concludes upon reaching Marwah at the end of the 7th lap, after which pilgrims proceed to shave or trim their hair
They must pray 4 rak'ahs on Marwah
They must wait until sunset on Marwah
explanationEn: Once the pilgrim completes the seventh lap from Safa to Marwah, the rite of Sa'i is complete.

questionEn: What do the two bright green fluorescent/LED light bands (Al-Milayn al-Akhdarayn) along the walls and ceiling of Al-Mas'a mark?
optionsEn: The place where pilgrims must sit down
The halfway distance to Madinah
The ancient low valley bed (Batn al-Wadi / Batn al-Mas'il) where Hajar (RA) ran swiftly and where the Prophet ﷺ jogged briskly
The entrance to Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Even though the modern marble floor of Al-Mas'a is level, the two green light markers preserve the exact span of the historic dry riverbed where Hajar and the Prophet ﷺ ran.

questionEn: Roughly how long is the stretch between the two green markers (Al-Milayn al-Akhdarayn) inside Al-Mas'a, where men jog briskly?
optionsEn: 1 kilometer
About 350 meters (the whole corridor)
Only 2 meters
About 50 to 75 meters
explanationEn: The green-lit zone spans roughly 50 to 75 meters closer to the Safa side of the corridor; men walk normally before the first green light, jog briskly between the two green lights, and walk normally again to Marwah.

questionEn: Does the Sunnah of jogging briskly (Sa'y / Harwalah) between the two green lights in Al-Mas'a apply to women as well as men?
optionsEn: No, scholars unanimously agree that women walk at a dignified normal pace throughout all of Sa'i and never jog between the green lights
Yes, women must run faster than men
Women jog only on odd laps
Women jog only at night
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) and scholarly consensus affirm that neither Raml in Tawaf nor brisk running between the green markers in Sa'i is prescribed for women; modesty and calm walking are their Sunnah.

questionEn: Is ritual purity (Wudu) a strict prerequisite for the validity of Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, as it is for Tawaf?
optionsEn: Breaking Wudu during Sa'i requires sacrificing a camel

While being in Wudu during Sa'i is recommended and virtuous, the majority of scholars hold that Sa'i remains valid even if one's Wudu breaks or a woman's menses begins after she already completed Tawaf
Wudu is forbidden during Sa'i
One must repeat Tawaf if Wudu breaks in Sa'i
explanationEn: Because the Prophet ﷺ told menstruating Aishah (RA) 'Do everything the pilgrim does except Tawaf around the House,' jurists deduce that if a woman completes Tawaf pure and then menstruates, she may still perform Sa'i and complete her Umrah/Hajj.

questionEn: Why is the ruling on a woman whose menses starts AFTER she finishes Tawaf but BEFORE she starts Sa'i such an important practical mercy in Makkah?
optionsEn: She can never enter Al-Mas'a
She must stay in Ihram for a whole year
Because Sa'i does not require purity from menses according to authentic hadith, allowing her to complete Sa'i, trim her hair, and finish her Umrah on schedule with her travel group
She must redo Tawaf while menstruating
explanationEn: Al-Mas'a is considered outside the strict prayer-hall ruling of the central mosque regarding menstruation after Tawaf, providing immense relief to traveling female pilgrims.

questionEn: Can a pilgrim perform voluntary (nafl) Sa'i between Safa and Marwah by itself without an Umrah or Hajj, the way one performs voluntary Tawaf?
optionsEn: Yes, instead of praying Fajr
Yes, people should do ten voluntary Sa'is daily
Yes, on Fridays only
No—there is no standalone voluntary Sa'i in Islam; Sa'i is legislated strictly as part of Hajj or Umrah following Tawaf
explanationEn: Unlike Tawaf, which can be performed voluntarily at any time around the Kaaba, Sa'i between Safa and Marwah is only performed once per Umrah and once per Hajj.

questionEn: On Mount Safa during the early Makkan period, which Qur'anic verse prompted the Prophet ﷺ to climb the hill and call out 'Ya Sabahah!' to gather the clans of Quraysh?
optionsEn: Surah Ash-Shu'ara 26:214 ('And warn your closest kindred')
Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255
Surah Al-Mulk 67:1
Surah Al-Nasr 110:1
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (4770), Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that when 'And warn your closest kindred' (26:214) was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ ascended Mount Safa and called each clan of Quraysh by name.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ stood on Mount Safa and asked Quraysh: 'If I told you that cavalry in the valley behind this mountain were about to attack you, would you believe me?', how did they reply?
optionsEn: 'No, we doubt your words'
'Yes! We have never experienced anything from you except truth!'
'Only if Abu Jahl agrees'
'Show us the horses first'
explanationEn: Even his staunchest opponents testified atop Mount Safa to the Prophet's ﷺ lifelong truthfulness before he warned them of a severe Day of Judgment.

questionEn: Who rudely shouted 'Tabban laka sa'iral-yawm! Is this why you gathered us?' at the foot of Mount Safa, prompting the revelation of Surah Al-Masad (111)?
optionsEn: Abu Sufyan
Umar ibn al-Khattab
Abu Lahab
Utbah ibn Rabi'ah
explanationEn: When Abu Lahab cursed the Prophet's ﷺ gathering at Mount Safa, Allah immediately revealed 'Tabbat yada Abi Lahabin wa tabb' (Surah Al-Masad 111:1-5).

questionEn: Where near Mount Safa was the famous house 'Dar al-Arqam' located, where the Prophet ﷺ secretly taught the earliest Muslims in Makkah?
optionsEn: In Mina valley
On top of Mount Thawr
In Al-Tan'eem
At the foot/eastern slope of Mount Safa
explanationEn: Dar al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam (RA) sat right on the flank of Mount Safa, allowing companions to slip in discreetly while pretending to visit the sanctuary.

questionEn: Where did the Prophet ﷺ stand on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah (8 AH) to receive the pledge of allegiance (Bay'ah) from the men and women of Makkah after praying in the sanctuary?
optionsEn: Upon Mount Safa
Inside Cave Hira
At Al-Hudaybiyyah
In Jeddah
explanationEn: Coming full circle from the day he was mocked on Safa, the victorious Prophet ﷺ sat humbly upon Mount Safa on the Day of Conquest as Makkans streamed up to pledge allegiance to Islam.

questionEn: While sitting on Mount Safa after the Conquest of Makkah, how did the Prophet ﷺ reassure the Ansar when they feared he might stay permanently in his native Makkah?
optionsEn: He told them to buy houses in Makkah
He raised his head from dua on Safa and said: 'Allah forbid! My life is your life, and my death is with you [in Madinah]!'
He appointed an Ansari king of Makkah
He stayed in Makkah for five years
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim (1780), seeing the Ansar whisper anxiously as he prayed at length on Mount Safa, the Prophet ﷺ moved them to tears by pledging never to leave Madinah.

questionEn: What did the natural rocks of Mount Safa and Mount Marwah look like before and after the modern multi-story expansions of Al-Mas'a?
optionsEn: They are 200-meter tall cliffs inside the building
The rocks were completely removed and replaced with plastic
Today portions of the original natural dark mountain rock are preserved beneath protective glass domes/barriers at the Safa and Marwah ends of the air-conditioned gallery
They are covered with grass and trees
explanationEn: At the southern (Safa) and northern (Marwah) ends of the ground-floor Mas'a, the original rough bedrock outcrops of both sacred hills remain visible and protected.

questionEn: Does a pilgrim need to climb all the way onto the bare rocky dome of Safa or Marwah for their Sa'i lap to be valid?
optionsEn: Climbing invalidates Sa'i
Yes, one must touch the top rock with bare hands
Only if wearing sandals
No—reaching the base/paved incline of the hill (or the end of the designated Mas'a walkway on upper floors) completely fulfills the requirement
explanationEn: Jurists explain that 'walking between Safa and Marwah' requires traversing the span from hill to hill; ascending high onto the rocks is a Sunnah when uncrowded, not an obligation.

questionEn: What major architectural milestone did the First Saudi Expansion (begun in 1375 AH / 1955 CE) achieve regarding Al-Mas'a between Safa and Marwah?
optionsEn: It enclosed and roofed Al-Mas'a into a two-story covered gallery integrated into Al-Masjid al-Haram, separating pedestrian pilgrims from street traffic and market stalls
It moved Safa 100 meters west
It dug a canal between Safa and Marwah
It removed the roof of Al-Mas'a
explanationEn: Prior to 1955, the path between Safa and Marwah was an open street flanked by shops, homes, and passing animals; the First Saudi Expansion built a dedicated covered two-story Mas'a.
reference: History of the Two Holy Mosques Expansions

questionEn: During the 2007–2009 (King Abdullah) expansion of Al-Mas'a, how was the width and capacity of the Safa-Marwah corridor increased?
optionsEn: It was narrowed to 5 meters
Its width was doubled from ~20 meters to ~40 meters and expanded across four stories, nearly tripling hourly Sa'i capacity
It was moved underground only
It was shortened to 100 meters
explanationEn: Consulted upon by senior scholars confirming that the biological/geological bases of Safa and Marwah extended eastward, the expansion doubled Al-Mas'a's width to 40 meters across multiple levels.
reference: Council of Senior Scholars & Haram Expansion Records

questionEn: On what geographic basis did Islamic scholars approve widening Al-Mas'a eastward during the modern expansion?
optionsEn: Because Marwah was moved north
Because direction does not matter in Sa'i
Geological and historical evidence confirmed that the natural rocky extensions of Mount Safa and Mount Marwah stretched further east across the widened footprint
Because only 3 laps were needed
explanationEn: Because Sa'i must take place strictly between the physical hill masses of Safa and Marwah, geologists and scholars verified that the widened eastern lanes still lie directly between the two natural mountains.
reference: Resolutions of the Council of Senior Scholars

questionEn: Why is the corridor of Al-Mas'a divided longitudinally into two one-way pedestrian channels with a central wheelchair lane?
optionsEn: To close half the hall every hour
To separate tall and short pilgrims
To allow camels in the middle
So pilgrims going from Safa to Marwah never collide head-on with pilgrims returning from Marwah to Safa
explanationEn: Keeping outbound (Safa -> Marwah) traffic on the right and inbound (Marwah -> Safa) traffic on the opposite side prevents head-on congestion for tens of thousands of walkers.

questionEn: What should a pilgrim do if the Iqamah for congregational Salah is called while they are on Lap 3 of Sa'i inside Al-Mas'a?
optionsEn: Stop walking, join the congregational prayer facing the Kaaba right there in Al-Mas'a, and immediately resume Lap 3 from that exact spot once Salah finishes
Keep running through the prayer rows
Restart from Lap 1 at Safa after Salah
Leave the mosque without praying
explanationEn: Congregational Fard prayer takes priority; once the Imam says Taslim, pilgrims simply stand up and continue their Sa'i lap from the exact spot where they paused.

questionEn: If an elderly or exhausted pilgrim rests on a bench at Safa or Marwah for a few minutes between laps of Sa'i, does that invalidate their Sa'i?
optionsEn: Yes, stopping for 10 seconds invalidates Sa'i
No—briefly sitting to rest out of fatigue or drinking Zamzam water along the way is completely permissible and does not break continuity
They must pay a fidyah
They must add two extra laps
explanationEn: Scholars agree that pausing briefly to catch one's breath, drink from the Zamzam dispensers in Al-Mas'a, or use the restroom does not invalidate the continuity (muwalah) of Sa'i.

questionEn: How did the Prophet ﷺ perform the latter part of his Sa'i between Safa and Marwah during the Farewell Pilgrimage when crowds pressed closely around him?
optionsEn: He postponed it for three weeks
He asked Bilal to complete it for him
He began walking on foot and then completed it riding his camel so people could see him and ask questions without crushing him
He flew over the crowd
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) and Abu al-Tufayl (RA) narrated in Sahih Muslim (1274) that when the crowd grew dense around the Prophet ﷺ in Al-Mas'a, he rode his camel—proving that riding (or using a wheelchair/cart) in Sa'i is valid.

questionEn: In which direction does Mount Marwah lie relative to Mount Safa?
optionsEn: In Mina valley
Due south of Mount Safa
Due west of the Kaaba
Roughly north-northeast of Mount Safa
explanationEn: Mount Safa sits at the southern end of Al-Mas'a (connected to the flank of Jabal Abi Qubays), while Mount Marwah sits ~394 meters to the north-northeast (connected to Jabal Qu'ayqi'an).

questionEn: To which larger Makkan mountain is the rocky spur of Mount Safa geologically connected?
optionsEn: Jabal Abi Qubays
Jabal Thawr
Jabal al-Noor
Jabal Rahmah
explanationEn: Mount Safa is the lower northwestern rocky spur extending from the foot of Jabal Abi Qubays on the eastern side of Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: To which larger Makkan mountain is the rocky outcrop of Mount Marwah geologically connected?
optionsEn: Jabal Hira
Jabal Qu'ayqi'an
Jabal Uhud
Jabal Thawr
explanationEn: Mount Marwah forms the lower projection extending from the base of Jabal Qu'ayqi'an on the northern/northeastern side of the sanctuary.

questionEn: What do the Arabic names 'Al-Safa' and 'Al-Marwah' literally mean in describing their rock types?
optionsEn: They mean East and West
They mean Sun and Moon
Al-Safa means smooth, hard, solid rock slabs; Al-Marwah means white flint or quartz-pebble stone
They mean Water and Fire
explanationEn: Classical Arabic lexicographers note that 'Safa' denotes smooth, hard granite boulders, while 'Marwah' denotes bright flinty quartz stone—matching the actual geology of the two hills.

questionEn: Which famous supplication did Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) and Abdullah ibn Umar (RA) recite while jogging briskly between the two green markers in Al-Mas'a?
optionsEn: 'Qul a'udhu bi-Rabbil-falaq'
'Bismillahi wal-hamdu lillah'
'Subhana Rabbiyal-Azim'
'Rabbi ighfir warham, innaka Antal-A'azzul-Akram' ('My Lord, forgive and have mercy; indeed You are the Most Mighty, the Most Noble')
explanationEn: Authentically reported from Ibn Mas'ud and Ibn Umar (RA) during Sa'i in Batn al-Mas'il: 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, and pardon what You know; indeed You are the Most Mighty, the Most Generous.'

questionEn: Is it valid for a pilgrim to perform Sa'i BEFORE Tawaf during a regular Umrah?
optionsEn: No—for Umrah, Tawaf around the Kaaba must be performed FIRST, followed by Sa'i between Safa and Marwah
Yes, in Umrah order never matters
Only if starting at Marwah
Yes, if done at night
explanationEn: In Umrah, performing Tawaf before Sa'i is a required order (whereas on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah in Hajj, the Prophet ﷺ accepted those who did Hajj rites out of order).

questionEn: After finishing the 7th lap of Umrah Sa'i at Mount Marwah, what rite must a pilgrim perform to exit the state of Ihram (Tahallul)?
optionsEn: Jump three times on Marwah
Men shave their entire head (Halq—which is superior) or trim hair evenly from all over the head (Taqsir); women trim a fingertip's length (~1–2 cm) from the ends of their hair
Walk back to Safa
Wash their sandals in Zamzam
explanationEn: Halq or Taqsir after completing Sa'i at Marwah releases the Umrah pilgrim from Ihram restrictions; the Prophet ﷺ prayed three times for those who shave (Muhalliqin) and once for those who trim (Muqassirin).

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ pray 'O Allah, have mercy on those who shave their heads (al-muhalliqin)' three times before saying 'and on those who trim (al-muqassirin)' on the fourth time?
optionsEn: Because women must shave their heads
Because scissors had not been invented
To highlight the greater humility and complete devotion of shaving the entire head for Allah (for men), while confirming trimming is also valid
Because trimming invalidates Umrah
explanationEn: For men, shaving the entire head (Halq) is superior unless another Hajj follows immediately within days; for women, shaving is strictly forbidden and only trimming a fingertip length is prescribed.

questionEn: What is a common mistake some men make when trimming (Taqsir) their hair at Marwah after Umrah?
optionsEn: Stepping outside Marwah first
Using clean clippers
Facing the Qiblah
Snipping only two or three hairs from one side instead of trimming evenly across the whole head
explanationEn: Majority jurists (Maliki, Hanbali, and many scholars) emphasize that valid Taqsir requires shortening hair across the general expanse of the head, not merely snipping three single strands.

questionEn: Why are pilgrims discouraged from cutting their hair right on the marble floor atop Mount Marwah inside the crowded Mas'a?
optionsEn: Because loose hair on the marble floor is unsanitary, slippery for barefoot walkers, and blocks pilgrims finishing Lap 7—licensed barbers sit just outside the Marwah exits
Because scissors break inside Al-Haram
Because hair must only be cut in Jeddah
Because cutting hair at night is forbidden
explanationEn: A pilgrim stays in Ihram until stepping outside Marwah to a clean barbershop or hotel room to shave/trim hygienically, keeping the sanctuary floor spotless.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ do with Zamzam water right after praying the two Sunnah rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim during his Farewell Hajj?
optionsEn: He boiled it with tea
He walked to the Zamzam station, drank from it, and poured some of the blessed water over his head
He poured it onto the Black Stone
He fasted from water for two days
explanationEn: Narrated in Musnad Ahmad and Sahih Muslim (1218) from Jabir (RA), the Prophet ﷺ came to the sons of Abd al-Muttalib at Zamzam, drank from the bucket, and poured some water over his head.

questionEn: What is the hydrologic miracle of the Zamzam well regarding its continuous operation over thousands of years?
optionsEn: It flows with milk in Ramadan
It freezes solid every winter
Despite sitting in a desert valley with no surface rivers and serving millions of pilgrims annually, it has never run dry nor suffered biological algae/bacterial overgrowth blocking the spring
It is refilled from the Red Sea by trucks
explanationEn: Fulfilling the prophecy given to Hajar (RA) and Abdul-Muttalib ('La tunzafu wa la tudham'), Zamzam has continuously supplied millions of liters across millennia in a desert basin.
reference: Sirah Ibn Hisham & Saudi Geological Survey

questionEn: How does the Zamzam Studies and Research Center (under the Saudi Geological Survey) monitor the Zamzam aquifer so it is never over-pumped?
optionsEn: No monitoring is ever done
By dropping a rope with knots once a year
By guessing from cloud cover
Using digital sensors that continuously monitor water table levels, rainfall recharge across Wadi Ibrahim, pH, conductivity, and pumping rates
explanationEn: Digital telemetry tracks water levels, recharge across the 60 km² Wadi Ibrahim catchment basin, and pumping schedules 24/7 to safeguard sustainability.

questionEn: What is the name of the natural valley catchment basin (~60 square kilometers) in Makkah that channels rainwater recharge into the bedrock fractures feeding Zamzam?
optionsEn: Wadi Ibrahim
Wadi al-Aqiq
Wadi Hanifah
Wadi Qana
explanationEn: Al-Masjid al-Haram sits along the course of Wadi Ibrahim, Makkah's main valley basin named after Prophet Ibrahim (AS).

questionEn: In 1399–1400 AH (1979–1980 CE), when King Khalid ordered a thorough underwater cleaning of the bottom of the Zamzam well, who dove down to clean it?
optionsEn: Roman divers
Trained Muslim engineers and divers led by Engineer Yahya Koshak, who removed centuries of coins, buckets, and debris while mapping the bedrock springs
Unmanned submarines from Europe
No one has ever entered the well
explanationEn: Engineer Yahya Koshak and his team sanitized the well bottom, removed antique copper pots and coins dropped by past visitors, and documented the exact rock fissures gushing with water.

questionEn: What words were found carved on an ancient marble stone plaque inside the Zamzam well wall during historical inspections?
optionsEn: Greek philosophy
A map to buried gold in Yemen
Historical restoration dates (such as Abbasid/Mamluk refurbishments) and 'Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim'
Names of Roman emperors
explanationEn: Stone inscriptions inside the upper masonry lining record historical restorations and casings of the Zamzam shaft across Islamic centuries.

questionEn: Why is the commercial sale or black-market profiteering of Zamzam water prohibited by regulations in Saudi Arabia, while official 5-liter bottles are sold at nominal bottling cost at airports?
optionsEn: To restrict Zamzam to Makkah residents
Because Zamzam evaporates in shops
Because plastic bottles are illegal
To preserve the ancient Islamic principle of Al-Siqayah—keeping Zamzam freely accessible inside the Two Holy Mosques and preventing exploitation or counterfeit bottles
explanationEn: Banning commercial resale protects pilgrims from counterfeit water and honors the Prophetic tradition that Zamzam is a free gift of Allah to His guests.
reference: King Abdullah Zamzam Water Project Regulations

questionEn: How should pilgrims dispose of used disposable plastic cups after drinking Zamzam inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: Place them into the 'Used Cups' (Musta'mal) side compartment of the dispenser rack—never putting used cups back into the 'Clean/New Cups' stack or dropping them on the marble floor
Put used cups back on top of the clean stack
Leave them on the prayer carpet
Throw them into Hijr Ismail
explanationEn: Every Zamzam rack has a clearly marked clean dispenser and a separate waste/used receptor; keeping used cups separate prevents spreading illness among Allah's guests.

questionEn: What happens if a few drops of Zamzam water spill onto the smooth white marble floor of Al-Mataf or Al-Mas'a?
optionsEn: The marble absorbs it instantly in 1 second
It creates a serious slipping hazard for barefoot pilgrims; worshipers should drink carefully over the tray and alert cleaners if water spills
It turns the marble black
Nothing—wet marble is never slippery
explanationEn: Polished marble becomes extremely slick when wet; drinking neatly over the dispenser basin and avoiding splashing water across walkways protects elderly pilgrims from falls.

questionEn: Which two sons of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) represent the two branches of prophetic lineage—with Ismail (AS) settled at Zamzam in Makkah and Ishaq (AS) in the Levant?
optionsEn: Dawud and Sulayman (AS)
Musa and Harun (AS)
Prophet Ismail (AS) in Makkah (ancestor of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) and Prophet Ishaq (AS) in Al-Sham (ancestor of Yaqub and the Israelite prophets)
Habil and Qabil
explanationEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:39), aged Ibrahim (AS) praises Allah for granting him Ismail and Ishaq, linking the sanctuaries of Makkah and Al-Aqsa in one prophetic family.

questionEn: In Surah Ibrahim (14:40), what personal prayer for Salah did Ibrahim (AS) make immediately after praying for Makkah and his family at Zamzam?
optionsEn: 'Give us ships on the sea'
'Grant me a kingdom like Sulayman'
'Make the desert cold'
'Rabbi ij'alni muqimas-salati wa min dhurriyyati, Rabbana wa taqabbal du'a'' ('My Lord, make me an establisher of prayer, and from my descendants; our Lord, and accept my supplication')
explanationEn: Surah Ibrahim (14:37–41) reveals that the entire purpose of settling Ismail at the Kaaba and Zamzam was establishing Salah ('li-yuqimus-salah') and grateful devotion to Allah.

questionEn: What did Ibrahim (AS) state in Surah Ibrahim (14:37) was the ultimate spiritual reason he settled his family by the Sacred House in Makkah's barren valley?
optionsEn: 'Our Lord, that they may establish prayer (Rabbana li-yuqimus-salah)'
'That they may mine gold'
'That they may build fortresses'
'That they may escape taxes'
explanationEn: The phrase 'Rabbana li-yuqimus-salah' in 14:37 anchors Makkah's existence: Hajar, Ismail, Zamzam, and the Kaaba were all brought together so prayer to Allah would be established.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say in Sahih al-Bukhari (3364) regarding Hajar's (RA) seven runs between Safa and Marwah: 'Fa-dhalika sa'yu an-nasi baynahuma'?
optionsEn: To say only mothers should do Sa'i
To honor a believing mother's perseverance and Tawakkul by making her exact footsteps between Safa and Marwah a permanent pillar of Hajj and Umrah for all believers until the end of time
To say Sa'i was invented by Quraysh
To cancel Sa'i after the Conquest
explanationEn: Millions of prophets, scholars, kings, and believers across history walk in the exact footsteps of Hajar (RA)—a black/Egyptian bondwoman honored eternally by Allah for her faith and motherly devotion.

questionEn: What does the word 'Al-Sa'i' (السعي) literally mean in Arabic?
optionsEn: Standing motionless
Sleeping under shade
Striving, walking purposefully, or hastening in effort
Circle dancing
explanationEn: In Arabic and the Qur'an (e.g., 'wa an laysa lil-insani illa ma sa'a', 53:39), Sa'i means purposeful striving and effort—embodied physically between Safa and Marwah.

questionEn: What does 'Al-Mas'a' (المسعى) mean grammatically in Arabic?
optionsEn: The curtain of the door
The name of a well
The key of the Kaaba
A noun of place (ism makan) meaning 'the place/corridor where Sa'i is performed'
explanationEn: Just as 'Al-Mataf' is the place of Tawaf, 'Al-Mas'a' is the grammatical noun of place denoting the gallery between Safa and Marwah where Sa'i takes place.

questionEn: How many total levels (floors) can be used for Sa'i in the expanded Al-Mas'a building today?
optionsEn: Multiple levels (basement/lower level, ground floor, first floor, second floor, and roof/mezzanine tiers)
Only a single open dirt path
Twenty underground floors
Only the roof
explanationEn: Modern expansions constructed a multi-story air-conditioned Mas'a building with escalators and elevators connecting its levels so hundreds of thousands can perform Sa'i simultaneously.
reference: General Presidency for the Affairs of the Two Holy Mosques

questionEn: Is performing Sa'i on the upper floors or roof of Al-Mas'a just as valid as on the ground floor?
optionsEn: No, upper floors only count as half a lap
Yes, completely valid, because the air column directly above the space between Safa and Marwah shares the exact same legal status
Only valid for wheelchair users
Only valid during Hajj, not Umrah
explanationEn: Islamic scholars unanimously confirm that upper floors of Al-Mas'a vertically aligned between Safa and Marwah carry the exact same validity as the ground floor.

questionEn: Where are the automated electric golf carts and wheelchair rental services located for elderly or mobility-impaired pilgrims needing assistance in Sa'i?
optionsEn: Only outside Makkah
Inside Hijr Ismail
On designated upper mezzanine/floor lanes of Al-Mas'a, accessed via elevators and ramps near Safa and Marwah
Behind Maqam Ibrahim on the ground floor
explanationEn: Dedicated upper-tier lanes in Al-Mas'a host electric mobility carts and smooth wheelchair tracks separated from foot traffic for maximum safety.

questionEn: If a healthy person pushes their elderly parent in a wheelchair during all seven laps of Sa'i while both are in Ihram for Umrah, whose Sa'i is fulfilled?
optionsEn: Neither—both must repeat it alone
Only the person sitting in the wheelchair
Only the person pushing

BOTH the elderly parent riding in the wheelchair AND the son/daughter pushing it fulfill their own Sa'i simultaneously (provided both intended their own Sa'i), plus the pusher earns great reward for khidmah (service)
explanationEn: Jurists confirm that a pilgrim in Ihram who pushes another pilgrim in a wheelchair during Tawaf or Sa'i validly completes their own Tawaf/Sa'i AND helps the rider complete theirs.

questionEn: What is the ruling on a pilgrim talking to a family member about necessary directions or safety while walking in Al-Mas'a?
optionsEn: Permissible when needed without invalidating Sa'i, though devoting one's tongue primarily to Dhikr, dua, and Qur'an is far better
Speaking a single word invalidates that lap
They must pay a penalty for talking
They must restart from Safa
explanationEn: Necessary, polite speech does not invalidate Sa'i or Tawaf, though guarding the tongue from idle talk and focusing on remembrance of Allah fulfills the spirit of pilgrimage.

questionEn: During Hajj al-Tamattu' (the most common type of Hajj), how many times does a pilgrim perform Sa'i between Safa and Marwah in total?
optionsEn: Only once for both combined
Twice in total: once for their initial Umrah upon arriving in Makkah, and a second time for their Hajj (after Tawaf al-Ifadah)
Seven separate days of Sa'i
Never during Tamattu'
explanationEn: Because a Tamattu' pilgrim performs a complete standalone Umrah (Tawaf + Sa'i + hair trim) and later enters a separate Ihram on 8th Dhul-Hijjah for Hajj, they perform a second Sa'i for Hajj.

questionEn: By contrast, during Hajj al-Ifrad or Hajj al-Qiran, how many times is Sa'i between Safa and Marwah required?
optionsEn: Three times
Four times
Only ONCE—either right after the arrival Tawaf (Tawaf al-Qudum) or after Tawaf al-Ifadah
Zero times
explanationEn: As Jabir (RA) narrated in Sahih Muslim (1218), the Prophet ﷺ (who performed Qiran) and his companions who kept one continuous Ihram performed only one Sa'i between Safa and Marwah.

questionEn: If a Hajj Ifrad or Qiran pilgrim already performed their Hajj Sa'i right after Tawaf al-Qudum upon arriving in Makkah, do they repeat Sa'i after Tawaf al-Ifadah on the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: They must do Sa'i at Arafat
Yes, they must do three more Sa'is
Their earlier Sa'i was invalid
No—their earlier Sa'i already fulfilled the Hajj pillar, so on the 10th they perform Tawaf al-Ifadah without repeating Sa'i
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) explicitly reported: 'The Prophet ﷺ and his companions who had sacrificial animals did not perform Sa'i between Safa and Marwah except a single Sa'i—his first Sa'i.'

questionEn: Does Tawaf al-Wada' (the Farewell Tawaf before leaving Makkah) have any Sa'i between Safa and Marwah after it?
optionsEn: No—Tawaf al-Wada' is strictly seven circuits around the Kaaba (plus two rak'ahs of prayer) with NO Sa'i afterward
Yes, seven laps of Sa'i are required after Tawaf al-Wada'
Yes, three laps of Sa'i
Only if leaving by plane
explanationEn: Tawaf al-Wada' is a farewell greeting to the Kaaba alone; no Sa'i follows it.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158) commentary / Hadith that Allah is 'Shakirun Alim' (Appreciative, All-Knowing) at the end of the Safa and Marwah verse?
optionsEn: Because only scholars know the distance
'And whoever volunteers good—indeed, Allah is Appreciative and Knowing,' assuring pilgrims that Allah rewards every sincere step, drop of sweat, and humble supplication between Safa and Marwah
Because walking is easy
To limit reward to rich people
explanationEn: Surah Al-Baqarah (2:158) closes with 'Fa-man tatawwa'a khayran fa-inna Allaha Shakirun Alim'—reminding every tired pilgrim that Allah appreciates even the smallest sincere effort.

questionEn: What historical gate on the eastern/southeastern side of the Mataf did the Prophet ﷺ exit through after praying at Maqam Ibrahim to ascend Mount Safa?
optionsEn: Bab al-Fath
Bab al-Umrah
Bab al-Safa
Bab al-Wada'
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated in Sahih Muslim (1218): 'Then he went out through the gate (Bab al-Safa) to Al-Safa, and as he neared Al-Safa he recited: Inna as-Safa wal-Marwata min sha'a'irillah.'

questionEn: When standing on Mount Safa or Mount Marwah today on the upper floors where the Kaaba wall is blocked from direct view by interior columns, how should a pilgrim orient for dua?
optionsEn: Look straight up at the ceiling
Face backward toward the eastern street
Skip the dua completely if the Kaaba isn't visible
Face the direction of the Kaaba (guided by Qiblah signs and floor geometry), raise open palms, and supplicate sincerely
explanationEn: Seeing the Kaaba from Safa was done by the Prophet ﷺ in ORDER to face the Qiblah during dua; even when modern columns block line-of-sight on certain tiers, facing the Kaaba's direction fulfills the Sunnah.

questionEn: How many times did the Prophet ﷺ repeat the cycle of Takbir, Tahlil ('La ilaha illAllahu wahdahu...'), and personal dua each time he stood on Safa or Marwah?
optionsEn: Three times—making lengthy personal dua in the two intervals between the three recitations
Once for two seconds
Ten times without personal dua
Forty times
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) noted: 'He said this three times, supplicating to Allah in between,' spending meaningful moments in heartfelt personal conversation with Allah atop each hill.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim walks at a calm normal pace through the green-lit zone in Al-Mas'a instead of jogging (for instance, due to age, tiredness, or accompanying family)?
optionsEn: Their Sa'i is invalid
Their Sa'i is 100% valid with no penalty whatsoever, as jogging between the green markers is a recommended Sunnah for able men, not an obligation
They must pay a fidyah sheep
They must add an 8th lap
explanationEn: Jogging between the two green markers is a Sunnah for men who are able without harming others or abandoning weaker family members; walking calmly is completely valid.

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) say regarding jogging in Batn al-Mas'il: 'Were I to walk, I would walk, and were I to jog, I have seen the Messenger of Allah ﷺ jog'?
optionsEn: Ordering women to jog
Forbidding anyone from jogging
Confirming that jogging through the valley dip is an authentic Prophetic Sunnah, while walking is also permissible
Moving the green markers to Mina
explanationEn: Early narrations from Umar and Ibn Umar (RA) show the Companions cherished following the Prophet's ﷺ brisk pace in Batn al-Wadi while recognizing its status as a Sunnah.

questionEn: Which two historic water sources sustained Makkah across centuries before modern desalination—one inside the Mataf and one channeled from Wadi Nu'man/Hunayn?
optionsEn: Only rainwater barrels
The Nile and Euphrates
Lake Tiberias and Barada
The miraculous well of Zamzam inside Al-Haram, and the historic Ain Zubaydah aqueduct built by Queen Zubaydah
explanationEn: While Zamzam has always been the blessed spiritual well of Al-Haram, Queen Zubaydah bint Ja'far (wife of Harun al-Rashid) funded the monumental Ain Zubaydah stone aqueduct to supply Makkah and Arafat with abundant water.

questionEn: When Queen Zubaydah's chief engineer warned her that carving the water canal through Makkah's rocky mountains would cost a fortune, what famous reply did she give?
optionsEn: 'Carry out the work even if every single pickaxe strike costs a dinar of gold!'
'Cancel the project immediately'
'Build it only halfway'
'Tax the pilgrims to pay for it'
explanationEn: Selling her own estates and jewels, Queen Zubaydah funded the ~30+ km masonry aqueduct from Wadi Nu'man/Hunayn to Arafat, Muzdalifah, Mina, and Makkah, saving generations of pilgrims from thirst.

questionEn: What did scholars report seeing in a dream after Queen Zubaydah passed away, asking how Allah had treated her?
optionsEn: Because of her palaces in Baghdad
That Allah forgave her and honored her because of the first cups of water pilgrims drank from Ain Zubaydah on the road to Makkah
Because of her silk clothes
Because of her army
explanationEn: Providing water (Saqy al-Ma')—especially to Allah's pilgrim guests in sterile desert valleys—ranks among the greatest ongoing charities (Sadaqah Jariyah) in Islam.

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ say 'The best charity is giving water to drink (Saqy al-Ma')'—a virtue historically embodied by Zamzam Siqayah in Makkah?
optionsEn: Because food is disliked
Because water costs nothing
Because water is the essence of life ('And We made from water every living thing', 21:30), especially in hot pilgrimage lands
Only in winter
explanationEn: Narrated by Sa'd ibn Ubadah and Ibn Abbas (RA) in Sunan Abi Dawud and Ibn Majah, giving water to the thirsty—epitomized in Makkah's Siqayah—is among the most beloved charities to Allah.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 1679 & Sunan Ibn Majah 3684

questionEn: Who famously asked the Prophet ﷺ during the Farewell Hajj: 'O Messenger of Allah, my mother died; what charity is best for her?' and was told: 'Water!'?
optionsEn: Mu'awiyah
Abu Lahab
Suhail ibn Amr
Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA)
explanationEn: Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA) dug a well and dedicated its water to his deceased mother's soul after the Prophet ﷺ recommended water as the finest ongoing charity.

questionEn: What did Ibn Abbas (RA) call Zamzam water when asked about its nicknames in prophetic tradition?
optionsEn: 'Shabba'ah' (the Satisfier of hunger) and 'Ni'mal-'Awn 'alal-'Iyal' (a wonderful helper in nourishing one's family)
'Al-Bahr' (the Ocean)
'Al-Thalj' (the Ice)
'Al-Malih' (the Salty)
explanationEn: Recorded in Musannaf Abd al-Razzaq and Musnad Ahmad from Ibn Abbas (RA), Zamzam was affectionately called Shabba'ah because it satisfies hunger and nourishes families.

questionEn: According to a narration in Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir by al-Tabarani from Ibn Abbas (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ call the best water on the face of the earth?
optionsEn: 'Water from melting snow'
'The best water on the face of the earth is the water of Zamzam; in it is nourishing food and healing from illness'
'Rainwater from Rome'
'River water in Persia'
explanationEn: Authenticated by al-Albani and classical hadith masters from Ibn Abbas (RA), the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Khayru ma'in 'ala wajhil-ardi ma'u Zamzam; fihi ta'amun min al-tu'mi wa shifa'un min al-suqm.'

questionEn: When was the underground basement entrance to the Zamzam wellhead beneath the Mataf finally closed to pedestrian traffic to give 100% of the surface courtyard to Tawaf?
optionsEn: In 1925 CE
In 1200 CE
In 1424 AH (2003 CE), when the subterranean stairwells in the middle of the Mataf were sealed and paved over with cool white marble
It is still an open staircase in the Mataf today
explanationEn: From the 1960s to 2003, pilgrims descended stairs in the Mataf to a basement viewing gallery around the Zamzam well; in 2003 those stairs were covered over to eliminate a major bottleneck in the Mataf.

questionEn: Before the 2003 sealing of the basement stairs in the Mataf, why were separate men's and women's underground staircases leading down to the Zamzam well removed?
optionsEn: Because lighting failed
Because the stairs were made of wood
Because the water stopped flowing
Because the stair railings right in the middle of the eastern Mataf obstructed the flow of tens of thousands of Tawaf pilgrims per hour
explanationEn: Removing the two wide stairwell openings right in front of the Kaaba door and Maqam Ibrahim instantly freed up prime Mataf space while automated pumps delivered Zamzam to every corner of the mosque.

questionEn: Where can visitors view historical models, antique Zamzam buckets, pulleys, and well inscriptions today in Makkah?
optionsEn: At the Exhibition of the Two Holy Mosques Architecture in Umm al-Jud (near the Kiswah Complex)
Inside Cave Thawr
On top of Mount Arafat
Inside the Kaaba
explanationEn: The Exhibition of the Two Holy Mosques Architecture displays the historic bronze/marble Zamzam well collar, antique pulley wheels, copper vessels, and historical inscriptions.
reference: Exhibition of the Two Holy Mosques Architecture

questionEn: What was the 'Kharazat al-Bi'r' (the historic marble wellhead collar of Zamzam) now preserved in the Two Holy Mosques Museum?
optionsEn: A golden crown
The circular carved marble parapet that surrounded the mouth of the Zamzam well when water was drawn up with ropes and buckets
A wooden bridge
A stone from Mount Sinai
explanationEn: The historic marble well-curb—grooved deeply around its inner rim by centuries of bucket ropes—is preserved as a priceless artifact in Makkah's Two Holy Mosques Exhibition.
reference: Exhibition of the Two Holy Mosques Architecture

questionEn: Why does the preserved marble collar (Kharazah) of the old Zamzam wellhead have deep vertical grooves worn into its stone rim?
optionsEn: From rainwater erosion
From decorative chisel carving
From centuries of hemp ropes pulling up leather and copper buckets of Zamzam water day and night for pilgrims
From sword strikes
explanationEn: Those deep rope-grooves worn into solid marble bear silent witness to countless generations of pilgrims whose thirst was quenched from Ismail's (AS) well.
reference: Exhibition of the Two Holy Mosques Architecture

questionEn: Who were the traditional 'Zamazimah' (guilds of Zamzam water servers) in Makkah's history?
optionsEn: Soldiers guarding Jeddah
Camel breeders from Najd
Silk weavers from Syria
Licensed Makkan families and stewards who drew, cooled in porous clay jars (dawraq), scented with mastic, and served Zamzam to pilgrims in Al-Haram and their lodgings
explanationEn: For centuries the honorable Unified Zamazimah Office (Maktab al-Zamazimah al-Muwahhad) organized the distribution of Zamzam water to pilgrims arriving in Makkah—a service modernized today.
reference: History of Makkah Guilds & Maktab al-Zamazimah

questionEn: How did traditional Makkan Zamazimah cool Zamzam water naturally before electricity and refrigeration?
optionsEn: By storing it in porous earthenware jugs (dawariq/qulal) placed in breezy lattice windows (rawashin), where natural evaporation kept the water refreshingly cool
By importing icebergs from Europe
By burying it under hot sand
They served it boiling hot
explanationEn: Porous clay vessels (dawraq) sweat microscopic moisture that evaporates in Makkah's dry breeze, naturally chilling the water inside.

questionEn: What continues the legacy of the historic Zamazimah Guild in modern Makkah today?
optionsEn: It was abolished with no replacement
The Zamazimah Company (and Haramain water distribution services), which delivers millions of sealed Zamzam bottles directly to pilgrims' hotels and residences in Makkah
It now sells carpets
It operates only in Cairo
explanationEn: Today the Zamazimah institution distributes millions of hygienic bottled Zamzam packages to pilgrims at checkpoints, hotels, and departure terminals.

questionEn: When a pilgrim walks from the Mataf after praying behind Maqam Ibrahim toward Mount Safa, what water station is immediately available along the way?
optionsEn: Coffee stalls
Only saltwater taps
Dedicated Zamzam marble drinking fountains and insulated cylinders allowing pilgrims to follow the Sunnah of drinking Zamzam before starting Sa'i
No water is available near Safa
explanationEn: Both around the perimeter of the Mataf and along every level of Al-Mas'a, Zamzam stations allow pilgrims to drink and refresh themselves just as the Prophet ﷺ did before ascending Safa.

questionEn: What is the ruling if a pilgrim performs 6 laps of Sa'i and mistakenly stops at Safa thinking they finished 7 laps, then remembers shortly afterward?
optionsEn: They must fast three days
Stopping at Safa is valid as Lap 7
They must redo Tawaf
Since Lap 6 always ends at Safa and Lap 7 always ends at Marwah, realizing they stopped at Safa proves they only did 6 laps—so they simply return and walk the 7th lap from Safa to Marwah
explanationEn: One of the easiest built-in checks in Sa'i is that odd laps (1, 3, 5, 7) ALWAYS end at Marwah and even laps (2, 4, 6) ALWAYS end at Safa; ending at Safa is an unmistakable sign of an even lap.

questionEn: How can a pilgrim easily keep track of odd vs even laps during Sa'i without getting confused?
optionsEn: Every odd-numbered lap (1, 3, 5, 7) goes from Safa to Marwah, and every even-numbered lap (2, 4, 6) returns from Marwah to Safa
Odd laps go Marwah to Safa
All seven laps start at Safa
Count by hours instead of laps
explanationEn: Remembering 'Odd = toward Marwah (1, 3, 5, 7); Even = toward Safa (2, 4, 6)' eliminates counting confusion during Sa'i.

questionEn: What happens if a pilgrim is completely unsure whether they are on Lap 5 or Lap 7 as they walk toward Marwah?
optionsEn: Assume it is Lap 7 and leave
Take the lower number they are certain of (Lap 5), complete Lap 6 back to Safa, and finish Lap 7 to Marwah
Start over from Lap 1
Ask a stranger to guess for them
explanationEn: Applying the juristic maxim 'Certainty is not overruled by doubt,' one builds on the lesser certain count (5) and completes the remaining two laps.

questionEn: During the pre-Islamic period, why did some pilgrims from the Ansar feel reluctant to walk between Safa and Marwah even after accepting Islam?
optionsEn: Because Quraysh charged a toll on Marwah
Because they preferred walking in Madinah
Because in Jahiliyyah they had chanted Talbiyah for the idol Manat near Qudayd and used to avoid Safa and Marwah, so they asked the Prophet ﷺ if walking there was a pre-Islamic carryover
Because they disliked climbing hills
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (1643), Aishah (RA) explained that those who had venerated Manat at Al-Mushallal in Jahiliyyah hesitated to perform Sa'i until Allah revealed Surah Al-Baqarah 2:158.

questionEn: Where did the pre-Islamic idol 'Manat' stand that caused certain tribes to avoid Safa and Marwah before Surah 2:158 was revealed?
optionsEn: In Taif
Inside Hijr Ismail
On top of Mount Arafat
At Al-Mushallal near Qudayd on the Red Sea coast between Makkah and Madinah
explanationEn: Manat stood on the coast at Al-Mushallal near Qudayd; tribes who entered Ihram for it avoided Safa and Marwah until Islam restored the pure Abrahamic rite of Sa'i.

questionEn: What is the juristic ruling on Sa'i between Safa and Marwah in Hajj and Umrah according to the Shafi'i, Maliki, and Hanbali schools?
optionsEn: It is an essential pillar (Rukn) of both Hajj and Umrah, without which the pilgrimage is not complete (while Hanafis classify it as Wajib)
It is merely a light recommendation
It is required only for women
It is required only for Makkah residents
explanationEn: Based on the Prophet's ﷺ command and Aishah's (RA) statement 'Allah does not complete the Hajj or Umrah of anyone who does not perform Sa'i between them,' the majority hold Sa'i to be a pillar (Rukn).

questionEn: Which hadith reported by Habiba bint Abi Tajrah (RA)—who watched the Prophet ﷺ perform Sa'i from the house of Abu Husayn—describes his vigorous stride in Batn al-Wadi?
optionsEn: She saw him walking slowly with a cane
She saw his lower garment (izar) whirling around his knees from the vigor of his running while he said: 'Perform Sa'i, for Allah has prescribed Sa'i for you!'
She saw him sitting on Marwah for an hour
She saw him doing Sa'i at midnight only
explanationEn: Habiba bint Abi Tajrah (RA), a Makkan companion watching from a house overlooking Al-Mas'a, vividly described the Prophet's ﷺ energetic stride through the valley dip.

questionEn: Why does the ground floor of Al-Mas'a incline gently upward as you approach the ends of Mount Safa and Mount Marwah?
optionsEn: To hide escalators underneath
To drain water toward the middle
Because it follows the natural rising bedrock slopes of the two sacred hills at the southern and northern ends of the corridor
Because of a construction error
explanationEn: Even after paving in cool marble, the ground floor rises up the natural slopes of Safa and Marwah at either end, culminating at the preserved exposed rock domes.

questionEn: How is the exposed bedrock of Mount Safa protected today while remaining visible to pilgrims?
optionsEn: Hidden behind a brick wall
Covered completely with black Kiswah cloth
Submerged in a pool of water
Enclosed beneath a circular glass/open-view barrier under a high ornate dome at the southern end of Al-Mas'a
explanationEn: At the southern terminus of Al-Mas'a beneath the grand Safa dome, the dark natural bedrock of Mount Safa is preserved inside a protective enclosure so pilgrims see the historic hill without slipping on rough boulders.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ first arrived in Makkah for his Farewell Pilgrimage on the 4th of Dhul-Hijjah 10 AH, in what sequence did he perform the rites inside Al-Masjid al-Haram?
optionsEn: He entered the mosque, performed 7 circuits of Tawaf around the Kaaba, prayed 2 rak'ahs behind Maqam Ibrahim, drank Zamzam, and then performed 7 laps of Sa'i between Safa and Marwah
He did Sa'i first and Tawaf two days later
He went straight to Arafat without visiting the Kaaba
He stayed in Mina for four days first
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah's (RA) long hadith in Sahih Muslim (1218) preserves this exact, step-by-step prophetic sequence inside Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ command his companions who had NOT brought sacrificial animals (hady) with them after they finished Sa'i at Mount Marwah on the 4th/5th of Dhul-Hijjah?
optionsEn: To stay in Ihram for a whole month
To shorten their hair and exit Ihram completely, converting their pilgrimage into Hajj al-Tamattu' until the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah
To return to Madinah immediately
To fast for ten days
explanationEn: Standing at Mount Marwah after Sa'i, the Prophet ﷺ instructed every companion without a sacrificial animal to make their Tawaf and Sa'i a complete Umrah and exit Ihram comfortably (Hajj al-Tamattu').

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ himself remain in Ihram after finishing Sa'i at Marwah during the Farewell Pilgrimage while ordering most companions to exit Ihram?
optionsEn: Because he did not perform Sa'i
Because he forgot to bring scissors
Because he had brought his sacrificial animals (hady) with him from Dhul-Hulayfah (performing Qiran), and a pilgrim with hady remains in Ihram until the 10th of Dhul-Hijjah
Because he lived in Makkah
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ explained at Marwah: 'Had I known beforehand what I came to know later, I would not have brought the sacrificial animals and would have made it an Umrah [Tamattu'] with you!'

questionEn: Which companion stood up at Mount Marwah and asked the Prophet ﷺ: 'O Messenger of Allah, is this [making Umrah in the Hajj months] for this year of ours only, or forever?'
optionsEn: Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
Abu Sufyan (RA)
Salman al-Farsi (RA)
Suraqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum (RA)
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim (1218), Suraqah ibn Malik (RA) asked this at the foot of Marwah; the Prophet ﷺ interlocked his fingers and replied: 'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Resurrection! No, rather forever and ever!'

questionEn: What gesture did the Prophet ﷺ make at Mount Marwah when answering Suraqah ibn Malik (RA) about the permanent permissibility of Umrah during the Hajj months?
optionsEn: He interlocked the fingers of his two hands together and said, 'Umrah has entered into Hajj until the Day of Resurrection—forever and ever!'
He pointed toward Yemen
He drew a line in the sand
He raised his staff thrice
explanationEn: Interlocking his fingers at Marwah, the Prophet ﷺ permanently abolished the Jahiliyyah taboo against performing Umrah in Dhul-Qi'dah and Dhul-Hijjah.

questionEn: When Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) arrived in Makkah from Yemen during the Farewell Pilgrimage, where did he find Fatima (RA) having already exited her Umrah Ihram?
optionsEn: At Mount Arafat
In their lodging in Makkah after she had completed Tawaf, Sa'i between Safa and Marwah, and trimmed her hair as the Prophet ﷺ had commanded
In Madinah
Inside Cave Thawr
explanationEn: Fatima (RA) followed her father's ﷺ command at Marwah to exit Ihram after Umrah, while Ali (RA) remained in Ihram because, like the Prophet ﷺ, he had brought sacrificial animals from Yemen.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ ask Ali (RA) upon his arrival in Makkah from Yemen regarding how Ali had formulated his intention (niyyah) for Ihram?
optionsEn: Ali had intended only a visit to Taif
Ali had not entered Ihram at all
Ali said: 'I said: O Allah, I enter Ihram with the same intention as Your Prophet!'—so the Prophet ﷺ told him to remain in Ihram and share in the sacrificial animals
The Prophet ﷺ told him to cancel his Hajj
explanationEn: Because Ali (RA) had tied his intention to the Prophet's ﷺ own Qiran Ihram and brought sacrificial camels from Yemen, the Prophet ﷺ instructed him to stay in Ihram and shared the hady with him.

questionEn: How many sacrificial camels did the Prophet ﷺ and Ali (RA) bring together to Makkah during the Farewell Pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Five hundred horses
Ten camels
Three sheep
One hundred camels in total (63 slaughtered by the Prophet's ﷺ own hand—matching the years of his life—and the remaining 37 by Ali RA)
explanationEn: Jabir (RA) narrated in Sahih Muslim (1218) that the total sacrificial camels numbered 100; the Prophet ﷺ slaughtered 63 with his own hand and gave the spear to Ali (RA) to slaughter the remaining 37.

questionEn: What did the Prophet ﷺ command be done with a piece of meat from every single one of those 100 sacrificial camels?
optionsEn: A piece from each camel was placed into a single cooking pot and cooked, and both he and Ali (RA) ate from its meat and drank from its broth—while distributing the rest to the poor without paying the butcher from the sacrifice itself
They were all left untouched
They were sold in the market
Only the skins were kept
explanationEn: By cooking a piece from each of the 100 camels in one pot and drinking the broth, the Prophet ﷺ partook of every single sacrificial animal in fulfillment of Surah Al-Hajj (22:28: 'So eat from them and feed the needy').

questionEn: Why did the Prophet ﷺ forbid Ali (RA) from giving the butcher any portion of the sacrificial meat or skin as his wage, paying the butcher from their own funds instead?
optionsEn: Because butchers are forbidden to eat meat
Because the sacrificial animal (hady/udhiyah) is offered wholly for Allah; its meat and skin may be gifted or given in charity, but never used as commercial payment for labor
Because skins must be burned
Only in Madinah
explanationEn: Ali (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (1717) and Muslim (1317): 'The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered me to oversee his sacrificial camels and to distribute all their meat, skins, and coverings in charity, and not to give the butcher anything from them as wages.'

questionEn: What is the relationship between the floor level of the Mataf and the floor level of the ground-floor Mas'a today?
optionsEn: One must take a bus between them
They are separated by a 5-kilometer highway
They are connected by wide, smooth marble corridors and ramps on the eastern side, allowing pilgrims to walk seamlessly from Maqam Ibrahim and Zamzam straight to Mount Safa
They are on opposite sides of Makkah
explanationEn: The eastern colonnade directly links the Mataf courtyard with the southern Safa entrance of Al-Mas'a, preserving the continuous walk from Tawaf into Sa'i.

questionEn: Why are there air-conditioning vents built directly into the columns and ceilings along the entire 394-meter length of Al-Mas'a?
optionsEn: Only for decoration
To heat the corridor in July
To blow sand across the floor
To keep the enclosed multi-story gallery cool and well-ventilated while tens of thousands exert physical effort walking 2.8 kilometers across seven laps
explanationEn: Cooled chilled-water air conditioning piped from massive central cooling stations outside the Haram keeps Al-Mas'a at a comfortable temperature year-round.

questionEn: Where are the massive central air-conditioning chiller plants that cool Al-Masjid al-Haram and Al-Mas'a located so their noise and exhaust never disturb worshipers?
optionsEn: In remote utility stations (such as Shamiya and Ajyad) outside the mosque, piping chilled water underground into Al-Haram's air handlers
On top of the Kaaba roof
Inside Hijr Ismail
On Mount Safa's rock
