explanationEn: Qusayy ibn Kilab built Dar al-Nadwah just north of the Sanctuary in Makkah; no war was declared, no trade caravan dispatched, and no major civic decision made by Quraysh except by consultation within it.

questionEn: In the civic administration of Makkah established by Qusayy ibn Kilab, what was the specific function of the office of 'Al-Rifadah'?
optionsEn: Inspecting the weights and measures in the market of Dhu al-Majaz
Providing food and hospitality to needy pilgrims visiting Makkah through a collective contribution from Quraysh
Leading the summer trade caravan to the markets of Busra in Syria
Guarding the mountain passes leading into Makkah from raiders
explanationEn: Qusayy instituted Al-Rifadah, reminding Quraysh that the pilgrims are the guests of Allah and worthy of generosity, so Quraysh contributed annually from their wealth to prepare food for poor pilgrims in Makkah and Mina.

questionEn: What was the civic duty of 'Al-Siqayah' in the traditional administration of Makkah?
optionsEn: Maintaining the boundary stones on the roads to Ta'if
Announcing the sighting of the new moon from Mount Abu Qubays
Supplying fresh water and sweetened date or raisin beverages in leather cisterns for pilgrims in Makkah
Forging armor and swords for the defense of the city
explanationEn: Al-Siqayah was the honorable office of providing water—often sweetened with raisins (nabidh) or dates due to the brackishness of many early wells—to pilgrims visiting Makkah.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Sahih Muslim 1318

questionEn: In the division of Makkan civic offices after Qusayy ibn Kilab, what did the office of 'Al-Liwa'' represent?
optionsEn: The duty of lighting beacons on the hills of Muzdalifah
The right to collect market taxes during the season of 'Ukaz
The custody of the treaties written on leather scrolls
The right to tie and present the official war banner of Quraysh when an army was mobilized
explanationEn: Al-Liwa' was the standard-bearing office in Makkah: the banner of Quraysh was tied only by its holder when unanimous agreement was reached for a military expedition.

questionEn: When the descendants of Abd Manaf and the descendants of Abd al-Dar disputed over the civic offices of Makkah, how did the clan of Abd Manaf seal their allianceknown as 'Al-Mutayyabun' (The Perfumed Ones)?
optionsEn: By dipping their hands into a bowl of perfume placed near the Sanctuary and wiping them on the wall
By burning incense atop Mount Thawr for three consecutive nights
By exchanging silk garments imported from Damascus
By planting frankincense trees from Yemen in the courtyard of Dar al-Nadwah
explanationEn: Umm Hakim bint Abd al-Muttalib notes in Makkan history that the clans backing the sons of Abd Manaf dipped their hands into a bowl of perfume (tib) and wiped the Kaaba, earning the name Al-Mutayyabun ('The Perfumed Ones'), before reaching a peaceful compromise sharing the offices.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: What were the two main shares decided in the peaceful compromise between the sons of Abd Manaf and the sons of Abd al-Dar regarding Makkah's civic duties?
optionsEn: The sons of Abd Manaf took all military posts, while Abd al-Dar moved permanently to Ta'if
The sons of Abd Manaf received Al-Siqayah and Al-Rifadah, while the sons of Abd al-Dar retained the Hijabah (keys), Liwa' (banner), and Nadwah
The offices were rotated every lunar month among all twelve clans of Quraysh
Both clans handed all offices over to the tribe of Thaqif for arbitration
explanationEn: To avoid bloodshed in Makkah, the two factions agreed that the sons of Abd Manaf would hold Al-Siqayah (water supply) and Al-Rifadah (feeding pilgrims), while the sons of Abd al-Dar kept the Hijabah, Liwa', and Dar al-Nadwah.

questionEn: Why did Amr ibn Abd Manaf, the great-grandfather of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, earn the famous name 'Hashim' in Makkah?
optionsEn: Because he shattered the rock blocking the southern pass to Yemen
Because he forged the first iron swords used by the horsemen of Quraysh
Because during a severe drought in Makkah, he crumbled bread (hashama al-tharid) into meat broth to feed the hungry inhabitants and pilgrims
Because he broke the trade monopoly of the Lakhmid kings of Hira
explanationEn: His birth name was Amr, and he was called Hashim ('The Crumbler') because during a year of famine in Makkah he brought flour from Syria, slaughtered camels, and crumbled bread into broth (tharid) to feed the people and pilgrims.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Tarikh al-Tabari

questionEn: Which Surah of the Qur'an explicitly reminds Quraysh of Allah's favor in granting them familiarity and safe passage for their winter and summer trade caravans from Makkah?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Humazah (Surah 104)
Surah Al-Balad (Surah 90)
Surah Al-Takathur (Surah 102)
Surah Quraysh (Surah 106)
explanationEn: Surah Quraysh (106:1-4) reminds the people of Makkah of Allah's blessing in securing their winter and summer journeys (rihlat al-shita'i wal-sayf) and commands them to worship the Lord of this House Who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear.

questionEn: In the seasonal trade system established by Hashim ibn Abd Manaf for Makkah, what were the respective destinations of the winter caravan and the summer caravan?
optionsEn: Yemen in the winter and Sham (Greater Syria) in the summer
Abyssinia in the winter and Bahrain in the summer
Egypt in the winter and Persia in the summer
Oman in the winter and Najd in the summer
explanationEn: Because Makkah lay in an arid valley, Hashim instituted two regular commercial journeys: south to the warm lands of Yemen in winter, and north to the cooler fertile markets of Sham (Gaza/Busra) in summer.

questionEn: In which city did Hashim ibn Abd Manaf pass away while leading a summer trade caravan from Makkah?
optionsEn: Alexandria in Egypt
Gaza in Palestine (Sham)
Sana'a in Yemen
Hira in Iraq
explanationEn: Hashim ibn Abd Manaf died in Gaza while on a trade journey to Sham, and his younger brother Al-Muttalib succeeded him in holding the offices of Siqayah and Rifadah in Makkah.

questionEn: How did Shaybah ibn Hashim acquire the famous name 'Abd al-Muttalib' when he first arrived in Makkah from Yathrib (Madinah)?
optionsEn: He was ransomed by Al-Muttalib from a Bedouin raid near Badr
His mother Salma bint Amr named him after a revered scholar of Yathrib
When he rode into Makkah behind his uncle Al-Muttalib, the Makkans mistook the youth for Al-Muttalib's newly acquired servant ('Abd al-Muttalib')
He took an oath at Dar al-Nadwah to serve his uncle for ten years
explanationEn: When Al-Muttalib ibn Abd Manaf brought his young nephew Shaybah from Yathrib to Makkah wearing travel-worn clothes, the people of Makkah exclaimed, 'This is Abd al-Muttalib (the servant of Al-Muttalib)!' Even after Al-Muttalib clarified that Shaybah was his nephew, the name remained with him.

questionEn: What structure did Abraha al-Ashram, the Abyssinian viceroy in Yemen, build in Sana'a with the explicit aim of diverting the Arab pilgrimage away from Makkah?
optionsEn: A stone fortress named Ghumdan
A commercial marketplace named Suq Ma'rib
A monumental dam named Sadd Himyar
A grand cathedral named Al-Qullays
explanationEn: Abraha built a lavishly decorated cathedral in Sana'a called Al-Qullays and wrote to the Negus of Abyssinia that he would not rest until he diverted the pilgrimage of the Arabs from Makkah to it.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Tafsir al-Tabari on Surah 105

questionEn: During Abraha's march against Makkah in the Year of the Elephant (c. 570 CE), what was the name of the lead elephant that knelt down and refused to advance toward the Sacred Sanctuary?
optionsEn: Mahmud
Ya'fur
Duldul
Qaswa
explanationEn: When Abraha prepared to enter Makkah from the valley of Muhassir, his lead war elephant, named Mahmud, knelt down whenever directed toward the Haram of Makkah, yet ran briskly whenever turned toward Yemen, north, or east.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Raheeq Al-Makhtum

questionEn: Which captive Arab guide took hold of the elephant Mahmud's ear outside Makkah and whispered to it: 'Kneel, Mahmud, or return soundly from whence you came, for you are in Allah's Sacred Land'?
optionsEn: Suhail ibn Amr al-Amiri
Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khat'ami
Dhu al-Kala' al-Himyari
Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi
explanationEn: Nufayl ibn Habib al-Khat'ami stepped up to the elephant Mahmud, held its ear, and told it to kneel or return because it was in the Sacred Land of Allah; immediately the elephant knelt and refused to march toward Makkah.

questionEn: When Abd al-Muttalib met Abraha outside Makkah and asked only for the return of his 200 seized camels, what famous reply did he give when Abraha expressed surprise that he did not plead for the Kaaba?
optionsEn: 'The tribes of Najd and Kindah are already marching to defend the House'
'We have hidden the treasures of the Sanctuary in the caves of Mount Thawr'
'I am the lord of the camels, and the House has a Lord Who will protect it'
'Our council at Dar al-Nadwah forbids speaking of the Sanctuary to strangers'
explanationEn: Abd al-Muttalib replied with memorable certainty: 'I am the lord (owner) of the camels, whereas the House has a Lord Who will protect it (Inna lil-bayti Rabban yahmih).'
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Fil (105:1-5), how did Allah destroy Abraha's army as it prepared to attack Makkah?
optionsEn: By sending a sandstorm that lasted forty days across the Tihamah plain
By causing a sudden flash flood from Mount Arafat that swept them into the Red Sea
By opening a chasm in the earth that swallowed their camp at Tan'im
By sending flocks of birds (Tayran Ababil) that pelted them with stones of baked clay (Hijaratin min Sijjil), leaving them like eaten straw
explanationEn: Surah Al-Fil (105:3-5) recounts: 'And He sent against them birds in flocks, striking them with stones of hard clay, and He made them like eaten straw.'

questionEn: In which year, day of the week, and lunar month was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ born in Makkah?
optionsEn: On a Monday in the month of Rabi' al-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant
On a Friday in the month of Rajab ten years before the Year of the Elephant
On a Wednesday in the month of Sha'ban five years after the Year of the Elephant
On a Thursday in the month of Muharram during the Fijar War
explanationEn: When asked about fasting on Mondays, the Prophet ﷺ said, 'That is the day on which I was born and the day on which I received revelation' (Sahih Muslim 1162), and scholars agree his birth in Makkah took place in Rabi' al-Awwal in the Year of the Elephant.

questionEn: Who carried the newborn Prophet ﷺ into the Sacred Sanctuary in Makkah, thanked Allah, and gave him the name 'Muhammad' so that he would be praised in heaven and on earth?
optionsEn: His paternal uncle Abu Talib
His grandfather Abd al-Muttalib
The Hanif scholar Waraqah ibn Nawfal
His maternal uncle Al-Aswad ibn Wahb
explanationEn: Since his father Abdullah had passed away before his birth, his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib rejoiced at the news, carried his grandson into the Sanctuary in Makkah, prayed for him, and named him Muhammad.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Dala'il al-Nubuwwah by Al-Bayhaqi

questionEn: Before Halimah al-Sa'diyyah of Banu Sa'd arrived in Makkah, who was the first woman after his mother Aminah to nurse the infant Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: Fatimah bint Asad
Shayma bint al-Harith
Thuwaybah, the freedwoman of Abu Lahab
Umm Ayman (Barakah al-Habashiyyah)
explanationEn: Thuwaybah, the freedwoman of Abu Lahab, nursed the infant Prophet ﷺ in Makkah before Halimah al-Sa'diyyah took him to the desert of Banu Sa'd (as she had also nursed Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib and Abu Salamah).

questionEn: What humble occupation did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ mention he practiced in his youth for the people of Makkah in common with every prophet sent by Allah?
optionsEn: Breaking wild horses in the valley of Marr al-Zahran
Carving stone inscriptions for the merchants of Dar al-Nadwah
Weaving striped Yemeni cloaks in the lower quarter of Makkah
Herding sheep for the people of Makkah for a few qirats
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Allah never sent a prophet who did not herd sheep.' His companions asked, 'And you?' He replied, 'Yes, I used to herd them for the people of Makkah for some qirats.'

questionEn: Why were the pre-Islamic battles fought between Quraysh (with Kinanah) and Qays 'Aylan during the Prophet's ﷺ youth called 'Harb al-Fijar' (The Sacrilegious Wars)?
optionsEn: Because they violated the sanctity of the Sacred Months and the sanctity of Makkah
Because both sides used poisoned arrows imported from Abyssinia
Because they burned the palm groves of Yathrib and Khaybar
Because they refused to bury the fallen warriors on the battlefield
explanationEn: They were called the Fijar ('Sacrilegious/Transgressive') Wars because the combatants transgressed (fajaru) the inviolable sanctity of the Sacred Months during which fighting was strictly prohibited among the Arabs.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Raheeq Al-Makhtum

questionEn: What incident in Makkah directly triggered the formation of 'Hilf al-Fudul' (The Pact of the Virtuous)?
optionsEn: A dispute broke out over who should hold the keys of Dar al-Nadwah
A merchant from the Yemeni tribe of Zabid was denied payment for his goods by Al-'As ibn Wa'il in Makkah and cried out for help near the Sanctuary
A flood destroyed the marketplace of 'Ukaz outside Ta'if
A caravan belonging to Banu Makhzum was plundered by Bedouins near Badr
explanationEn: When a Yemeni merchant from Zabid sold goods in Makkah to Al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, who refused to pay him, the wronged stranger climbed Mount Abu Qubays at dawn and recited verses appealing to the honor of Quraysh, prompting Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib and honorable clans to form Hilf al-Fudul.

questionEn: In whose house in Makkah did the clans of Banu Hashim, Banu al-Muttalib, Banu Asad, Banu Zuhrah, and Banu Taym gather to swear the oath of Hilf al-Fudul?
optionsEn: The house of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb
The house of Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam
The house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an al-Taymi
The house of Utbah ibn Rabi'ah
explanationEn: The elders and youths of these five clans gathered in the house of the respected senior chief Abdullah ibn Jud'an al-Taymi in Makkah, where they pledged before Allah to stand with any wronged person in Makkah—native or stranger—until his right was restored.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Sunan al-Kubra by Al-Bayhaqi

questionEn: How did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ later speak of the Hilf al-Fudul pact that he had witnessed in his youth in Makkah?
optionsEn: He forbade his companions from mentioning any pre-Islamic pacts of Quraysh
He stated that it applied only to members of the tribe of Banu Taym
He declared it abrogated because it took place before the revelation of the Qur'an
He said he would not exchange witnessing it for the finest red camels, and if called to such a pact in Islam he would readily respond
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ praised Hilf al-Fudul after Islam: 'I witnessed a pact in the house of Abdullah ibn Jud'an that I would not love to exchange for red camels; and if I were called to it in Islam, I would respond.'

questionEn: Before receiving revelation at age forty, by what two titles of upright character was the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ universally known among the people of Makkah?
optionsEn: Al-Sadiq (The Truthful) and Al-Amin (The Trustworthy)
Al-Khatib (The Orator) and Al-Sha'ir (The Poet)
Al-Mujammi' (The Unifier) and Al-Sayyid (The Chieftain)
Al-Faruq (The Criterion) and Dhu al-Nurayn (Possessor of Two Lights)
explanationEn: Throughout Makkah, prior to prophethood, Muhammad ﷺ was known as Al-Sadiq (The Truthful) and Al-Amin (The Trustworthy), and the people of Makkah deposited their most precious trusts with him.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Sahih al-Bukhari 4770

questionEn: During the first three years of the Prophet's ﷺ mission in Makkah, in whose house at the foot of Mount Safa did the early Muslims secretly gather to learn the Qur'an and pray?
optionsEn: The house of Abu Sufyan ibn Harb in the upper valley
Dar al-Arqam (the house of Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam, RA)
The courtyard of Utbah ibn Rabi'ah near Marwah
Dar al-Nadwah (the council hall of Qusayy ibn Kilab)
explanationEn: Al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam (RA), a young companion from Banu Makhzum, offered his house at the foot of Mount Safa—known as Dar al-Arqam—as the covert educational and spiritual center for the early Muslims in Makkah.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse commanded the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to transition from secret invitation to publicly warning his closest clan relatives in Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Today I have perfected your religion for you' (Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:3)
'Permission to fight is given to those who are fought' (Surah Al-Hajj 22:39)
'And warn your closest kindred' (Surah Al-Shu'ara 26:214)
'Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest' (Surah Al-Fath 48:1)
explanationEn: When Allah revealed 'And warn your closest kindred (Wa-andhir 'ashirataka al-aqrabin)' (Qur'an 26:214), the Prophet ﷺ gathered Banu Abd Manaf and climbed Mount Safa to deliver his first open call in Makkah.

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ climbed Mount Safa in Makkah to proclaim Islam publicly, what traditional Arab warning cry did he call out to summon the clans of Quraysh?
optionsEn: 'Labbaik Allahumma Labbaik!'
'Hayya 'ala al-Falah!'
'Ya Mansur Amit!'
'Ya Sabahah!' (an alert signaling an urgent morning alarm)
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari, Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated that when 'And warn your closest kindred' was revealed, the Prophet ﷺ ascended Mount Safa and called out 'Ya Sabahah!' to gather the clans of Quraysh.

questionEn: How did the assembled people of Quraysh respond at the foot of Mount Safa when the Prophet ﷺ asked whether they would believe him if he told them cavalry were in the valley ready to attack?
optionsEn: 'Yes! We have never experienced anything from you except truthfulness'
'We do not listen to warnings delivered outside the Sacred Months'
'Only if the elders of Dar al-Nadwah confirm the news'
'No, until we send scouts to the hilltops of Tan'im'
explanationEn: Before he even announced his prophetic warning from Mount Safa, the people of Makkah unanimously testified to his lifelong integrity: 'Yes, we have never experienced anything from you but truth (Ma jarrabna 'alayka illa sidqan).'

questionEn: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ angrily interrupted the gathering at Mount Safa by shouting 'May you perish the rest of the day! Was it for this that you gathered us?', prompting the revelation of Surah Al-Masad?
optionsEn: Abu Talib (Abd Manaf ibn Abd al-Muttalib)
Abu Lahab (Abd al-'Uzza ibn Abd al-Muttalib)
Al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib
Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib
explanationEn: Abu Lahab cried out 'Tabban laka sa'ira al-yawm, a-li-hadha jama'tana?' at the foot of Mount Safa, whereupon Allah revealed Surah Al-Masad (111:1-5): 'Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he!'

questionEn: How was Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) tortured in the scorching heat of the valley of Makkah by his master Umayyah ibn Khalaf, and what words did Bilal repeat?
optionsEn: He was locked inside a subterranean granary while repeating 'Sabr, Sabr'
He was chained to the pillars of Dar al-Nadwah while reciting Surah Al-Fath
A heavy boulder was placed on his chest on the burning sand while he repeated 'Ahad, Ahad' ('One, One')
He was exiled to the desert of Najd without water for forty days
explanationEn: Umayyah ibn Khalaf used to bring Bilal (RA) out at midday when the valley floor of Makkah was scorching hot, order a great rock placed on his chest, and demand he renounce Muhammad ﷺ and worship Lat and 'Uzza, while Bilal steadfastly repeated 'Ahad, Ahad' ('One, One').

questionEn: Which companion purchased Bilal ibn Rabah (RA) and several other persecuted enslaved Muslims in Makkah and emancipated them purely for the sake of Allah?
optionsEn: Mu'adh ibn Jabal (RA)
Usayd ibn Hudayr (RA)
Sa'd ibn Mu'adh (RA)
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA)
explanationEn: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) spent generously from his wealth in Makkah to purchase and free persecuted enslaved believers, including Bilal ibn Rabah, Amir ibn Fuhayrah, Umm 'Ubays, and Zanirah (RA), regarding whom verses of Surah Al-Layl (92:17-21) were revealed.

questionEn: What consoling promise did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ give to Yasir, Sumayyah, and Ammar (RA) when he passed by them as they were being tortured in the heat of Makkah?
optionsEn: 'Patience, O family of Yasir! Indeed, your appointed meeting place is Paradise'
'Pay ransom to Banu Makhzum from the treasury of Dar al-Arqam'
'Take up arms immediately, for an army is coming from Yathrib'
'Flee tonight to the mountains of Ta'if and remain hidden there'
explanationEn: Lacking military power in Makkah to physically rescue them from Banu Makhzum, the Prophet ﷺ comforted them with the glad tidings: 'Sabran Ala Yasir! Fa-inna maw'idakum al-Jannah' ('Patience, O family of Yasir! Indeed, your appointed place is Paradise').

questionEn: Who holds the honor of being the very first martyr (shahidah) in the history of Islam after being killed by Abu Jahl in Makkah for refusing to renounce her faith?
optionsEn: Umm Salamah (RA)
Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA), the mother of Ammar ibn Yasir
Fatimah bint al-Khattab (RA)
Asma' bint Umais (RA)
explanationEn: Sumayyah bint Khayyat (RA) refused to recant her faith in Allah despite severe torture in Makkah and was fatally struck with a spear by Abu Jahl, becoming the first martyr in Islam.
reference: Musannaf Ibn Abi Shaybah 37041; Al-Isti'ab by Ibn Abd al-Barr

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse was revealed in Makkah to comfort Ammar ibn Yasir (RA) after his persecutors forced him under unbearable torture to utter words against his will while his heart remained firm in faith?
optionsEn: 'So remember Me; I will remember you' (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:152)
'Allah does not charge a soul except with what He has given it' (Surah At-Talaq 65:7)
'Except for one who is forced while his heart is secure in faith' (Surah An-Nahl 16:106)
'And say: Truth has come and falsehood has vanished' (Surah Al-Isra 17:81)
explanationEn: When Ammar (RA) came weeping to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah after being coerced under torture, the Prophet ﷺ wiped his tears, asked how he found his heart, and upon hearing it was tranquil with faith, Surah An-Nahl 16:106 was revealed.

questionEn: Which companion—a blacksmith in Makkah tortured with red-hot coals on his back—came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was resting in the shade of the Kaaba and asked him to pray for relief, hearing the prophecy of Islam's future security?
optionsEn: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA)
Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman (RA)
Zayd ibn Harithah (RA)
Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA)
explanationEn: Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) recounted in Sahih al-Bukhari (3612) that he approached the Prophet ﷺ while he was leaning on his cloak in the shade of the Kaaba; the Prophet ﷺ reminded him of the patience of earlier believers and swore that Allah would complete this matter until a rider travels from Sana'a to Hadramawt fearing none but Allah.

questionEn: Who was the first companion after the Prophet ﷺ to recite the Qur'an aloud publicly before the leaders of Quraysh assembled near the Kaaba in Makkah, reciting the opening verses of Surah Ar-Rahman?
optionsEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA)
Ubayy ibn Ka'b (RA)
Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (RA)
Zayd ibn Thabit (RA)
explanationEn: When the companions noted that Quraysh had never heard the Qur'an recited aloud publicly in their gathering at the Kaaba, Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) volunteered, stood at the Maqam at forenoon, and recited 'Ar-Rahman, 'Allama al-Qur'an' (55:1-2), enduring their blows on his face.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: When young Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA)—once the most finely dressed youth in Makkah—embraced Islam secretly at Dar al-Arqam, how did his wealthy mother Khunas bint Malik react upon discovering his faith?
optionsEn: She immediately migrated with him to the court of the Negus in Abyssinia
She imprisoned him in his room and deprived him of her wealth and fine garments, which he willingly gave up for Islam
She sent him as a trade envoy to the Lakhmid court in Iraq
She donated her entire estate to repair the walls of Dar al-Nadwah
explanationEn: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) had been pampered with the finest clothes and perfumes of Makkah, yet when his mother imprisoned him and cut off all his luxury to force him away from Islam, he remained steadfast and later wore patched garments in the path of Allah.

questionEn: In the fifth year of prophethood, to which land did the Prophet ﷺ advise his persecuted companions in Makkah to migrate first, describing its ruler as 'a king under whom no one is wronged'?
optionsEn: The Byzantine province of Egypt
The Sassanid Empire of Persia
Abyssinia (Al-Habashah)
The island of Socotra in the Arabian Sea
explanationEn: Seeing the severe persecution of his companions in Makkah while Abu Talib protected him, the Prophet ﷺ advised them to migrate across the Red Sea to Abyssinia (Al-Habashah), saying therein was a righteous king (Ashamah al-Najashi) under whom no one was oppressed.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: When Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) set out to leave Makkah due to persecution and met the chieftain Ibn al-Daghinnah at Bark al-Ghimad, what did Abu Bakr build at his home after returning under Ibn al-Daghinnah's protection?
optionsEn: A subterranean vault to store weapons for the Muslims
A watchtower overlooking the road to Tan'im
A market stall next to the gate of Banu Shaybah
A small prayer place (masjid) in the courtyard of his Makkan house where he prayed and recited the Qur'an tearfully
explanationEn: As recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (3905), Abu Bakr (RA) built a masjid in the courtyard of his house in Makkah where he prayed and recited the Qur'an with deep emotion; when Quraysh complained that their women and children were drawn to his recitation, Abu Bakr returned Ibn al-Daghinnah's protection and declared he was content with the protection of Allah alone.

questionEn: What event in Makkah immediately prompted Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA), 'the Lion of Allah,' to publicly declare his Islam?
optionsEn: Learning from a freedwoman upon returning from a hunt that Abu Jahl had harshly reviled and insulted his nephew Muhammad ﷺ near Mount Safa while the Prophet ﷺ remained silent
Hearing Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recite Surah Ar-Rahman at night
Witnessing the splitting of the moon from the peak of Mount Hira
Returning from a trade journey to Damascus with Abu Bakr
explanationEn: When Hamzah (RA) returned from hunting with his bow and learned that Abu Jahl had insulted and harmed the Prophet ﷺ near Safa, Hamzah marched straight into the Sanctuary, struck Abu Jahl with his bow, and proclaimed: 'I follow his religion and say what he says!'
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Mustadrak al-Hakim

questionEn: Which supplication of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ in Makkah was answered when Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) embraced Islam in the sixth year of prophethood?
optionsEn: 'O Allah, open the gates of Ta'if and Yemen before the gates of Yathrib'
'O Allah, strengthen Islam with the more beloved of these two men to You: Abu Jahl or Umar ibn al-Khattab'
'O Allah, cause the trade caravans of Quraysh to lose their way in the desert'
'O Allah, send down angels from heaven to guard the doors of Dar al-Arqam'
explanationEn: Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ prayed in Makkah: 'O Allah, strengthen Islam with the more beloved of these two men to You: by Abu Jahl or by Umar ibn al-Khattab,' and the more beloved of the two to Allah was Umar (RA).

questionEn: Passage from which Surah of the Qur'an—written on a parchment page at the Makkan home of his sister Fatimah bint al-Khattab and her husband Sa'id ibn Zayd (RA)—softened the heart of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) and led him to Dar al-Arqam?
optionsEn: The opening verses of Surah Al-Kahf (Surah 18)
The parables of Surah Al-Nur (Surah 24)
The opening verses of Surah Ta-Ha (Surah 20)
The closing verses of Surah Al-Baqarah (Surah 2)
explanationEn: At his sister Fatimah's house in Makkah, where Khabbab ibn al-Aratt (RA) had been teaching them, Umar (RA) washed himself and read the parchment containing the opening verses of Surah Ta-Ha (20:1-14), exclaiming, 'How noble and eloquent is this speech!' before going to the Prophet ﷺ at Dar al-Arqam to embrace Islam.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Sunan al-Daraqutni

questionEn: How did Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) describe the impact of Umar ibn al-Khattab's (RA) conversion on the Muslims living in Makkah?
optionsEn: 'All persecution in Makkah ended permanently on that very day'
'The Muslims no longer needed to migrate to Abyssinia or Madinah'
'Quraysh immediately handed over the keys of Dar al-Nadwah to the Muslims'
'We continued to be in strength and honor ever since Umar embraced Islam,' as the Muslims came out to pray openly at the Kaaba
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) said: 'We continued to be strong (ma zilna a'izzah) since Umar embraced Islam' (Sahih al-Bukhari 3684), as Umar's conversion enabled the Muslims to leave Dar al-Arqam in two ranks—led by Hamzah and Umar—and pray openly at the Sanctuary.

questionEn: In the seventh year of prophethood, in which narrow mountain ravine of Makkah were the Prophet ﷺ, Banu Hashim, and Banu al-Muttalib confined during the three-year social and economic boycott by Quraysh?
optionsEn: Shi'b Abi Talib (the Ravine of Abu Talib)
Shi'b 'Ali (outside the sacred boundaries)
Wadi Fatima (north of Tan'im)
Wadi Muhassir (between Mina and Muzdalifah)
explanationEn: Both the Muslim and non-Muslim members of Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib (except Abu Lahab) stood together in tribal solidarity to protect the Prophet ﷺ, enduring a three-year blockade in Shi'b Abi Talib in Makkah.

questionEn: What were the strict terms of the boycott document that Quraysh wrote and hung inside the Kaaba against Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib in Makkah?
optionsEn: That they must pay double the annual Rifadah tax during the pilgrimage season
That no one in Makkah would marry into them, give them in marriage, sell anything to them, or buy anything from them until they surrendered the Prophet ﷺ
That they were forbidden from speaking Arabic in the markets of 'Ukaz and Majannah
That their camels would be confiscated if seen near the wells of lower Makkah
explanationEn: The boycott pact sealed by Quraysh forbade all intermarriage, trade, food sales, and social dealings with Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib, reducing the families in Shi'b Abi Talib to eating tree leaves and dry skins.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Sahih al-Bukhari 1590

questionEn: What miraculous sign did Allah reveal to the Prophet ﷺ that brought about the end of the three-year boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib when Quraysh inspected the parchment inside the Kaaba?
optionsEn: That lightning had struck the roof of Dar al-Nadwah and burned the scroll to ashes
That rain had washed away the ink while leaving the signatures intact
That Allah had sent termites (al-ardah) that ate every unjust clause of the parchment, leaving only the words 'Bismika Allahumma' ('In Your Name, O Allah')
That the ink had turned from black to white overnight
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ informed his uncle Abu Talib that Allah had given termites mastery over the boycott sheet so that every word of injustice and cutting of family ties was eaten away, leaving only Allah's name ('Bismika Allahumma'); when Quraysh opened the Kaaba and saw this with their own eyes, five noble Makkans led by Hisham ibn Amr and Zuhayr ibn Abi Umayyah annulled the boycott.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Raheeq Al-Makhtum

questionEn: Why is the tenth year of prophethood in Makkah known in Islamic history as ''Am al-Huzn' (The Year of Sorrow)?
optionsEn: Because a severe plague struck the valleys surrounding Makkah
Because the wells of lower Makkah dried up for twelve consecutive months
Because the Abyssinian army launched a second expedition toward the Hijaz
Because both the Prophet's ﷺ protective uncle Abu Talib and his beloved wife Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA) passed away in Makkah within a short time of each other
explanationEn: Shortly after emerging from the three-year boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib, the Prophet ﷺ lost his uncle Abu Talib—who had shielded him externally before Quraysh—and his wife Khadijah (RA)—who had supported and comforted him at home—making it a year of profound grief.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya

questionEn: In which cemetery of upper Makkah (Al-Ma'lah) was the Mother of the Believers Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA) laid to rest in the tenth year of prophethood?
optionsEn: Jannat al-Mu'alla (Al-Hajun) in Makkah
Jannat al-Baqi' in Madinah
The cemetery of the Martyrs of Uhud
The valley of Badr al-Kubra
explanationEn: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid (RA), the first person to believe in the Prophet ﷺ, passed away in Makkah three years before the Hijrah at the age of sixty-five and was buried at Al-Hajun (Jannat al-Mu'alla) in Makkah.
reference: Tabaqat Ibn Sa'd; Al-Isabah by Ibn Hajar

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ returned from his difficult journey to Ta'if in the tenth year of prophethood, which Makkan nobleman granted him formal protection (jiwar) and escorted him with his armed sons to perform Tawaf at the Sanctuary?
optionsEn: Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt (of Banu Abd Shams)
Al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi (chief of Banu Nawfal)
Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah (chief of Banu Makhzum)
Umayyah ibn Khalaf (chief of Banu Jumah)
explanationEn: Al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi armed himself and his sons, stood at the corners of the Kaaba, and announced to Quraysh that he had taken Muhammad ﷺ under his protection (jiwar); the Prophet ﷺ never forgot this noble deed, saying at Badr: 'Had Al-Mut'im ibn 'Adi been alive and spoken to me regarding these captives, I would have released them for him.'

questionEn: According to Surah Al-Isra (17:1) and authentic hadith, from which sacred site did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ begin the miraculous Night Journey (Al-Isra') to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa?
optionsEn: From the valley of Quba on the outskirts of Madinah
From the Cave of Thawr south of Makkah
From Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah (specifically near Al-Hatim / Hijr)
From the summit of Mount Arafat on the ninth of Dhul-Hijjah
explanationEn: Surah Al-Isra (17:1) states: 'Exalted is He Who took His Servant by night from Al-Masjid al-Haram to Al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs.' Authentic hadiths in Bukhari (3887) specify he was lying at Al-Hatim (Al-Hijr) in Al-Masjid al-Haram.

questionEn: What was the name of the white celestial steed—larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, whose stride reached as far as its eye could see—that carried the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah to Jerusalem on the Night of Isra'?
optionsEn: Al-Qaswa'
Al-Sakb
Al-'Adba'
Al-Buraq
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim (162), the Prophet ﷺ stated: 'I was brought Al-Buraq, which is a white animal, long, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, which places its hoof at a distance equal to the range of its vision.'

questionEn: Which pillar of Islam was directly enjoined upon the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his Ummah during the Ascension (Al-Mi'raj) to the heavens before he returned to Makkah that same night?
optionsEn: The five obligatory daily prayers (Al-Salawat al-Khams)
The distribution of Zakat on agricultural produce
The prohibition of usury (Riba) in trade transactions
The annual fasting of the month of Ramadan
explanationEn: During Al-Mi'raj, fifty daily prayers were initially enjoined and then mercifully reduced by Allah to five daily prayers in action while retaining the reward of fifty.

questionEn: On the morning after the Night Journey in Makkah, when the disbelievers of Quraysh challenged the Prophet ﷺ to describe Al-Masjid al-Aqsa in detail because they knew he had never visited Jerusalem before, how did Allah assist him?
optionsEn: He postponed answering for three days until a caravan arrived from Gaza
Allah unveiled and raised Bayt al-Maqdis before his eyes while he stood in the Hijr of Makkah so that he described every detail while looking directly at it
He asked the merchants of Banu Umayyah to draw a map on the sand
He read the architectural plans from a scroll kept by Waraqah ibn Nawfal
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (3886) and Sahih Muslim (170): 'When Quraysh disbelieved me, I stood up in Al-Hijr and Allah displayed Bayt al-Maqdis before me, so I began informing them about its signs while I was looking at it.'

questionEn: How did Abu Bakr (RA) earn the enduring title 'Al-Siddiq' ('The Truthful / The Ever-Affirming') in Makkah on the morning after Al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj?
optionsEn: By memorizing the entire Makkan revelation on parchment sheets
By donating forty camels laden with wheat during the famine of Makkah

When told that his companion claimed to have traveled to Jerusalem and back in a single night, he immediately declared: 'If he said that, then he has spoken the truth! Indeed, I believe him regarding news from heaven in a morning or evening'
By winning a public poetry contest defending Banu Hashim at Suq 'Ukaz
explanationEn: When Abu Jahl and the polytheists rushed to Abu Bakr hoping to shake his faith with news of the Night Journey, Abu Bakr unhesitatingly affirmed the Prophet's ﷺ truthfulness, saying he already believed him regarding heavenly revelation that comes in an instant—earning the title Al-Siddiq.

questionEn: During the pilgrimage season in the eleventh year of prophethood, at which site in Mina did the Prophet ﷺ meet six men from the tribe of Khazraj of Yathrib (Madinah), planting the first seed of the Ansar's Islam?
optionsEn: At the marketplace of Dhu al-Majaz east of Arafat
Inside the Cave of Hira on Jabal al-Nur
At the well of Maymun in upper Makkah
Near Al-'Aqabah in Mina
explanationEn: While calling the visiting Arab tribes during the Hajj season, the Prophet ﷺ met six men of Khazraj (including As'ad ibn Zurarah, RA) at Al-'Aqabah in Mina; they recognized him as the Prophet whom the Jewish scholars of Yathrib had foretold, embraced Islam, and returned the following year with twelve men.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Raheeq Al-Makhtum

questionEn: After the First Pledge of Aqabah (12th year of prophethood) with twelve men from Madinah, which Makkan companion did the Prophet ﷺ send with them as the first ambassador and teacher of Islam ('Al-Muqri'')?
optionsEn: Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA)
Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As (RA)
Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
Tufayl ibn Amr al-Dawsi (RA)
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ dispatched Mus'ab ibn Umayr (RA) from Makkah to Yathrib to recite the Qur'an to them, teach them Islam, and lead them in prayer; through his wisdom and gentle preaching, Islam entered nearly every household of the Ansar before the next Hajj.

questionEn: How many men and women from Madinah met the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ by night in the valley at Al-'Aqabah during the Days of Tashreeq in the thirteenth year of prophethood to swear the Second Pledge of Aqabah?
optionsEn: Three hundred and thirteen men and four women
Seventy-three men and two women (Nusaybah bint Ka'b and Asma' bint Amr, RA)
Twelve men and one woman
Forty men and ten women
explanationEn: In the middle of the Days of Tashreeq, seventy-three men and two women (Umm 'Umarah Nusaybah bint Ka'b and Umm Mani' Asma' bint Amr, RA) secretly left their camp at night to meet the Prophet ﷺ at Al-'Aqabah and pledge to protect him as they protected their own families.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Musnad Ahmad 15798

questionEn: Which uncle of the Prophet ﷺ—who had not yet publicly declared Islam—accompanied him to the secret night meeting of the Second Pledge of Aqabah in Mina to verify that the Ansar were serious about protecting his nephew?
optionsEn: Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib
Al-Zubayr ibn Abd al-Muttalib
Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib
Abu Lahab ibn Abd al-Muttalib
explanationEn: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib accompanied his nephew to the night meeting at Al-'Aqabah and spoke first, reminding the Khazraj and Aws that Muhammad ﷺ was still protected in honor among his clan in Makkah, so they should pledge only if they were truly resolved to defend him against all enemies.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: When the companions began migrating from Makkah to Madinah, how did Suhayb al-Rumi (RA) secure his departure when Quraysh blocked his path and refused to let him leave with the wealth he had earned in Makkah?
optionsEn: He hired Bedouin horsemen from Banu Kinanah to escort his caravan by force
He waited in Makkah until the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah six years later
He sailed from Shu'aybah to Abyssinia and traveled overland through Egypt
He directed them to the hiding place of all his gold and savings in Makkah in exchange for letting him migrate freely with his faith, earning the praise of Surah Al-Baqarah 2:207
explanationEn: Suhayb al-Rumi (RA) handed over the location of all his Makkan wealth to leave with his faith; when he reached Madinah, the Prophet ﷺ greeted him saying, 'The transaction has profited, O Abu Yahya!' in connection with Surah Al-Baqarah (2:207): 'And of the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah.'
reference: Mustadrak al-Hakim 5602; Tafsir Ibn Kathir on Qur'an 2:207

questionEn: When Umm Salamah (RA) and her husband Abu Salamah (RA) set out to migrate from Makkah to Madinah, what severe hardship did the clans of Banu al-Mughirah (her clan) and Banu Abd al-Asad (her husband's clan) inflict on them in Makkah?
optionsEn: Her clan prevented her from leaving with her husband, and her husband's clan took away her young son Salamah until she wept at Al-Abtah for nearly a year before being reunited
They burned their date palms and livestock in the valley of Marr al-Zahran
They forced them to pay a hundred camels in ransom before crossing Tan'im
They confiscated their house near Marwah and exiled them both to Yemen
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) endured heart-wrenching separation in Makkah for nearly a year: her husband migrated alone to Madinah, her husband's clan took her young child Salamah, and her own clan detained her in Makkah until a compassionate relative shamed them into returning her son and letting her travel to Madinah, escorted nobly by Uthman ibn Talhah.

questionEn: Which Qur'anic verse explicitly captures the three options debated by the chiefs of Quraysh at Dar al-Nadwah in Makkah when plotting against the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ on the eve of the Hijrah?
optionsEn: 'Indeed, He Who ordained the Qur'an upon you will surely return you to a place of return' (Surah Al-Qasas 28:85)
'And remember when those who disbelieved plotted against you to imprison you, or kill you, or expel you; and they plan, and Allah plans, and Allah is the Best of planners' (Surah Al-Anfal 8:30)
'And say: My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance and exit a sound exit' (Surah Al-Isra 17:80)
'If you do not aid him, Allah has already aided him when those who disbelieved drove him out' (Surah At-Tawbah 9:40)
explanationEn: At their assembly in Dar al-Nadwah in Makkah, the chiefs of Quraysh proposed three exact schemes—imprisoning him in chains, expelling him from Makkah, or assassinating him—which Allah revealed verbatim in Surah Al-Anfal (8:30).

questionEn: Why did Abu Jahl propose at Dar al-Nadwah that one strong young man be selected from every clan of Quraysh to strike the Prophet ﷺ simultaneously with their swords in Makkah?
optionsEn: Because Dar al-Nadwah's ancient constitution required twelve witnesses for any execution
To intimidate the visiting pilgrims from Yathrib before they left Mina
So that responsibility for his blood would be dispersed among all the clans, preventing Banu Abd Manaf from waging war against every clan at once and forcing them to accept blood money
Because none of the individual clans possessed swords sharp enough for the task
explanationEn: Abu Jahl's sinister plan at Dar al-Nadwah was designed to bypass tribal blood vengeance in Makkah by dividing the fatal blow across every clan of Quraysh simultaneously.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: Why did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ instruct Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) to sleep in his bed wrapped in his green Hadrami cloak on the night of the Hijrah and remain in Makkah for three days afterward?
optionsEn: To guard the manuscripts of the Qur'an stored inside Dar al-Arqam
To sell the properties of Banu Hashim in the market of lower Makkah
To negotiate a six-month trade truce with Abu Sufyan at Dar al-Nadwah
Both to foil the assassins watching through the doorway and to return all the financial trusts and valuables (amanat) that the people of Makkah had deposited with the Prophet ﷺ
explanationEn: Even while plotting against the Prophet ﷺ, the people of Makkah knew none was more trustworthy than him ('Al-Amin') and kept their valuables deposited with him; Ali (RA) risked his life in the Prophet's bed and stayed three days in Makkah until every single trust was returned to its owner.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 1; Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya

questionEn: As the Prophet ﷺ walked out of his surrounded house in Makkah past the waiting assassins on the night of the Hijrah, he cast a handful of dust toward their heads while reciting verses from which Surah?
optionsEn: The opening nine verses of Surah Ya-Sin (36:1-9), ending with 'So We have covered them, and they do not see'
The opening five verses of Surah Al-Falaq (113:1-5)
The final verses of Surah Al-Hashr (59:22-24)
The Throne Verse (Ayat al-Kursi) of Surah Al-Baqarah (2:255)
explanationEn: Allah took away the sight of the assassins waiting outside the Prophet's ﷺ door in Makkah as he stepped out scattering dust upon their heads and reciting Surah Ya-Sin (36:1-9): 'And We have placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier and covered them, so they do not see.'

questionEn: When the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ came to the house of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (RA) at unusual midday heat in Makkah wearing a head-cover to inform him that Allah had granted permission to migrate, how did Abu Bakr react when told he would accompany him?
optionsEn: Abu Bakr advised taking the northern coastal route immediately without hiding
Abu Bakr wept out of pure joy, causing Aisha (RA) to say she had never realized before that day that someone could weep from happiness
Abu Bakr sent his son Abd al-Rahman ahead to alert the elders of Quraysh
Abu Bakr asked for three days' delay to gather his trade debtors from Ta'if
explanationEn: Aisha (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (3905) that when Abu Bakr asked, 'Companionship, O Messenger of Allah?' and the Prophet ﷺ replied, 'Companionship,' Abu Bakr wept for joy—and Aisha remarked, 'By Allah, I did not know before that day that anyone could weep from joy until I saw Abu Bakr weeping that day.'

questionEn: Instead of heading directly north toward Madinah on the night they left Makkah, in which direction did the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) walk to take shelter in the Cave of Thawr for three nights?
optionsEn: Due east toward the mountain passes of Arafat and Ta'if
Directly north along the main coastal caravan highway past Usfan
South of Makkah (in the opposite direction from Madinah) to baffle the trackers of Quraysh
Due west toward the Red Sea port of Shu'aybah
explanationEn: Demonstrating exemplary strategic planning alongside reliance upon Allah, the Prophet ﷺ left Makkah heading south—opposite the northern road to Madinah—and stayed three nights in the Cave of Thawr until the search parties subsided.

questionEn: Who were the four individuals in Makkah who secretly supported the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA) during their three days in the Cave of Thawr with intelligence, food, milk, and expert guiding?
optionsEn: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Abu Talib, Mus'ab ibn Umayr, and Zayd ibn Harithah
Umar ibn al-Khattab, Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib, Bilal ibn Rabah, and Suhayb al-Rumi
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Talhah ibn Ubaydullah, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf
Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr (intelligence), Asma' bint Abi Bakr (food/nitaq), Amir ibn Fuhayrah (milk and covering tracks with sheep), and Abdullah ibn Urayqit (expert desert guide)
explanationEn: As detailed in Sahih al-Bukhari (3905), Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr brought Makkan intelligence by night, Asma' bint Abi Bakr ('Dhat al-Nitaqayn') prepared their provisions, Amir ibn Fuhayrah grazed his flock over their footprints and provided milk, and the skilled guide Abdullah ibn Urayqit led them along the coastal route.

questionEn: When the polytheist trackers of Quraysh stood right at the mouth of the Cave of Thawr above the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr (RA), what did the Prophet ﷺ say to reassure Abu Bakr, as immortalized in Surah At-Tawbah (9:40)?
optionsEn: 'What do you think of two when Allah is their Third? Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us'
'Draw your sword, O Abu Bakr, for we shall fight them at the cave entrance'
'Climb down the western slope while I distract their horses'
'Call out to the tribe of Khuza'ah in the valley below to rescue us'
explanationEn: When Abu Bakr (RA) whispered, 'O Messenger of Allah, if one of them were to look down at his feet, he would see us!' the Prophet ﷺ answered: 'O Abu Bakr, what do you think of two when Allah is their Third? Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us (La tahzan inna Allaha ma'ana).'

questionEn: As the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ looked back at Makkah upon departing for the Hijrah, with what moving words did he express his deep love for the Sacred City?
optionsEn: 'Only the merchants of Syria and Yemen shall visit your markets hereafter'
'By Allah, indeed you are the best of Allah's earth and the most beloved of Allah's earth to Allah; had I not been driven out from you, I would never have left you'
'I leave your valleys behind forever and shall never return to your mountains'
'May your wells run dry until your leaders come begging at the gates of Yathrib'
explanationEn: Standing at Al-Hazwarah in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ addressed the Sacred City: 'By Allah, indeed you are the best of Allah's earth and the most beloved of Allah's earth to Allah, and had I not been driven out from you, I would never have left you.'

questionEn: In the month of Dhul-Qa'dah 6 AH, what inspired the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ to set out toward Makkah with approximately 1,400 unarmed companions in the state of Ihram?
optionsEn: An invitation letter sent by the elders of Dar al-Nadwah offering a military alliance
A request from the tribe of Thaqif to arbitrate a land dispute in lower Makkah
A true dream shown to him by Allah that he and his companions would enter Al-Masjid al-Haram in security with their heads shaved or hair shortened
News that the Abyssinian viceroy had launched a coastal raid near Shu'aybah
explanationEn: As confirmed in Surah Al-Fath (48:27), Allah showed His Messenger ﷺ a true vision in sleep that the Muslims would enter Al-Masjid al-Haram safely, shaving their heads and shortening their hair without fear, so he set out in Dhul-Qa'dah 6 AH purely to perform Umrah.

questionEn: When the Prophet's ﷺ she-camel Al-Qaswa' knelt down at the pass leading to Al-Hudaybiyyah and the companions said 'Al-Qaswa' has become stubborn!', how did the Prophet ﷺ explain her stopping?
optionsEn: 'She is exhausted from the desert heat and needs water from the wells of Usfan'
'She has sensed the cavalry of Khalid ibn al-Walid hiding behind the hill'
'She refuses to walk on rocky ground during the month of Dhul-Qa'dah'
'Al-Qaswa' has not become stubborn, nor is that her nature, but she has been held back by the One Who held back the Elephant from Makkah!'
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (2731), the Prophet ﷺ defended his camel and revealed the divine wisdom behind the halt at Hudaybiyyah: 'Al-Qaswa' has not become stubborn, nor is that her character; rather, she was restrained by the One Who restrained the Elephant!'

questionEn: Immediately after Al-Qaswa' knelt at the edge of Hudaybiyyah, what solemn oath did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ swear regarding the sanctity of Makkah?
optionsEn: 'By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, they (Quraysh) will not ask me today for any plan by which they honor the sacred ordinances of Allah except that I will grant it to them!'
'No envoy from Quraysh will be permitted to speak in our camp'
'We shall storm the passes of Makkah before sunset even if we have only travelers' swords'
'We shall remain camped at Hudaybiyyah for an entire year until the gates open'
explanationEn: Honoring the inviolable sanctity of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ swore at Hudaybiyyah that whatever proposal Quraysh put forward that magnified the sacred things of Allah (hurumat Allah), he would accept it.

questionEn: When the 1,400 companions camped at Hudaybiyyah found its single well almost completely dry, what miracle occurred through the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ?
optionsEn: An underground aqueduct from Ta'if burst open beside the camp
He rinsed his mouth and placed an arrow from his quiver into the well, causing fresh water to gush forth until the entire army and their mounts drank their fill
A sudden summer cloudburst filled the valley of Marr al-Zahran for three days
Caravans from Khuza'ah brought ten thousand skins of water from the Red Sea coast
explanationEn: Jabir ibn Abdullah (RA) and Al-Bara' (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (2731, 3576) that the well at Hudaybiyyah was dry until the Prophet ﷺ sat by its edge, rinsed his mouth into it, and had an arrow placed in its bottom, whereupon water gushed out abundantly for all 1,400 men.

questionEn: When Urwah ibn Mas'ud al-Thaqafi visited the Muslim camp at Hudaybiyyah as an envoy for Quraysh, what testimony did he give upon returning to the leaders of Makkah?
optionsEn: That the Muslims were suffering from famine and would retreat within two days
That the Muslims had brought siege engines hidden beneath their tents
That he had visited the courts of Caesar, Chosroes, and the Negus, and had never seen any king honored and loved by his companions as Muhammad ﷺ was by his companions
That the Ansar had refused to support the Muhajirun outside Madinah
explanationEn: Urwah ibn Mas'ud told Quraysh in Makkah: 'O people! By Allah, I have been sent as an envoy to kings—to Caesar, Chosroes, and the Negus—and by Allah, I have never seen a king whose companions venerate him as the companions of Muhammad ﷺ venerate Muhammad!'

questionEn: Why did Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) recommend sending Uthman ibn Affan (RA) instead of himself as the Prophet's ﷺ peace envoy into Makkah from Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: Because Uthman was the only companion who knew the secret mountain path into lower Makkah
Because Umar was suffering from a leg injury sustained during the march from Dhul-Hulayfah
Because the treaty laws of Qusayy required an envoy who owned a house near Marwah
Because Quraysh knew Umar's fierce opposition to their idolatry and none of Banu 'Adi could shield him in Makkah, whereas Uthman was held in high esteem by his clan of Banu Umayyah
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ called Umar (RA) to go as envoy to Makkah, Umar explained that Quraysh knew his hostility toward their polytheism and there was no one of Banu 'Adi ibn Ka'b in Makkah to protect him, adding: 'I will point you to a man more honored there than I—Uthman ibn Affan.'
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 2; Musnad Ahmad

questionEn: While Uthman ibn Affan (RA) was inside Makkah delivering the Prophet's ﷺ message, how did he reply when his relative Aban ibn Sa'id offered him permission to perform Tawaf around the Kaaba alone?
optionsEn: 'I would never do so until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performs Tawaf around it!'
'Only the elders of Banu Hashim are permitted to circle the House in Dhul-Qa'dah'
'I will perform three circuits now and four when the army enters tomorrow'
'I cannot perform Tawaf without first sacrificing my camel at Mina'
explanationEn: Out of profound love and loyalty to the Prophet ﷺ, Uthman (RA) declined the personal privilege offered by Quraysh in Makkah, declaring: 'Ma kuntu li-af'ala hatta yatufa bihi Rasulullahi ﷺ' ('I would never do so until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ performs Tawaf around it').
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 2; Al-Bidaya wa'l-Nihaya

questionEn: What event at Hudaybiyyah directly triggered 'Bay'at al-Ridwan' (The Pledge of Good Pleasure) beneath the tree, praised by Allah in Surah Al-Fath (48:18)?
optionsEn: Banu Bakr raided a caravan of Banu Khuza'ah near the well of Hudaybiyyah
A rumor reached the Muslim camp that Uthman ibn Affan (RA) had been treacherously murdered in Makkah while serving as an unarmed envoy
Khalid ibn al-Walid's cavalry attacked the rear guard of the Muslim camp at night
Suhail ibn Amr tore up the first draft of the peace treaty
explanationEn: When news reached Hudaybiyyah that Uthman (RA) had been killed in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ sat beneath a Samurah (acacia) tree and took the pledge from his 1,400 companions not to flee (and to stand unto death), regarding which Allah revealed: 'Certainly was Allah pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree' (48:18).

questionEn: How did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ include the absent Uthman ibn Affan (RA)—who was detained inside Makkah—in the honor of Bay'at al-Ridwan under the tree at Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: He repeated the pledge a second time after Uthman returned from Makkah
He sent a rider to shout the words of the pledge from the hilltop of Tan'im
He held up his own right hand, declared 'This is the hand of Uthman,' and struck it upon his left hand, saying 'This pledge is for Uthman'
He asked Talhah ibn Ubaydullah to sign Uthman's name on a parchment scroll
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (3698), Ibn Umar (RA) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ held out his own hand and said, 'This is the hand of Uthman,' then struck it with his other hand and said, 'This is for Uthman'—making the Prophet's ﷺ own hand better for Uthman than his own!

questionEn: When Quraysh sent Suhail ibn Amr from Makkah to negotiate the treaty at Hudaybiyyah, what optimistic remark (fa'l hasan) did the Prophet ﷺ make upon hearing his name?
optionsEn: 'Victory will come before the rising of the Canopus star (Suhail)!'
'The eloquence of Quraysh has yielded to peace!'
'We shall enter Makkah through the southern plain (al-Sahl)!'
'Your matter has been made easy for you!' (playing on the root of 'Suhail,' meaning ease)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ saw Suhail ibn Amr approaching the camp at Hudaybiyyah, he drew a good omen from his name (which comes from sahl/suhulah, meaning ease) and said: 'Laqad suhhila lakum min amrikum' ('Your affair has been made easy for you').

questionEn: During the drafting of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, when the scribe Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA) wrote 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' and 'Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah,' what did Suhail ibn Amr insist be written instead?
optionsEn: 'Bismika Allahumma' and 'Muhammad ibn Abdullah'
'Bi-Ahd Qusayy' and 'Abu al-Qasim'
'Bismillah al-Malik' and 'Sayyid Yathrib'
'Bi-'izzat al-Lat' and 'Al-Hashimi al-Makki'
explanationEn: Suhail ibn Amr objected that if he acknowledged Muhammad ﷺ as the Messenger of Allah, he would not have barred him from the House or fought him; the Prophet ﷺ replied, 'By Allah, I am indeed the Messenger of Allah even if you disbelieve me,' and personally erased the title to write 'Muhammad ibn Abdullah' for the sake of peace.

questionEn: Under the terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH), how long was the agreed truce between the Muslims and Quraysh, and which two tribes immediately joined the respective alliances around Makkah?
optionsEn: A five-year truce; Banu Sulaym allied with the Prophet ﷺ and Banu Hawazin allied with Quraysh
A ten-year truce; Banu Khuza'ah entered into the covenant of the Prophet ﷺ, while Banu Bakr entered into the covenant of Quraysh
A twenty-year truce; Banu Asad allied with the Prophet ﷺ and Banu Ghatafan allied with Quraysh
A three-year truce; Banu Thaqif allied with the Prophet ﷺ and Banu Kinanah allied with Quraysh
explanationEn: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah stipulated cessation of war for ten years so people would be safe, and allowed any tribe to join either alliance: Banu Khuza'ah promptly joined the covenant of the Prophet ﷺ, while their historic rivals Banu Bakr joined the covenant of Quraysh.

questionEn: Whose sudden arrival in chains from lower Makkah right as the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was being concluded tested the patience of the companions when his father insisted he be returned to Makkah?
optionsEn: Salamah ibn Hisham (RA)
Abu Basir Utbah ibn Asid (RA)
Abu Jandal ibn Suhail ibn Amr (RA)
Al-Walid ibn al-Walid (RA)
explanationEn: Just as the treaty was agreed upon, Suhail ibn Amr's own son, Abu Jandal (RA), came staggering in his fetters from lower Makkah; when Suhail insisted on returning him under the treaty terms, the Prophet ﷺ comforted Abu Jandal: 'Be patient and seek reward, for Allah will grant for you and the weak with you a way out and relief.'

questionEn: After the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was signed and the grieving companions hesitated when told to slaughter their sacrificial animals and shave their heads outside Makkah, whose wise counsel did the Prophet ﷺ follow?
optionsEn: Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA), who suggested waiting until the army returned to Dhul-Hulayfah
Sa'd ibn Ubadah (RA), who advised holding a general consultation under the acacia tree
Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA), who suggested sending the sacrificial camels into Makkah with Suhail
His wife Umm Salamah (RA), who advised him to go out without speaking a word, slaughter his own camel, and shave his head—whereupon all the companions immediately followed his example
explanationEn: Umm Salamah (RA) demonstrated remarkable wisdom at Hudaybiyyah: she told the Prophet ﷺ that the companions were only stunned by grief at not entering Makkah that day, and advised him to go out silently, sacrifice his camel, and call his barber—and the moment they saw him do so, they raced to follow suit.

questionEn: Which Surah was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ on the return journey from Hudaybiyyah, declaring that apparent diplomatic concession to be a 'Clear Conquest' (Fathan Mubinan)?
optionsEn: Surah Al-Fath (Surah 48)
Surah Al-Nasr (Surah 110)
Surah Al-Anfal (Surah 8)
Surah Muhammad (Surah 47)
explanationEn: On the return from Hudaybiyyah, Allah revealed Surah Al-Fath (48:1): 'Indeed, We have granted you a clear conquest (Inna fatahna laka fathan mubinan),' and the Prophet ﷺ said a Surah had been revealed to him more beloved to him than all the world.

questionEn: In Dhul-Qa'dah 7 AH—one year after Hudaybiyyah—the Prophet ﷺ and his companions entered Makkah peacefully for three days to perform which pilgrimage?
optionsEn: Umrah al-Ji'ranah (The Umrah after Hunayn)
Umrah al-Qada' (The Fulfilled / Compensatory Umrah)
Hajj al-Akbar (The Greater Pilgrimage of 9 AH)
Hajjat al-Wada' (The Farewell Pilgrimage)
explanationEn: Fulfilling the exact terms of the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah and the true dream of Surah Al-Fath (48:27), the Prophet ﷺ led the companions of Hudaybiyyah into Makkah in Dhul-Qa'dah 7 AH for Umrah al-Qada' (also called Umrah al-Qadiyyah) and stayed three days.

questionEn: During Umrah al-Qada' (7 AH), why did the Prophet ﷺ command his companions in Makkah to uncover their right shoulders (Idtiba') and jog briskly in the first three circuits of Tawaf (Ramal)?
optionsEn: To finish their Tawaf before the midday heat reached the valley floor
To make space for the women and children arriving from Madinah
To display their physical strength and vigor to the polytheists of Quraysh watching from Mount Qu'ayqi'an, who had rumored that the fevers of Yathrib had weakened the Muslims
Because the ground on the northern side of the Sanctuary was flooded
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (1602, 4256) that when the Prophet ﷺ and his companions arrived in Makkah for Umrah al-Qada', the polytheists sitting by the Hijr/Qu'ayqi'an claimed the fevers of Yathrib had enfeebled them, so the Prophet ﷺ ordered them to perform Ramal in the first three rounds and walk between the two Yemeni corners.

questionEn: What violent act in Sha'ban 8 AH directly violated and nullified the ten-year Treaty of Hudaybiyyah?
optionsEn: The elders of Dar al-Nadwah closed the road between Tan'im and Hudaybiyyah
Abu Sufyan confiscated the properties of the Muhajirun in upper Makkah
A Makkan trade caravan refused to pay customs duties when passing near Badr
Banu Bakr—secretly supplied with weapons and night fighters by leaders of Quraysh—attacked the Prophet's ﷺ allies, Banu Khuza'ah, at Al-Watir and killed them even inside the Haram of Makkah
explanationEn: Banu Bakr took advantage of the night to ambush Banu Khuza'ah at the water of Al-Watir, and several prominent men of Quraysh (including Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl and Safwan ibn Umayyah) disguised themselves to supply weapons and fight alongside Banu Bakr, pursuing Khuza'ah even into the Sacred Sanctuary of Makkah.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 2; Al-Raheeq Al-Makhtum

questionEn: Which poet and representative of Banu Khuza'ah rode swiftly from Makkah to Madinah to stand before the Prophet ﷺ in the mosque and recite verses pleading for aid after Quraysh and Banu Bakr massacred his people at Al-Watir?
optionsEn: Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i
Hassan ibn Thabit al-Ansari
Labid ibn Rabi'ah al-'Amiri
Ka'b ibn Zuhayr al-Muzani
explanationEn: Amr ibn Salim al-Khuza'i stood before the Prophet ﷺ in Madinah and recited his moving poem reminding him of their alliance and how Quraysh had attacked them at Al-Watir while they bowed and prostrated in prayer; the Prophet ﷺ replied: 'You have been helped, O Amr ibn Salim!' (Nusirta ya Amr ibn Salim).

questionEn: As the Prophet ﷺ prepared in strict secrecy to march on Makkah in Ramadan 8 AH, why did he forgive the Badr veteran Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah (RA) after intercepting a letter Hatib had sent warning Quraysh?
optionsEn: Because Hatib paid a hundred camels in expiation to the public treasury

Because Hatib explained he had no family clan in Makkah to protect his vulnerable relatives there and did not act out of hypocrisy, and the Prophet ﷺ reminded Umar that Allah had already pardoned the participants of Badr
Because the letter was written in a cipher that Quraysh could not read
Because Abu Sufyan had already learned of the march from Syrian merchants
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (3007), Ali, Zubayr, and Miqdad (RA) intercepted the courier at Rawdat Khakh; Hatib explained he had no blood ties in Quraysh to protect his family in Makkah, and the Prophet ﷺ accepted his truthfulness and reminded Umar of Allah's forgiveness for the people of Badr (while Surah Al-Mumtahanah 60:1 was revealed).

questionEn: With how many companions did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ march in the month of Ramadan 8 AH for the Conquest of Makkah (Fath Makkah)?
optionsEn: Three thousand companions
Thirty thousand companions
Ten thousand companions
One thousand four hundred companions
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (4276) that the Prophet ﷺ left Madinah in Ramadan with ten thousand Muslims for the Conquest of Makkah, eight and a half years after his Hijrah.

questionEn: When the Muslim army of 10,000 camped at Marr al-Zahran (Wadi Fatima) just outside Makkah at night in Ramadan 8 AH, what strategic order did the Prophet ﷺ give to ensure Makkah surrendered peacefully without bloodshed?
optionsEn: He ordered the wells of lower Makkah to be diverted toward the Red Sea
He ordered the army to beat war drums continuously from sunset to dawn
He ordered catapults to be erected on the heights of Mount Hira
He ordered every warrior to kindle an individual campfire, illuminating the entire valley with ten thousand fires to overawe the scouts of Quraysh
explanationEn: At Marr al-Zahran, the Prophet ﷺ commanded the 10,000 soldiers to light separate campfires across the valley; when Abu Sufyan and Hakim ibn Hizam came out to scout and saw the vast sea of fires, they realized resistance was impossible.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 2; Dalail al-Nubuwwah

questionEn: Who rode out at night on the Prophet's ﷺ white mule from the camp at Marr al-Zahran hoping to warn Quraysh to seek peace before the army entered Makkah by force, and brought Abu Sufyan ibn Harb under protection to the Prophet ﷺ?
optionsEn: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA)
Abu Dharr al-Ghifari (RA)
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (RA)
Khalid ibn al-Walid (RA)
explanationEn: Al-Abbas ibn Abd al-Muttalib (RA), anxious lest Quraysh be destroyed if Makkah was entered by force, rode the Prophet's ﷺ white mule out of Marr al-Zahran, encountered Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and brought him behind him on the mule to the Prophet's ﷺ tent, where Abu Sufyan embraced Islam the next morning.
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 2; Sahih Muslim 1780

questionEn: What threefold proclamation of safety did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ grant upon Al-Abbas's recommendation to encourage the peaceful surrender of Makkah and honor Abu Sufyan?
optionsEn: 'Whoever pays fifty dinars at the gate of Dar al-Nadwah is granted safety'
'Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, whoever closes his own door behind him is safe, and whoever enters Al-Masjid al-Haram is safe'
'Only the clans of Banu Hashim, Banu Zuhrah, and Banu Taym are granted safety'
'Whoever flees to Ta'if is safe, whoever sails from Shu'aybah is safe, and whoever climbs Mount Thawr is safe'
explanationEn: As recorded in Sahih Muslim (1780), the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'Whoever enters the house of Abu Sufyan is safe, whoever lays down his arms is safe, and whoever locks his door is safe' (and in other narrations, whoever enters the Mosque is safe), ensuring a nearly bloodless entry into Makkah.

questionEn: To enter Makkah from all directions simultaneously on 20 Ramadan 8 AH while commanding his generals not to fight unless attacked, into how many main columns did the Prophet ﷺ divide the army, and who led them?
optionsEn: Two columns, led solely by Abu Bakr al-Siddiq and Umar ibn al-Khattab
Seven columns, led by seven chiefs of the tribe of Khuza'ah
Four columns, led by Abu Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, Al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, Khalid ibn al-Walid, and Qays ibn Sa'd (taking the banner from his father Sa'd ibn Ubadah)
Twelve columns, one for each lunar month of the Hijri calendar
explanationEn: The Prophet ﷺ divided the army at Dhu Tuwa into four entry columns—Al-Zubayr from upper Makkah (Kada'), Khalid from lower Makkah (Lait/Kuda), Abu Ubaydah with the infantry through the valley floor, and Sa'd ibn Ubadah/his son Qays—strictly instructing every commander not to shed blood unless fought first.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 4280; Sahih Muslim 1780; Sirat Ibn Hisham

questionEn: In what posture and reciting which Surah did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ enter Makkah as a victorious conqueror on the Day of Conquest (8 AH)?
optionsEn: Standing upright in golden armor atop a war chariot while trumpets were blown
Riding a horse at a gallop with an unsheathed sword raised above his head
Carried on a wooden palanquin surrounded by Persian silk banners
With his head bowed so low in humility and gratitude to Allah that his beard nearly touched the middle of his camel's saddle, while reciting Surah Al-Fath in a vibrating voice (tarji')
explanationEn: Unlike worldly conquerors who enter in arrogance, the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah bowing his head so low in humble submission to Allah that the tip of his beard nearly touched his saddle, while Abdullah ibn Mughaffal (RA) heard him reciting Surah Al-Fath (48) with a melodious vibrating tone (tarji').

questionEn: How many idols stood around and inside the Sanctuary of Makkah on the Day of Conquest when the Prophet ﷺ pointed at them with his staff and they fell down?
optionsEn: Three hundred and sixty idols
One thousand idols
Seventy-two idols
Ninety-nine idols
explanationEn: Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (2478, 4287) that the Prophet ﷺ entered Makkah on the Day of Conquest while there were 360 idols around the Kaaba, and he began prodding them with a stick in his hand until they fell over.

questionEn: Which two Qur'anic verses did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ recite aloud as he purified the Sanctuary of Makkah from idols on the Day of Conquest?
optionsEn: 'Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship' (109:1-2)
'Truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood is ever bound to vanish' (17:81) and 'Truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor repeat' (34:49)
'Permission to fight is given to those who are wronged' (22:39) and 'Fight in the way of Allah' (2:190)
'Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with the companions of the Elephant?' (105:1) and 'For the familiarity of Quraysh' (106:1)
explanationEn: Ibn Mas'ud (RA) reported in Sahih al-Bukhari (4287) that as the Prophet ﷺ struck down the idols around the Kaaba, he recited Surah Al-Isra (17:81) and Surah Saba' (34:49) proclaiming the triumph of Tawhid over falsehood.

questionEn: Standing at the door of the Kaaba on the Day of Conquest while the people of Quraysh waited below in anxious anticipation, what famous words of general amnesty did the Prophet ﷺ pronounce after asking 'What do you think I am about to do with you?'
optionsEn: 'Leave Makkah within three days and settle in the desert of Najd!'
'Serve in the garrison of Madinah for seven years to earn your pardon!'
'Go, for you are the freed ones!' ('Idhhabu fa-antum al-tulaqa'!')
'Pay half of your commercial property as war reparations to the Muhajirun!'
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ asked Quraysh what they thought he would do with them and they answered, 'Good—a noble brother and the son of a noble brother,' he granted them historic unconditional pardon: 'Idhhabu fa-antum al-tulaqa'' ('Go, for you are the freed ones!').
reference: Sirat Ibn Hisham, Vol. 2; Sunan al-Kubra by Al-Bayhaqi 18055

questionEn: Whom did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ command to climb atop the roof of the Kaaba on the Day of the Conquest of Makkah to call the Adhan for prayer?
optionsEn: Sa'd al-Qaraz (RA)
Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum (RA)
Abu Mahdhurah al-Jumahi (RA)
Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)
explanationEn: On the Day of the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ commanded Bilal ibn Rabah (RA)—who had once been tortured on the burning sands of Makkah for his faith—to climb atop the Kaaba and proclaim the Adhan of Tawhid over the entire valley.
reference: Sunan Abi Dawud 5135; Sirat Ibn Hisham

questionEn: Which young Makkan of Quraysh, possessing a remarkably beautiful voice, did the Prophet ﷺ personally teach the wording of the Adhan after Hunayn and appoint as the regular Mu'adhdhin of Al-Masjid al-Haram in Makkah?
optionsEn: Abu Mahdhurah (Aws ibn Mi'yar al-Jumahi, RA)
Suwayd ibn Samit (RA)
Bara' ibn 'Azib (RA)
Mu'aiqib ibn Abi Fatimah (RA)
explanationEn: When the Prophet ﷺ heard the powerful, resonant voice of young Abu Mahdhurah (RA), he wiped his forehead and chest with his blessed hand, prayed for him, taught him the Adhan, and appointed him as the Mu'adhdhin of Makkah—an office that remained in his family for generations.

questionEn: On the second day after the Conquest of Makkah, what eternal ruling did the Prophet ﷺ proclaim in his sermon regarding the sanctity of Makkah and the temporary permission he had been given to fight there?
optionsEn: That only the area within ten cubits of the Kaaba remained sacred after 8 AH

That Allah made Makkah sacred the day He created the heavens and earth; fighting in it was permitted for him for only one hour of a single day, and its sanctity has returned today just as it was yesterday until the Day of Resurrection
That Makkah's sanctity applied only during the four Sacred Months and was lifted during the rest of the year
That the Conquest permanently abrogated the sacred boundaries of Makkah so armies could battle there whenever needed
explanationEn: In Sahih al-Bukhari (1834) and Sahih Muslim (1353), Ibn Abbas and Abu Shurayh (RA) narrated that on the day after the Conquest, the Prophet ﷺ stood and declared that Allah—not human beings—made Makkah sacred from the creation of the heavens and earth, and that the brief one-hour permission granted to him on Conquest day did not make it lawful for anyone after him.

questionEn: In his sermon at the Kaaba after the Conquest of Makkah, what pre-Islamic social institution did the Prophet ﷺ explicitly abolish when he recited Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13): 'Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you'?
optionsEn: The provision of water and food to visiting pilgrims
The winter and summer trade caravans to Yemen and Syria
The arrogance of Jahiliyyah and boasting over tribal lineage and forefathers
The use of gold dinars and silver dirhams in Makkan commerce
explanationEn: Standing at the Kaaba in Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ declared: 'O people, Allah has removed from you the arrogance of Jahiliyyah and its boasting in forefathers. People are of two kinds: a righteous, God-fearing person who is honorable to Allah, and a wicked, miserable sinner who is insignificant to Allah. All people are the children of Adam, and Adam was created from dust.'

questionEn: Upon which hill in Makkah did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ sit after the Conquest to receive the pledge of allegiance (Bay'ah) from the men and women of Makkah?
optionsEn: Mount Arafat
Mount Hira (Jabal al-Nur)
Mount Thawr
Mount Safa
explanationEn: After the Conquest of Makkah, the Prophet ﷺ sat on Mount Safa to take the pledge of Islam from the people of Makkah—first the men, and then the women (including Hind bint Utbah, RA)—who pledged on the terms of Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60:12) without his hand ever touching the hand of a non-mahram woman.
reference: Sahih al-Bukhari 4891; Sahih Muslim 1866; Sirat Ibn Hisham

questionEn: When the Ansar of Madinah saw the Prophet ﷺ praying on Mount Safa after the Conquest of Makkah and feared among themselves that he might now remain permanently in his beloved hometown of Makkah, how did he reassure them?
optionsEn: 'Allah forbid! My life is your life, and my death is your death!'
'I will divide the year equally—six months in Makkah and six months in Madinah'
'Only the Muhajirun will remain in Makkah while the Ansar guard the northern frontier'
'I will stay in Makkah for five years and then retire to Ta'if'
explanationEn: In Sahih Muslim (1780), Abu Hurayrah (RA) narrated that when the Ansar whispered to one another on the Day of Conquest, 'Compassion for his city and love for his homeland have overtaken the man,' the Prophet ﷺ learned of it by revelation and told them: 'Never! I am the servant of Allah and His Messenger; I migrated to Allah and to you, so my life is your life and my death is your death!'

questionEn: According to the hadith of Ibn Abbas (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari, for how many days did the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ remain in Makkah during the expedition of the Conquest while continuing to shorten the four-rak'ah prayers to two?
optionsEn: Three days
Nineteen days
Forty days
Sixty days
explanationEn: Ibn Abbas (RA) narrated in Sahih al-Bukhari (1080): 'The Prophet ﷺ stayed in Makkah for nineteen days, praying two rak'ahs.'

questionEn: When the Prophet ﷺ departed from Makkah after the Conquest in 8 AH, which youthful companion from Banu Umayyah (only about twenty years old) did he appoint as the first Islamic governor (Amir) of Makkah?
